# Sprinting — provisional 12-class curriculum

**Updated:** 2026-09-13. **Finalized prescriptions: Classes 1–11.** Actual completion, athlete performance and training response are unknown. Next run: Class 12 only, including the full-sequence audit, after reviewing all saved work and available feedback.

Latest prescription: [coach-ready Class 11](classes/class_11.md); preceding [Class 10](classes/class_10.md), [Class 9](classes/class_09.md), [Class 8](classes/class_08.md), [Class 7](classes/class_07.md), [Class 6](classes/class_06.md), [Class 5](classes/class_05.md), [Class 4](classes/class_04.md), [Class 3](classes/class_03.md), [Class 2](classes/class_02.md) and [Class 1](classes/class_01.md) remain available. Supporting records: [progression/workload ledger](progression_ledger.md), [resume state](progress.json), [athlete feedback](athlete_feedback.md), [Class 11 audit](supporting/class_11_audit.md), [exercise/source register](supporting/sources_and_exercises.md) and [supplied specification](supporting/VORTEX_12_CLASS_CURRICULUM_SPEC.md).

## Scope and authority

The user's request is a category-wide **Sprinting** curriculum covering starts and gym support for maximum-running-velocity mechanics. It maps to `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. Straight-line start work is the main application; the full acceleration subcategory name stays intact. A later multidirectional start application is conditional and must serve acceleration rather than become a separate agility class.

The supplied document supplies detailed programming requirements because the user explicitly requested that. The subsequent user instruction prioritizes unique drills while permitting recurring strength lifts for progression. That preference supersedes the spec's default of retaining explosive anchors; preserve continuity through sprinting demands and recurring strength measures instead. Its Vertical Jumps default and example are not the requested target or a locked exercise list. The user's location instruction takes precedence over its example directory: save this plan and all supporting files under the existing root `workout_plan/sprinting/`. Finalize one new class per run, update state, then stop. No recurring automation or weekly calendar is requested.

## Exact seven-category framework

### Protracted running
- Endurance
- sustained pace
- pacing control

### Sprinting
- Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)
- Maximum velocity

### Jumps
- Vertical
- Horizontal
- Lateral
- Force absorption
- Elastic rebound

### Agility
- Deceleration
- Change of direction/reacceleration
- Reactive agility and anticipation

### Object control & receiving
- Tracking
- Catching/receiving
- Controlling/manipulating objects

### Upper-body force generation
- Pushing
- Pulling
- Straight-line projection (such as chest passes)

### Rotational explosiveness
- Upper-body emphasis (rotational throws, punches, and swings)
- Lower-body emphasis (rotational kicks)

Strength, stability, explosiveness and resilience are supporting qualities, not additional categories. Jumps used here support Sprinting and do not change the curriculum target. Body control/tumbling stays separate. Each class references the existing **Access & Prepare 1** and then uses exactly **6 Explosiveness / 2 Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) / 6 Strength (Primary)** entries in that order.

## Provisional map

Only Classes 1–11 have exercise tables. Later rows are intended jobs, not finalized workouts or automatic load increases. A hold, reduction or consolidation can replace a planned progression at any class number.

| Class | Intended emphasis and continuity | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Establish repeatable first-two-step projection; introduce upright ankle recoil/thigh timing and targeted strength with limited impact volume. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 2 | Low-origin push and opposite-thigh recovery: four half-kneeling starts with distinct supported exchange, seated/split jumps and small unilateral/upright contact tasks; strength doses held. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 3 | Leg-specific push and support transfer: three-point starts, rapid nonflight step-ups, opposite-leg bounds and complementary dynamic projection/recovery work; RDL/walkout volume reduced. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 4 | Upright support and nearby foot placement: distinct stationary exchanges, single-leg vertical reception, long-leg rebound and rapid nonflight support tasks; split-squat working volume reduced. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 5 | Unilateral upright support and thigh recovery: asymmetric running, shared jump reception, knee-drive pogo/skip release and rapid nonflight exchanges; Class 4 strength doses held. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 6 | Connect controlled falling-start initiation, staggered projection, supported ankle recoil, leg exchange and upright return; eight upright running contacts and six parked swings, strength held. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 7 | Settled forward-force initiation through seated starts/broad jumps, paused unilateral projection and brief wall tasks; dead-stop swings deliberately recur and strength doses hold. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 8 | Straight-line four-point release and consecutive push: small forward rebound, split receiver, paired wall exchanges, knee-fold recovery and contained forward ball release; strength held. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 9 | Upright coupled recovery, small vertical rebound and split ankle recoil; nonflight placement/limb timing and four shallow unilateral hip returns, with strength doses held. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 10 | Static bent-over starts, split projection, shared takeoff into individual reception and alternating upright recovery; paired wall switches recur openly, light standing band drives are conditional, strength held. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 11 | Single-cue start, isolated same-leg forward reception, split-base release and resettable upright exchange; full-cycle/arm families recur openly and soleus work falls to one set. | Finalized prescription; response unknown. |
| 12 | Review matched strength anchors and drill-specific observations, audit all twelve prescriptions/observations and define the next training need; do not infer top-speed improvement from gym scores. | Next; full sequence audit required at that run. |

**Post-Class-1 reassessment:** Class 2 remains an opening-push refinement opportunity, now using a distinct drill where defensible under the user's updated preference. Class 1 already combines starts, eight horizontal jumps, ankle/skip impacts and challenging lower-body strength, so no extra contacts, longer sprint or heavier lifting is pre-authorized. Classes 4–5 and 9 deliberately revisit upright support, but actual maximum-velocity running remains outside the available space throughout this map.

**Post-Class-2 reassessment:** No actual Class 1 or Class 2 completion is reported. Six distinct default drills were prescribed; start count fell from six to four and strength sets stayed unchanged. Fourteen jump/hop events plus supported switches and low-dribble contacts are recorded separately; no claim of equivalent or lower tissue stress follows from the lower landing count. Class 3 remains a leg-specific push refinement, not a scheduled intensity increase. Review actual same-leg ankle response, low-start control, wall/floor choice and group timing before choosing its drills. See [Class 2 identity/source notes](supporting/class_02_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-3 reassessment:** Actual work remains unknown. Class 3 keeps four starts and introduces isolated opposite-leg reception plus rapid nonflight leg-force/hip-recovery tasks. RDL is reduced to one working set and walkout to three cycles to limit overlap; the change is not a reported recovery finding. The main split-squat prescription stays comparable. Class 4 shifts attention toward upright support/placement rather than automatically restoring volume or increasing impact. Review actual bound control, band resistance direction, equipment fit and recovery first; see the [Class 3 audit](supporting/class_03_audit.md) and [source/identity notes](supporting/class_03_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-4 reassessment:** Class 4 contains no start running: all six explosive tasks serve upright posture/support in stationary space. Ten unilateral jump/hop landings and twelve A-run contacts remain separate exposure types. Split squat drops to one working round, while RDL/walkout reductions and ankle doses hold. Actual execution remains unknown. Class 5 should review task-specific control, calf/hip response, equipment substitutions and lifting reserve before selecting another relevant unilateral/thigh-recovery task; see [Class 4 audit](supporting/class_04_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_04_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-5 reassessment:** Class 5 holds twelve running contacts and all Class 4 strength doses while changing the recovery task to an asymmetric rhythm. Twelve jump/hop events now include four bilateral receivers; this is not an equal-load swap for Class 4's ten unilateral events. Pogo dose is limited to two/leg, and no height or resistance increase is prescribed. All actual outcomes remain unknown. Class 6 should consolidate the start and upright demands using reported execution/recovery if available; see [Class 5 audit](supporting/class_05_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_05_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-6 reassessment:** The midpoint now includes four controlled falling starts with the established two-step/3 m driving and 9 m stopping caps, twelve mixed jump/hop events, eight upright running contacts and six parked-single swings. Strength doses remain held. Related variants consolidate forward initiation and upright support; they do not prove six completed training exposures or maximum-velocity improvement. Review actual stopping, wall/floor choice, swing control and total recovery before Class 7; see [Class 6 audit](supporting/class_06_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_06_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-7 reassessment:** Seated starts consume the first metre of the lane: feet at 1 m, driving ends by 4 m, stop by 9 m; fit/stopping must be qualified. Eight bilateral jump receivers and brief nonflight wall tasks emphasize force initiation. E6 deliberately repeats the dead-stop swing for its direct job, with unchanged strength doses; five other default tasks have substantive distinctions. Actual outcomes remain unknown. Class 8 should examine whether a different facing/stance serves a real acceleration need; see [Class 7 audit](supporting/class_07_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_07_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-8 reassessment:** No directional need was established, so four-point starts stay straight ahead. Eight bilateral jump receivers now include two immediate rebounds and four split receivers; eight wall contacts and eight upright contacts are separate, with controlled set-downs explicitly counted. Four forward tosses require verified containment or their documented replacement. Strength doses hold. Class 9 returns the intended emphasis to upright support/recovery without assumed tolerance; see [Class 8 audit](supporting/class_08_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_08_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-9 reassessment:** Upright running returns to twelve contacts, alongside eight bilateral jump/pogo receivers and short nonflight placement, coordinated limb and hip-return tasks. Knee/hip-driven jumps, low split pogos and running contacts are separate exposures. Draft running, pogo and hinge doses were reduced; strength stays at Class 8 doses. Related running/hinge families and actual-technique overlap are disclosed. Class 10 should connect starts and upright support using reported execution/recovery if available; see [Class 9 audit](supporting/class_09_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_09_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-10 reassessment:** Four starts return, alongside eight mixed jump receivers (four unilateral), eight upright contacts, the deliberate Class 8 paired-wall recurrence and six light standing band drives. Fewer landing-foot impacts than Class 9 do not establish lower load: receiver support has changed. Five proposed variants have specific distinctions; earlier families and replacements remain disclosed. Strength doses hold and all actual outcomes remain unknown. Class 11 should consolidate repeatability using actual quality, reserve, recovery and the surrounding schedule; see [Class 10 audit](supporting/class_10_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_10_sources_and_exercises.md).

**Post-Class-11 reassessment:** Four cue opportunities preserve the start allocation; missed/early responses are logged without make-up attempts. Eight isolated unilateral flight events, four throws and brief cycle/arm drills replace the preceding contact allocation; they are not equal-load substitutions. Four proposed task variants include an external-onset constraint on a known start family; two earlier drill families recur openly. Soleus work falls from 2 × 8 to 1 × 8 while other strengthening doses hold. All actual outcomes remain unknown. Class 12 must review matched observations if supplied and complete the full-sequence audit; see [Class 11 audit](supporting/class_11_audit.md) and [source notes](supporting/class_11_sources_and_exercises.md).

## Drill uniqueness and strength continuity

Prioritize a new, purposefully distinct set of explosive drills for each class. Check the [drill history](supporting/drill_history.md) before selecting them. A change in load, reps, cue, name or side alone does not create a new drill. A different start condition, support demand or force-expression task must have its own relevant job and be feasible in the same gym. Do not promise 72 unique drills before reviewing feasibility and athlete response; the user said to try, and relevance remains a requirement. If recurrence is necessary, document why the proposed alternatives are less suitable rather than quietly repeating or adding filler.

Strength exercises, including light resilience work, may recur when they support progression. Keep previous prescription → current dose → reason → next criterion traceable. For new explosive drills, keep mechanical quality observations and workloads traceable but establish a new measurement baseline: changing a drill does not establish performance improvement. No actual response still means unknown response, even when a new drill is selected.

## Athlete, space and delivery assumptions

- Baseline: ages 12–14 with established basic lifting and landing technique. Class 1 is not necessarily a first-ever training session. Supervision, demonstrated competence and readiness determine individual loading; no universal kilogram loads, maturity assumptions or invented test results.
- The supplied specification confirms **3 separate lanes, each 10 m**, barbells in multiple sizes, rubber plates, DBs, KBs, sand bags, wall balls, slam balls, medicine balls, one-/two-handed landmines, cones, small hurdles, agility ladders, battle ropes, boxes, light/heavy bands, jump ropes, timing gates, force plates, pull-up bars and benches. Quantities, weights, dimensions, surfaces and device capabilities remain unconfirmed.
- The separate [facility reference](../../docs/programming/FACILITY_AND_EQUIPMENT.md) says **12 m** and uses an older eight-tenet/preparation/90–60-minute architecture. Current user/spec requirements govern this curriculum: preserve seven categories, Access & Prepare 1, 6/2/6 and the tighter 10 m footprint. Do not rewrite the other document or import its booking as confirmation. The physical discrepancy remains recorded for reconciliation.
- Class 1 requires bodyweight space, cones, appropriate DBs, a suitable KB and a fitted stable bench (or suitable stable box for seated work). It assumes neither a rack nor a throwing wall, band anchor, sled, blocks, harness or sliding discs. Equipment-fit replacements are stated in the class.
- Earlier standing/kneeling/hand-supported and falling starts begin at 0 m, drive by 3 m and stop by 9 m. Class 7 seated starts place the feet at 1 m to include the seat in the lane, drive by 4 m and stop by 9 m; its standing fallback returns to the 0 m layout. Class 8 uses a 1 m front-toe origin for both four-point and standing starts, with the crouched hand/rear-foot footprint inside 0–2 m, driving ending by 4 m and stopping by 9 m. Class 10 also places default toes or the standing fallback front toe at 1 m, fits the whole starting body inside 0–2 m, drives by 4 m and stops by 9 m. Class 11 keeps the same 1 m front-toe origin, 0–2 m setup, 4 m drive-end and 9 m stop for auditory and self-start paths. The final metre remains clear. Individual stopping ability is not established by the layout. Use the defined first attempts/readiness checks and one-step regression; stop if controlled delivery is infeasible. Lane width, waiting positions and the return route still need on-site confirmation.
- Only one athlete uses the start lane at a time. One lane may be enough for individual delivery; three lanes do not establish capacity for three simultaneous athletes. Other areas must be protected from running, landings and bell sweep. Do not keep unsupervised children lifting to fill queue time.
- Timing gates and force plates are available categories, but no verified mode/setup is supplied. No device is needed for Class 1. Its start marker is observational and cannot be converted to sprint speed or force. Later device use, if useful, must remain within listed exercise attempts and use verified capabilities.
- Access & Prepare 1 is an existing external sequence: do not author, rename, infer or estimate it. Its actual impact/lifting exposure must enter the real whole-session ledger when supplied. Classes 1–2 estimate: **75–85 minutes each outside preparation**; Class 3: **74–84 minutes outside preparation**; Class 4: **64–74 minutes outside preparation**; Class 5: **65–75 minutes outside preparation**; Class 6: **72–82 minutes outside preparation**; Class 7: **76–86 minutes outside preparation**; Class 8: **74–84 minutes outside preparation**; Class 9: **68–78 minutes outside preparation**; Class 10: **72–82 minutes outside preparation**; Class 11: **73–83 minutes outside preparation**, with prompt equipment access; actual full-session and group duration remain unresolved.
- Other sport, gym and separately programmed tumbling are unknown. The neighboring written classes create potential overlap to review, not cumulative performed workload. Do not assemble every focus plan into the same week by default.

## Prior-work reviews

No Sprinting state/class folder or separate focus-curriculum progress was found in the inspected root workout plans and programming paths. The existing folder convention is one focus per subdirectory. Adjacent Vertical Jumps, Horizontal Jumps, directional/reaction Agility, and force-absorption/elastic-rebound plans contain prescribed lower-body work. Their athlete-feedback records report no actual observations; selected progression/workload records were read for overlapping jumps, starts/cuts, hinges, split squats and calf work. The athleticism plan's week-two attendance/workload file reports `PASS_BOUNDED_WRITTEN_WEEK2_AUDIT`: its modeled scenarios are not athlete attendance.

At Class 2 resumption, the spec snapshot, current state, Class 1, map, full prescription/overlap ledger, audit, source register, drill history and feedback were reviewed; all referenced files existed. No new actual response was present. Only Class 2 was then finalized.

At Class 3 resumption, state references and the spec snapshot were verified, and Classes 1–2 plus the current map, ledger, history, audit/source notes and available feedback were reviewed. No actual completion/recovery was reported. Class 3 alone was finalized with a distinct task allocation and a reduced RDL/walkout dose.

At Class 4 resumption, all state references and Classes 1–3 were checked against their saved hashes; the map, ledger, history, audit/source notes, supplied specification and feedback were reviewed. No new actual response was present. Class 4 alone was finalized, with a stationary upright-support emphasis and a reduced split-squat dose.

At Class 5 resumption, current state references, Classes 1–4 hashes and the specification snapshot were verified. Saved classes, strength anchors, workload/novelty records, audits/source notes and feedback were reviewed; no actual results were present. Class 5 alone was finalized, with floor-based unilateral support/recovery tasks and unchanged strength doses.

At Class 6 resumption, verified current references, preserved Classes 1–5 and the unchanged spec snapshot; reviewed saved work, start/strength anchors, workload, all drill contingencies and feedback. No actual response was reported. Class 6 alone was finalized with a start/upright consolidation, explicit wall/swing contingencies and unchanged strength doses.

At Class 7 resumption, verified current state paths, unchanged Classes 1–6 and the specification snapshot; reviewed all saved work, workload/history and feedback. No actual observations were present. Class 7 alone was finalized with a corrected seated-start footprint, brief force pulses, five distinct task variants, explicit swing recurrence and held strength doses.

At Class 8 resumption, all Class 7 checkpoint hashes matched and current files/feedback were reviewed. No actual observations were present. Class 8 alone was finalized with a straight-line four-point origin, modest linked tasks, a precisely identified forward scoop toss, explicit containment/replacement rules and unchanged strength doses.

At Class 9 resumption, all Class 8 checkpoint hashes matched, the spec snapshot matched the original and all state paths existed. Saved work, workload/identity history and feedback were reviewed; no actual observations were supplied. Class 9 alone was finalized with modest upright-support variants, reduced draft contact/hinge doses, explicit fallback recurrence and unchanged strengthening doses.

At Class 10 resumption, all Class 9 checkpoint hashes, state paths and the unchanged specification snapshot were verified. Reviewed Classes 1–9, start/upright and strength anchors, workload, all default/contingency history, audits/source notes and feedback; no actual results were supplied. Class 10 alone was finalized with returned starts, qualified individual receivers, five proposed task variants, one openly retained paired wall drill and unchanged strengthening doses.

At Class 11 resumption, the Class 10 checkpoint hashes, all state paths and original/snapshot specification matched. Reviewed the current map, Class 10, relevant earlier anchors, all Classes 1–10 defaults/contingencies, workload, audit/source records, equipment and feedback. No actual response was supplied. Class 11 alone was finalized with one simple start cue, isolated supporting work, two openly recurring families and reduced soleus working volume.

No applicable `AGENTS.md` was found in the repository or its ancestor directories checked. No live exercise database or external athlete account was inspected. Local library files provide identity evidence only; canonical readiness/publication is not implied. Exercise mapping and proposed additions are recorded separately, and no library or application records were edited.

## Evidence, style and limits

The design takes inspiration from Overtime Athletes' combination of start practice, directional plyometrics and upright mechanics, keeping each exercise tied to a named task. Its published examples include two-point starts, single-leg broad jumps and A-skips. Local distances, doses, replacements and six-strength-exercise architecture are authored for this request, not copied from an OTA program. [OTA speed-drill guidance](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/soccer-speed-drills/), [OTA two-point-start example](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/strength-training-for-basketball/).

Ground-force application and hip/ankle function provide mechanical reasons for these support jobs. They do not demonstrate that this exact collection of exercises improves sprint times in these athletes. Upright skipping is a constrained coordination drill, not top-speed running; force capacity and technique learned in the gym still require actual running practice for sport-specific integration when appropriate space is available. [Weyand et al., 2000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11053354/), [Dorn, Schache and Pandy, 2012](https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/article/215/11/1944/10883/Muscular-strategy-shift-in-human-running).

Youth resistance guidance supports supervised, individually appropriate technique, resistance and recovery. It does not validate this exact 14-entry session or establish readiness from age alone. The user's 2–3 technical RIR target and existing competence assumption guide working loads. [NSCA youth resistance training position statement](https://dxpprod.nsca.com/globalassets/about/position-statements/position_stand_youth_resistance_training---2009.pdf).

## Resume rule

Read the spec snapshot, this map, Classes 1–11, ledger, their audits, exercise/source registers, drill history, feedback and `progress.json`; verify their references and reconcile inconsistencies. Review new athlete observations and actual outside workload before developing **Class 12 only**. Review drill history and prioritize distinct explosive drills, while retaining strength anchors where useful. Hold unearned workload increases when response is unknown. Finalize and audit Class 12, then audit all twelve classes for continuity, coverage, realistic progression, exercise identity, workload, recovery, timing and unresolved assumptions. Correct substantive inconsistencies, document changes and verify every requested deliverable before marking the curriculum complete. Save all records and a clear next-training handoff, then stop. A class file is never evidence of athlete completion.

# Sprinting — athlete feedback

**As of 2026-09-13: no actual athlete observations supplied.** This file is a recording guide, not an attendance, readiness or completion record. Leave unreported fields unknown. Neighboring written classes and simulated workload paths are not athlete feedback.

**Class 2 pre-design review:** The above status is unchanged. Neither Class 1 nor Class 2 is recorded as performed. The table below preserves the Class 1 collection fields; the Class 2-specific fields follow it. Always identify the class and drill actually used.

Record a dated observation with its source and athlete/cohort reference when available:

| Field | Actual observation |
|---|---|
| Athlete/cohort, coach/source, training date, report date | Unknown |
| Attendance and actual Class 1 delivery/completion | Unknown |
| Readiness, restrictions, pain, fatigue and movement competence | Unknown |
| Recent and upcoming sprinting, sport, gym, other Vortex plans and separate tumbling | Unknown |

| E1: actual drive/total travel, stopping control, extra contacts and any boundary overrun | Unknown |
| E2/E3: attempted jumps, takeoff/landing sides, distance if recorded, pause/arm conditions, valid holds | Unknown |
| E4/E5: actual rebound/hop counts, skip transfer contacts, amplitude and rhythm/posture changes | Unknown |
| E6: swing or CMJ replacement, implement/load, actual efforts and quality/stop reasons | Unknown |

Separate observations from explanations. Do not add trials solely to fill this form; collect quality observations within prescribed attempts. Log each explosive drill's exact identity so later uniqueness checks distinguish written work from work actually used. When different drills are introduced, their scores are not interchangeable. Missing feedback does not prevent drafting a conditional next class, but does prevent claiming tolerance or earned progression.

## Class 2 collection fields — all currently unknown

- Date/cohort/source and whether Class 1 was actually performed; spacing and other actual sport/gym/tumbling exposure.
- E1 half-kneeling versus low standing, lead leg, one-/two-step choice, attempted starts, low-origin projection faults, actual stopping and route. Record knee comfort and any substitution. Do not compare start-type scores as equivalent tests.
- E2 wall versus high plank, actual exchanges/foot strikes, side counts, hold/reset adherence, trunk/pelvic control and wall/floor setup.
- E3 seated versus unsupported squat jump, seat height/arm policy, attempts, floor-landing control and any extra contacts.
- E4 lead leg for each attempt, preservation of split stance, actual height/control and any unplanned scissor action.
- E5 unilateral versus bilateral, actual hop/landing counts by leg, final hold, additional exit contacts and calf/ankle response.
- E6 actual low-dribble contacts, foot-cycle height, posture/placement/cadence and any extra settling steps.
- All S/P preparation and working work, exact load/leverage/tempo/RIR, P5 laterality, changes and stop reasons; actual section/full-session time and group constraints.
- Subsequent recovery/readiness, especially calf/Achilles, knee, hip/groin and hamstring response; distinguish what the athlete reported from coaching interpretation.

No fields were filled with expected results at Class 2 finalization. Collect observations only within actual delivery; no extra assessment block is authorized.

## Class 3 review and collection — all actual fields remain unknown

No attendance, execution or recovery was supplied for Classes 1–2 before Class 3 design. Adjacent saved feedback statuses also contained no reported actual results. Class 3 is a document, not evidence of a completed exposure.

- Athlete/cohort/source and date; which prior classes actually occurred; actual spacing, readiness/restrictions and outside sport/gym/tumbling work.
- E1 front leg/grounded hand, three-point versus standing, one-/two-step drive, attempts, hand-release/launch faults and stopping/route. No numerical comparison across start types.
- E2 actual box height and working leg, rapid rises and controlled floor returns, trailing-leg assistance, pelvic control and whether the split-jump replacement was used.
- E3 takeoff/receiving leg, actual distance, attempts, held landings and extra free-foot contacts; bilateral-reception substitution if used.
- E4 dynamic dip/arm policy, actual attempts/distance if recorded, landing control and any mistaken pause/no-arm execution.
- E5 actual cycles/target-foot strikes by side, support-foot motion, foot placement, cycle range and any unplanned stance-leg hops.
- E6 band/no band, exact starting posture, nonmoving heel traction, whether tension opposed the knee drive, range, actual cycles, symptoms and substitutions. Do not infer a resisted drive from merely seeing a band.
- S/P actual preparation/working doses, loads/lever endpoints, tempo and technical reserve; confirm the one-working-set RDL and three-cycle walkout as actually delivered or record deviations.
- Section/full-session time, equipment/teaching queues, extended recovery and stopped work; subsequent calf, hamstring, hip/groin and joint response before the next demanding session.

Keep observations separate from interpretation and prescribed counts. Collect within scheduled work rather than adding test attempts. Missing feedback still means unknown response at the next run.


## Class 4 review and collection — all actual fields remain unknown

No actual completion, execution or recovery from Classes 1–3 was supplied before Class 4. Saving Class 4 does not establish a fourth training exposure.

- Date, coach/source and athlete/cohort; which classes actually occurred, recent/upcoming sport/gym/tumbling, readiness and restrictions.
- E1 airborne A-run versus fast march; actual attempted/controlled contacts per foot, start leg, drift, reaching, lean, pelvic drop and extra settling/exit steps. Do not compare scores to low dribbles or skips.
- E2 unilateral versus bilateral jump, actual attempts/receiving legs, height intent, two-second holds and extra hops/contacts.
- E3 flight versus quick-step replacement, actual contacts by foot, knee strategy, amplitude, rhythm, drift and ankle/calf response.
- E4 platform height/stability, support foot staying on it, free-foot taps, pelvic motion and any standing-cycle replacement; record the actual identity rather than assumed novelty.
- E5 seated/standing support, eight intended opposing exchanges, actual count, arm range, shrugging/torso rocking and seat clearance.
- E6 unilateral/bilateral bridge, actual reps by side, hip range, speed, controlled lowering, pelvic position and cramp/symptoms.
- S/P actual preparation and working sets/reps/loads, leverage, tempo/range, technical RIR, P5 laterality and whether the reduced one-round split squat was delivered. Record omitted or added work and why.
- Actual section/full-session time, preparation workload, group/staff, queues, extra recovery and substitutions; subsequent symptoms and readiness before the next demanding exposure.

Record observations separately from coach interpretation. Collect within scheduled attempts; no additional assessment block. Unknown fields remain unknown at handoff to Class 5.


## Class 5 review and collection — actual results remain unknown

No attendance, executed workload or recovery from Classes 1–4 was supplied before Class 5. The new class is a prescription only.

- Date, athlete/cohort, source/coach and actual prior attendance; readiness/restrictions, outside sport/gym/tumbling and spacing.
- E1 target side, three intended cycles per target, actual controlled/attempted cycles, contact count, low-leg versus high-leg rhythm, heel recovery, lean/drift and any march replacement.

# Sprinting — progression and workload ledger

**Checkpoint:** 2026-09-13, after Class 11. **Eleven finalized prescriptions: Classes 1–11.** All quantities below are prescribed, not observed. Actual attendance, performed workload, loads, performance, symptoms and recovery remain unknown. No actual exposure is imported from another focus plan.

## Counting conventions

- One jump/hop repetition is one takeoff-flight-landing event, including an unsuccessful attempt. A bilateral landing is one event involving two feet; it is not interchangeable with a unilateral hop or low pogo. Walks and stance changes are not hidden jumps.
- Class 1 E5 uses a session-specific count: one left–right pair includes two step-hop actions. Three pairs = six hops/landings (three on each foot) plus six support-transfer steps/contacts (three per foot). These transfer contacts are additional to the six hop landings. Do not log three pairs as three contacts or as the library's traveling A-skip dose.
- In Classes 1–3, 6–8 and 10–11, E1's first two foot strikes after leaving the start stance are driving contacts. Initial support/pushes and subsequent easing-down contacts are separate; total running contacts cannot be known without observing them. Running steps are not added to the jump-event subtotal. A stop is an episode, not a single impact.
- For unilateral strength, a written set **round** includes both sides; a **bout** is each separately executed side. Bilateral simultaneous work is one bout. A bridge-walkout **cycle** is four alternating heel steps out and four back; a step is not a full repetition.
- Preparation sets, work sets, static holds and ballistic releases are separate. We do not calculate a combined jump-equivalent score or tonnage without actual loads. No workload is labeled safe solely because of a count.
- Totals exclude unknown Access & Prepare 1, walking returns and other training. Log changed/failed attempts, partial cycles, extra preparation sets and unscheduled athlete demonstrations as actual exposure when reported.

## Class 1 — prescribed explosive work

| Slot | Prescription | Planned exposure |
|---|---|---|
| E1 two-point start | 3 × 2 starts, one forward-foot choice each pair | 6 starts: 3 left foot forward, 3 right. Up to 12 driving foot strikes, normally 6 per foot under the two-step prescription. Drive ends by 3 m: **at most 18 m driving travel**. Stop by 9 m: **at most 54 m total outward travel**, including driving and easing down. Six stopping episodes; actual braking steps/distance unknown. |
| E2 paused broad | 2 × 2 | 4 bilateral horizontal takeoffs/landings; static two-second start and two-second finish. Energetic impulse, individually limited distance, no approach. |
| E3 single-leg broad to bilateral landing | 1 × 2 per takeoff leg | 4 unilateral horizontal takeoffs: 2 left, 2 right; 4 bilateral landings with two-second holds. Controlled distance, no repeated bounds. |
| E4 ankle pogo | 1 × 10 | 10 low-amplitude bilateral takeoff/landing events. |
| E5 stationary A-skip | 1 × 3 left–right pairs | 6 low-amplitude unilateral hop takeoffs/landings: 3 per side; **6 additional transfer contacts**, 3 per side. No intended forward travel. |
| E6 two-hand KB swing | 2 × 5 | 10 ballistic hip-extension swings, no intended athlete flight or ball releases. Record load and any unintended stepping. |

**Default jump/hop subtotal:** **24 landing events** = 8 horizontal jumps + 10 low pogos + 6 low skip hops. Takeoffs: 14 bilateral and 10 unilateral (5 each leg). Landings: 18 bilateral and 6 unilateral (3 each leg). These landing events entail 42 individual foot impacts, plus E5's 6 transfer contacts = **48 drill-related foot contacts**, reported as different types, not equivalent loading. E1 running contacts are additional and not fully known from its distance. No depth drops, continuous horizontal bounds, approach jumps, throws or maximum-velocity running are prescribed.

**Travel convention:** 18 m and 54 m are upper bounds, not fixed completed distances. Total outward path is the sum of each start's actual driving and slowing distances, capped at 9 m each. Do not add 18 m to 54 m. E2/E3 actual jump distances and walking returns are recorded separately; no total sprint metres are inferred from jump distances.

## Class 1 — prescribed strengthening

| Slot | Dose | Rounds / bouts / work |
|---|---|---|
| S1 short-foot | 1 × 3 × 5 s per foot | 1 / 2 / 6 holds, **30 foot-seconds**, easy. Both feet remain supported. |
| S2 side-lying hip abduction | 1 × 6 per side, 5 s/repetition | 1 / 2 / **12 reps**, 60 s active time, easy. |
| P1 split squat | 2 × 5 per leg | 2 / 4 / **20 reps**, 10 per leg, 2–3 technical RIR. |
| P2 DB RDL | 2 × 6 bilateral | 2 / 2 / **12 reps**, 2–3 RIR. |
| P3 seated DB hip flexion | 1 × 6 per leg | 1 / 2 / **12 reps**, 6 per leg, 2–3 RIR. |
| P4 bridge walkout | 1 × 4 complete cycles | 1 / 1 / **4 cycles = 32 heel steps**; about 32–40 s work, 2–3 cycles in reserve. |
| P5 bilateral standing DB calf raise | 1 × 10 | 1 / 1 / **10 bilateral reps**, 2–3 RIR. |
| P6 seated bent-knee soleus raise | 2 × 8 bilateral | 2 / 2 / **16 bilateral reps**, 2–3 RIR. |

**Light work:** 2 rounds / 4 bouts; 12 dynamic reps plus 30 foot-seconds of holds. **Primary work:** **9 rounds / 12 bouts; 70 dynamic reps plus 4 walkout cycles**. Both legs participate in each bilateral rep; do not double the repetition count. Two split-squat rounds are four side-specific bouts, not two total leg sets.

**Declared load-preparation work:** P1 4/leg (8); P2 5 + 3 (8); P3 3/leg (6); P4 1 short-lever cycle (8 small steps); P5 5 bilateral; P6 5 bilateral. Total **7 rounds / 9 bouts; 32 dynamic reps plus 1 walkout cycle**. Extra ramps are permitted only within listed movements and must be logged. No attempt to count Access & Prepare 1 is made.

## Replacement accounting

- **E1 one-step start:** use for remaining scheduled attempts, not as an added drill. If used for all six attempts, six driving foot strikes replace twelve; actual per-foot contacts and travel must be recorded. With mixed delivery, log the exact one-/two-step attempts. Do not reuse a two-step quality comparison silently.
- **E6 hands-on-hips CMJ to stick instead of KB swing:** six added bilateral jump landings; zero swings if fully substituted. The default jump/hop subtotal becomes **30**, comprising 8 horizontal, 6 dynamic vertical, 10 low pogos, 6 low skip hops. Bilateral landings become 24, unilateral remain 6. Foot contacts from jumps/skips become 60 including transfer steps. Sprint contacts remain separate. Allow about one additional minute for jump resets.

| Slot | Prescription | Planned exposure |
|---|---|---|
| E1 split-stance auditory start | Two pairs, one/front leg each pair | Four cue opportunities/four planned starts; at most eight driving strikes and 12 m drive within 32 m outward start/slowing travel. Front toes 1 m, setup 0–2 m, drive by 4 m, stop by 9 m. Early/missed opportunities are not made up. |
| E2 same-leg broad to stick | Two/takeoff and receiving leg | Four unilateral forward receivers + four controlled free-foot set-downs. |
| E3 split-base scoop toss | Two/lead | Four releases, feet planted; retrieval and full rest follow each throw. |
| E4 isolated A-switch to stick | Two/initially raised knee | Four unilateral in-place flight receivers + four finish set-downs. Included in the flight subtotal, not also running. |
| E5 full-cycle strike | Three/moving leg | Six nonflight target-foot strikes, other foot planted; intentional Class 3 repeat. |
| E6 standing arm action | Two bouts of four exchanges | Eight opposing arm exchanges with feet planted; intentional Class 4 contingency recurrence. |

**Flight subtotal: eight unilateral events / eight landing foot impacts**, comprising four forward same-leg hops and four low in-place exchanges. **Eight controlled free-foot set-downs** remain separate. Four throws and six nonflight cycle strikes are different exposure types. Zero continuous upright-running contacts, wall contacts/pulses, default swings and actual maximum-velocity runs. Start slowing/return and ball retrieval contacts remain observed quantities.

### Strength continuity from Class 10 to Class 11

| Entry | Previous prescribed dose → current dose | Reason and next criterion |
|---|---|---|
| S1 short foot | 1 × 3 × 5 s/foot → unchanged | Easy foot-force/control support for initial push and individual receivers; keep toes/foot organized at light effort. |
| S2 side-lying abduction | 1 × 6/side → unchanged | Easy pelvic-control capacity in same-leg reception and free-leg recovery; avoid pre-fatigue. |
| P1 DB split squat | 1 × 5/leg → unchanged | Retain loaded leg-extension force for the staggered push and support. |
| P2 DB RDL | 1 × 6 → unchanged | Retain flexed-hip force for start and external-release initiation. |
| P3 seated DB hip flexion | 1 × 6/leg → unchanged | Retain loaded thigh-recovery capacity for E1/E4/E5. |
| P4 bridge walkout | 1 × 3 cycles → unchanged | Retain knee-flexor capacity through E5's opening/returning lever. |
| P5 standing bilateral calf | 1 × 10 → unchanged | Retain near-straight-knee ankle force for the lengthening driving leg and upright support. |
| P6 bent-knee seated soleus | 2 × 8 → **1 × 8** | Reduce planned ankle-strength overlap while preserving a challenging flexed-knee contribution; do not restore the set by class number. |

Light: **2 rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps + 30 foot-seconds**, RPE 3–4. Primary: **6 rounds / 8 bouts / 46 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, 2–3 technical RIR. Preparation stays **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps + 1 cycle**. The P6 change removes eight working reps and 130 modeled seconds; actual loads and recovery remain unknown. All future strength changes require actual clean work at target reserve, matched protocols and adequate subsequent recovery; missing feedback calls for qualification/hold or reduction.

E5 continuity: **Class 3 six cycles → same dose/rest in Class 11 → full-cycle placement without further flight → retain/simplify based on actual nearby contacts and pelvic control**. E6 continuity: **Class 4 standing contingency eight exchanges/75 s → same Class 11 prescription → direct arm timing without foot contacts → retain/reduce from actual relaxed posture**. Neither earlier written entry proves it was performed.

### Replacement and recovery accounting

- E1 self-start removes the external-onset requirement while preserving the four-opportunity ceiling and lane. One-step starts cap driving contacts at four if used throughout; no extra accepted-reaction attempts.
- E2 shared receivers change the flight subtotal, with default E4, to **eight events / 12 landing foot impacts + four separate set-downs**. Bilateral-origin broad also changes the takeoff. Both are earlier families.
- E3 parallel tosses retain four releases; parked swing or rapid bilateral bridge paths replace those with four floats or four nonflight hip rises. Record actual identity, load and setup rather than completed throws.
- E4 nonflight exchange removes four airborne receivers and provides **four support-transfer placements + four finish set-downs**. Its body-support change remains distinct from E5's planted-support cycle/downstroke.
- E5 downstroke keeps six target-foot returns with a simpler recovery path. E6 seated arms keeps eight exchanges/rest with different support. Alternatives are used instead of the defaults.
- Supported unilateral P5 gives **9 primary bouts / 48 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, and **10 preparation bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**, about one additional minute.
- Four proposed task variants and two declared recurrences serve consolidation. The external start cue changes onset, not start kinematics. Fewer contact/strength counts than selected prior allocations do not establish lower actual tissue load or fatigue; all current flight receivers are unilateral and E2's horizontal same-leg reception is a new condition to qualify.

**Observed Class 11:** unknown. Modeled subtotal **4,347 seconds / 72.45 minutes**, allowance **73–83 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1**. Signal instruction and ball retrieval explain why fewer strength reps do not ensure a shorter session. Full-session/group fit, preparation, booking, queues and actual recovery remain unresolved; a 60-minute complete booking cannot fit. Qualify cue access, full starting/stopping footprint, individual receiving and complete ball containment or use the prescribed replacements. Actual surrounding sport/gym/tumbling governs scheduling.

## Handoff

Next run: review Classes 1–11, map, ledger, every default/contingency, audits/source notes, current state and actual feedback, then finalize **Class 12 only**. Audit all twelve classes for continuity, coverage, realistic progression, identity/recurrence, dosage, recovery, setup/timing and unaddressed assumptions; correct substantive inconsistencies and document changes. Verify all requested deliverables before marking the curriculum complete. Missing actual response stays unknown; no claim that saved classes were performed or that gym observations prove top-speed improvement.

# Sprinting — Class 1 of 12

**Primary effort:** Project out of a two-point start through the first two steps with a connected trunk and pelvis. Build the hip and ankle capacities that support those steps, with a small introduction to upright contact and thigh-recovery mechanics.

**Baseline:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting and landing technique, under qualified coaching. Individual readiness, recent training, restrictions and actual exercise competence remain unknown. This is a finalized, conditional prescription; no athlete completion is recorded.

**Scope:** `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. Today emphasizes straight-line starts. Everything beyond the very short start is supplemental gym work. There is **no actual maximum-velocity running** in this class and no claim that gym drills replace it.

**Quality marker:** During E1's six scheduled attempts, record whether the athlete pushes into the first two steps without a backward rock, waist fold, conspicuous reaching foot or immediate upward jump, and then stops inside the boundary. Record each criterion separately and valid attempts out of attempts actually made; never add attempts to improve a score. This is a coaching observation, not a sprint-time or force test.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload are unknown here. Reference it unchanged; do not create a replacement sequence. The coach must establish readiness for the listed efforts from the athlete's actual preparation and condition.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

E1 gets the greatest practice and recovery investment. Complete exercises in order. Jumps use bodyweight; speed and clean execution take priority over height, distance or fatigue.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Two-point start — two-step projection** | **3 × 2 starts**; one with each foot forward per pair. Two driving foot strikes, ending by 3 m, then ease down and stop by 9 m. **75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.** | **Primary start anchor:** coordinate the first push, reciprocal arm action and the first two ground contacts. Set a comfortable stagger; hold still briefly, then self-start. Push the floor behind you without deliberately lengthening the stride. First pair uses controlled fast intent to establish the route; remaining pairs use the fastest clean intent that preserves stopping room. |
| 2 | **Paused Broad Jump to Stick** | **2 × 2**. Hold a comfortable shallow squat **2 s**, hands on hips; jump forward without re-dipping. **20 s between reps; 90 s between sets.** | Express horizontal impulse from stillness without a running approach or arm contribution. Use an energetic push to a coach-selected distance that permits a two-foot, two-second landing hold. Shorten distance if the athlete reaches with the feet or cannot hold. |
| 3 | **Single-leg Broad Jump to Two-foot Landing** | **1 × 2 per takeoff leg**. Natural arms, modest dip, controlled distance. **20 s between same-leg reps; 45 s before changing legs.** | Load each leg's forward push separately while keeping the receiving task bilateral. Push from one foot, then land on both; hold **2 s**. Reduce distance for twisting, uncontrolled takeoff or a staggered landing; do not add reps to a visually weaker side. |
| 4 | **Ankle Pogo in Place** | **1 × 10 rebounds**, low amplitude, bodyweight. | Isolate quick ankle recoil in a tall bilateral stance before integrating alternating contacts. Use small knee motion, brief contacts and quiet rhythm; do not chase jump height. Stop the set when contacts become heavy, the knees deepen or rhythm breaks. |
| 5 | **Stationary A-Skip** | **1 × 3 left–right pairs** = 6 step-hop actions: **3 per side**. Low amplitude, continuous rhythm, approximately 8–12 s; reps govern. | Link upright support with reciprocal thigh recovery and opposite-arm timing. Step onto the left foot and hop on it as the right thigh rises; step onto the right and hop as the left rises. Stay in place, ribs over pelvis, contact close beneath the body. Reduce thigh height/amplitude for leaning or reaching; this must retain a crisp hop, not become a slow march. |
| 6 | **Kettlebell Swing — two hands, chest-height ceiling** | **2 × 5**, light enough for a crisp hip-driven float. **90 s between sets.** Five full outward swings, then park under control. | Express rapid hip extension against an external load without further landing impacts. Hinge, hike, snap the hips and let the bell float; keep feet planted and finish tall without leaning back or lifting with the arms. Lower load for a slowing float or lost hinge. |

**Recovery between exercises:** After the last effort of E1, E2 and E3, allow **90 s** before the next exercise; after E4, E5 and E6 allow **60 s**. Instruction/setup may occupy that recovery; it is not an extra clock to count twice. Extend rest if breathing, concentration or force expression has not recovered. No conditioning rotations.

**Start layout and limits:** Use **one protected 10 m lane**: start at 0 m; stop driving after two contacts or at 3 m, whichever comes first; progressively ease down to a stop no later than 9 m; leave 9–10 m clear as reserve. These are planning boundaries, not proof that every athlete can stop there. Never sprint the full lane, aim for a hard stop at 3 m, or concatenate the three lanes. One athlete moves at a time; the lane remains closed while that athlete walks back. Waiting athletes and equipment need a separate verified space. Coach from the side outside the path. If the first controlled attempts reveal insufficient room, **use a one-step start instead of the two-step start** for remaining scheduled attempts, lowering intent as needed; record the change. If that still cannot be controlled, stop E1 and record incomplete work.

**Other space and replacement details:** E2/E3 each use a clear part of the same lane with the intended landing inside its first 3 m and further empty space beyond; distance is individualized and never a target to chase. E4/E5 need a clear impact-appropriate floor; E6 needs unobstructed bell sweep, grip and overhead clearance. If the athlete lacks a qualified swing or no suitable bell fits, **use hands-on-hips Countermovement Jump to Stick instead of E6**, **2 × 3**, 20 s between jumps and 90 s between sets. Use a shallow continuous dip, energetic vertical takeoff and a two-second two-foot finish. This changes the job to unloaded dynamic vertical extension and adds six bilateral landing events; log it as a different exercise, not ten swings.

**Quality rules:** A faulty attempt still counts as exposure. Cue or reduce demand before the next scheduled effort; repeated loss of the same criterion despite adjustment ends that exercise. Pain, altered gait, a slip or loss of control ends the affected task immediately. Do not fill stopped work with unlisted exercises or replacement attempts.

## 3. Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) — Exactly 2 Exercises

Keep these easy: approximately **RPE 3–4/10**, well short of fatigue. Bodyweight is sufficient. These are controlled strengthening doses, not mobility or balance tests.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Short-Foot Drill** | **1 × 3 holds × 5 s per foot**; both feet remain supported. Release **5 s between holds; 20 s between feet.** | Practice maintaining the heel, big-toe base and little-toe base while gently raising the working arch. This provides a controllable foot base for the start push and ankle loading without another calf set. Keep toes long; reduce effort or **use seated foot doming instead of standing** if toes claw or the foot rolls. |
| 2 | **Side-Lying Hip Abduction** | **1 × 6 per side**; bodyweight, **2 s up / 1 s hold / 2 s down**. **20 s between sides.** | Give the lateral hip a small, isolated strengthening dose for pelvic control over the stance leg. Bottom knee bent, top leg straight and in line with the torso; lift only while the pelvis stays stacked and the toes face forward. Reduce range if the pelvis rolls or the thigh drifts forward. |

Allow **45 s between S1 and S2**, and **60 s after S2** before primary-strength preparation sets. Neither exercise should create a burn that changes the first lifting set. Stop for pain or persistent compensation.

## 4. Strength (Primary) — Exactly 6 Exercises

Choose working loads or leverage that leave approximately **2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve (RIR)** at the prescribed endpoint. A clean but very easy set is a load-selection observation, not a reason to add repetitions. Do not use maximal tests, forced reps or grinding. Lower under control and lift deliberately; the fast-intent strength lifts need not move at ballistic speed.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides** | **2 × 5 per leg**, 2–3 RIR. Lower **2 s**, rise strongly. **60 s between legs; 120 s between rounds.** | **Main strength anchor:** strengthen lead-leg knee and hip extension in a stable split base for the initial sprint push. Both feet stay on the floor; use a modest whole-trunk forward inclination without rounding. Reduce load/depth for rear-leg hopping, knee collapse or pelvic rotation. |
| 2 | **Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells** | **2 × 6**, 2–3 RIR. **2 s down**, controlled strong ascent; **120 s between sets.** | Load hip extension with the hips flexed and hamstrings lengthened, complementing the knee-dominant component of P1 and the rapid hinge in E6. Soft knees, bells close, stop depth before the pelvis or spine compensates. Reduce range/load if control is lost. |
| 3 | **Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion** | **1 × 6 per leg**, 2–3 RIR. **1 s lift / 1 s hold / 2 s lower**; **45 s between legs.** | Directly strengthen thigh lifting while the trunk stays still, supporting swing-leg recovery rather than adding another squat. Sit near the front of a stable bench, starting with the foot supported and knee near a right angle. Secure a light DB across the distal thigh above the knee with both hands; lift the knee a few centimetres without hand assistance or leaning back. Return the foot gently. Reduce load/range for tipping, pinching or a shifting implement. |
| 4 | **Glute Bridge Walkout** | **1 × 4 complete cycles**, choose heel-step length for **2–3 clean cycles in reserve**. Each cycle = **4 alternating small heel steps out + 4 back**, about **8–10 s**. | Strengthen knee-flexor support as the knee opens while the pelvis stays raised. This adds a knee-extension/return demand to P2's hip hinge; it does not reproduce sprint swing speed. Start in a bilateral bridge, walk out only to a controlled soft-knee position, return to the original heel positions. Shorten steps for sagging or cramp; stop if control cannot be restored. |
| 5 | **Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, floor range** | **1 × 10**, 2–3 RIR. **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower**, heels return to floor. | Strengthen plantarflexion with the knees nearly straight for ankle force capacity, complementing the low-load recoil work. Hold DBs at sides; rise through both forefeet without rolling outward, bouncing or locking knees. Reduce load for lost heel height. If balance limits force, **use a single-leg calf raise with one DB and light contact on a verified stable support instead of this version**, **1 × 6 per leg**, same tempo, **30 s between legs**; log the changed laterality. |
| 6 | **Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, bilateral DB loading** | **2 × 8**, 2–3 RIR. **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower / 1 s bottom**; **90 s between sets.** | Load plantarflexion with flexed knees, giving the knee-flexed ankle-support task its own small strength dose. Keep knees near a right angle, weights secured on thighs above the knees, forefeet planted and heel travel repeatable. Reduce load if knees straighten, feet roll or the athlete bounces. |

**Load-preparation work — not working sets:** In the already listed movements, use P1 **1 × 4/leg** bodyweight or light (30 s between sides; 60 s before working); P2 **1 × 5 easy then 1 × 3 moderate** (60 s between; 90 s before working); P3 **1 × 3/leg light** (30 s between; 45 s before working); P4 **1 short-lever cycle** (45 s before working); P5 **1 × 5 easy** (45 s before working); P6 **1 × 5 easy** (60 s before working). These do not replace Access & Prepare 1. Add a small preparation set of the same movement only if needed to establish an appropriate load; record its work and added time. P5's single-leg replacement uses **1 × 3/leg easy** preparation, 20 s between sides and 45 s before working.

**Between primary exercises:** Allow **120 s after P1 and P2**, and **90 s after P3, P4 and P5**, before the next exercise's preparation set; equipment changes and instruction can occupy that time. No additional mandatory rest is assigned after the last set of P6. Keep all six productive by preserving these rests and reducing an inappropriate load rather than rushing. If bench height is unsuitable for P3/P6, **use a suitably sized stable box instead of the bench** for the same seated exercise; equipment fit and load range must be checked.

**Timing and delivery:** Budget approximately **75–85 minutes after Access & Prepare 1** for an athlete with prompt equipment access: roughly 30 min explosiveness, 6 min stabilization, 39 min primary work, including the listed rests, preparation sets, instruction and transitions; the upper end allows additional routine adjustment. Extra coaching, added ramps and group queues can extend this. The full session duration is unresolved because preparation duration and the actual booking/group/staff are unknown. A 60-minute total booking does not fit this prescription; a 90-minute total booking is not yet confirmed to fit. See the [timing audit](../supporting/class_01_audit.md).

**Recovery and scheduling:** Treat this as a demanding lower-body exposure despite the short running distance. Review actual sprinting, jumps, sport, gym and separately programmed tumbling before scheduling; other written Vortex classes are not evidence of completed work. A nonconsecutive demanding lower-body exposure, often around 48–72 hours later, is a planning starting point only. Adjust to actual fatigue, symptoms, soreness, movement quality and upcoming sport; elapsed time alone does not establish readiness. Do not add this session on top of another full lower-body plan without reconciling their actual doses.

**Progression note:** This establishes the first Sprinting prescription, not an earned increase from prior training. Per the updated user preference, prioritize distinct explosive drills across classes; retain useful strength lifts such as P1 for traceable progression. Class 2 should address the next opening-push demand through a meaningfully different drill, selected after reviewing E1 observations and the drill history. A new drill is not an earned intensity increase: with missing feedback, use a conditional entry dose and do not raise the total workload by default. Compare numerical results only within the same exercise and protocol. Any explosive-drill recurrence needs a specific relevance or feasibility justification, not convenience; do not invent cosmetic variants just to claim uniqueness.

**Audit summary:** Exact 6/2/6 counts are met; all 14 slots have distinct jobs. Review reduced repeated plyometrics to eight horizontal jump landings, ten low pogos and six low skip-hop landings, with six additional skip transfer contacts; E1 running contacts are separate. Only two loaded compound patterns receive two working rounds; direct hip flexion, a small walkout dose and two knee-angle ankle tasks fill the remaining strength roles. Wall attachments, throwing clearance, sleds, racks and long runways are not required. Six starts do not test top speed. Outstanding conditions are actual readiness/exposure, the 10 m versus 12 m facility discrepancy, surface/width, bench/load fit, equipment quantities, preparation time and group delivery. Detailed evidence and workload are in the [curriculum](../curriculum.md) and [ledger](../progression_ledger.md).

# Sprinting — Class 11 of 12

**Primary effort:** Initiate a clean forward push on one clear signal, then organize individual support and limb recovery without accumulating long drill bouts.

**Baseline and review:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting/landing technique and qualified coaching. Reviewed Classes 1–10, anchors, workload, all drill contingencies, equipment and feedback. **Actual attendance, execution, loads and recovery remain unknown.** Four proposed task variants are paired with two openly retained drill families. Soleus working volume is reduced; other strengthening doses hold. This is a conditional prescription, not a claim that ten exposures earned progression.

**Framework:** `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. The signal has one known forward response; it does not create a direction-choice agility task. Upright work stays stationary and supplemental. No actual maximum-velocity running is prescribed.

**Quality marker within E1:** Record assigned front foot, cue opportunity, whether movement began before/after the cue, forward push, body control and stopping for the four scheduled opportunities. A coach observation is not a measured reaction time. Keep this record separate from earlier self-start scores.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload remain unknown here. Use actual preparation/readiness to qualify today's tasks; no replacement sequence is created.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

E1 receives the main performance practice. Supporting work separates same-leg forward reception, externally loaded projection, a resettable upright exchange, free-leg placement and rapid opposing arms. Keep distances, heights and bout lengths modest; full resets preserve quality.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Split-Stance Auditory Sprint Start — first two steps** | **2 × 2 starts**, one/front leg per pair; four cue opportunities total. Front toes **1 m**, whole starting body inside **0–2 m**. At most **2 driving strikes or 3 m drive**, ending by **4 m**; progressively slow and stop by **9 m**. **75 s between opportunities; 120 s between pairs.** | **Main task:** preserve a useful staggered push while waiting for an external start signal. Use a comfortable two-point stagger and forward whole-body inclination, hands free. After the athlete settles, the coach waits an unannounced **2–4 s**, then says one clear, non-startling **“go”** from a verified position outside the lane. Push straight forward with natural opposing arms; no rocking, backward step or guessed launch. First pair is controlled-fast to establish stopping; faster intent in the second requires control. Do not force an upright transition in two steps. |
| 2 | **Single-Leg Broad Jump to Same-Leg Stick** | **1 × 2 per takeoff/receiving leg**, bodyweight, modest distance, natural dip/arms; hold **2 s**, then gently set the free foot down. **20 s between same-leg reps; 60 s between legs.** | Link one leg's forward push to controlled reception on that same leg, supporting individual force acceptance after a start. Use a small hip/knee dip, project forward and bring the receiving foot beneath the body; no linked second jump or distance record. Keep the pelvis facing forward and avoid reaching or an extra hop. Shorten distance for unstable reception; use the shared receiver below if this demand cannot be qualified. |
| 3 | **Split-Stance Forward Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — no step** | **1 × 2 per lead leg**, light suitable ball; **30 s after retrieval between throws, 90 s after retrieval between leads**. Four throws; no catch, jump or step. | Express leg/hip drive into a forward external release while retaining the asymmetric base used for E1. Both feet contribute: front foot flat, rear forefoot supported, hip-width tracks and modest stagger. Hold the ball below the hips in two hands; use a small hinge/knee bend, then extend and scoop forward underhand without twisting or an arm-only heave. Keep feet behind the **1 m line**, whole stance inside the lane, and finish balanced. Aim for a modest floor landing around **3–4 m**, only within the qualified containment layout below. Reduce ball mass/range for a slow release, rotation or a recovery step. |
| 4 | **Standing A-Switch to Stick — isolated support exchange** | **1 × 2 per initially raised knee**; one small airborne exchange per rep, **2 s receiving hold**, then gentle free-foot set-down. **20 s between reps; 60 s between starting sides.** Four exchanges total. | Quickly exchange thigh positions into upright individual support, then stabilize the new position before another attempt. Begin tall on one foot, opposite knee comfortably raised. Make only enough upward push to exchange legs once; place the previously raised foot near its standing position while the original support knee rises. Natural opposing arms, low flight and no extra bounce. Unlike a continuous A-run, every exchange finishes and resets. Reduce knee height/flight for drift, reaching or trunk motion; use the nonflight replacement if control is unsuitable. |
| 5 | **Standing Single-Leg Cycle and Strike** | **1 × 3 cycles per moving leg**. One compact recovery cycle followed by a quick target-foot strike; **10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs**. | **Intentional Class 3 repeat:** retain a full free-leg recovery/placement task with the support foot planted, adding no flight exchanges after E4. Recover the heel beneath the hip, lift the thigh comfortably, allow modest knee opening, then return the foot quickly beside the support foot. No kick, backward claw, long backswing, hop or deliberate hard stamp. Reduce cycle range for reaching or pelvic motion. One complete cycle is one rep. |
| 6 | **Standing Arm Action Drill — fast opposing exchanges** | **2 × 4 continuous arm exchanges**, bodyweight; **75 s between sets**. One exchange reverses both arms' opposing positions; eight total. Allow about 4 s/bout including the finish. | **Intentional earlier fallback recurrence:** practice quick opposing arm motion for initiation and upright limb timing without another foot-contact task. Parallel feet stay grounded, knees soft and trunk quiet. Move relaxed bent arms from the shoulders through a comfortable sprint-like range; hands do not cross the trunk. Use fast relaxed intent, then relax both arms. Reduce speed/range for shrugging, rocking or back arch. This isolates arms; it does not replace integrated arm–leg practice in E1/E4. |

**Recovery:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Setup/teaching may occupy recovery, counted once. Relax held positions between attempts and extend recovery if force, focus or control has not returned. No work fills waiting time.

**Cue and lane:** The coach confirms the cue is accessible before delivery. Use one protected **10 m lane**, one moving athlete, final metre clear; close the lane during the return. Four starts give at most **32 m outward start/slowing travel**, including at most 12 m drive. A premature start uses one opportunity: ease down inside the same route, log it and take full recovery; do not abruptly freeze or add a penalty start. A missed cue consumes its opportunity and is recorded as no start. Repeated anticipation or unclear/unusable cues triggers the self-start replacement for remaining opportunities. No extra trial or timed-reaction block. Confirm lane width, whole starting footprint, coach/waiting positions, traction and return route. The separate 12 m facility note remains unresolved; use ten metres.

**Throw qualification:** E3 uses the same closed lane after E1 has finished. Use only an intact light ball rated for the floor and with sufficiently low rebound. Verify grip, stance, flight, bounce and roll containment for the actual ball/surface before delivery. Keep all people outside the throw corridor, including lateral rebound space; the ball must settle by **8 m**, leaving **8–10 m clear**. Retrieve only after it settles and the coach releases the lane; full prescribed rest begins after retrieval. Listed balls alone do not prove containment. If this cannot be established, use the nonthrowing replacement; no test throws are added. Other exercises wait until retrieval and lane clearance are complete.

**Replacements — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** Use **Self-Started Two-Point Start instead** for remaining opportunities if cue access/anticipation cannot be managed; same front-toe line, limits, dose and rests. This is an earlier movement family. If stopping is insufficient, use one driving step at lower intent; stop if still uncontrolled. No additional attempts replace false/missed starts.
- **E2:** Use **Single-Leg Broad Jump to Two-Foot Landing instead**, same four jumps, rests and 2 s holds, if unilateral reception is unsuitable; Class 1 recurrence, removing the four separate free-foot set-downs. If unilateral takeoff itself cannot be qualified, use **Bilateral Broad Jump to Stick instead**, **2 × 2**, modest dip/arms, 20 s between reps and 60 s between sets. Choose one replacement, not both.
- **E3:** If only split-base control is unsuitable, use **Parallel Forward Scoop Toss instead**, **2 × 2**, same ball/containment, 30 s after retrieval between throws and 90 s between sets; Class 8 recurrence. If throwing cannot be qualified, use **Dead-Stop Two-Hand Kettlebell Swing instead**, **2 × 2 parked singles**, 20 s between reps and 90 s between sets; technically qualified light-to-moderate bell, one hike/hip-driven float no higher than chest level, controlled park, feet planted. Verify bell sweep/grip/space. If that setup is also unsuitable, use **Rapid Bilateral Glute Bridge instead**, **1 × 4**, quick hip rise / 1 s neutral finish / 2 s lower, **10 s between reps**; heels planted, no back arch. These are earlier families; choose one path only.
- **E4:** Use **Nonflight A-Step Exchange to Hold instead**, same four reps, holds and rests. From one-foot support, lower the raised foot beside its standing position before lifting the other knee; one foot always remains down. Hold 2 s, then set the free foot down. Four support-transfer placements plus four finish set-downs replace four flight receivers plus four set-downs. E5 keeps one support foot planted throughout and has a separate full-cycle job.
- **E5:** Use **Standing Straight-Leg Downstroke instead**, **1 × 3/leg**, controlled 1 s low forward lift with a soft knee, quick light return beside the support foot; 10 s resets and 45 s between legs. This repeats Class 9 and removes the full recovery cycle. Reduce range for reaching or discomfort.
- **E6:** Use **Seated Arm Action Drill instead**, same eight exchanges/rest, on a fitted stable bench/box with feet grounded and arm clearance; Class 4 recurrence. Stop if rapid relaxed action cannot be maintained after reducing range/speed.

**Quality rules:** Failed attempts count as exposure. Adjust the next scheduled attempt; persistent faults despite adjustment end that task. Pain, slipping, changed gait, lost control, cue distress or lane intrusion stops the affected work. Record actual defaults/replacements, contacts, set-downs, outside work, omissions and reasons. Incomplete delivery stays incomplete; no make-up attempts or extra exercise slots.

## 3. Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) — Exactly 2 Exercises

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload remain unknown here. Use actual preparation/readiness to qualify the listed tasks; no replacement preparation is created.
