E1 is the main rapid coordination task. Complete exercises in order. Brief supporting doses serve different parts of the same support/recovery effort; speed must remain clean and unforced.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Stationary Single-Leg High-Knee Run** | **1 × 3 cycles per target leg**; **90 s between target legs**. One cycle = target-foot running contact plus opposite-foot running contact: **12 total contacts**, 6/foot. | **Main task:** repeatedly recover one thigh while the other leg uses a low, compact running step. Begin supported on the opposite leg with target thigh comfortably raised. Exchange onto the target foot, then onto the opposite foot as the target heel folds beneath the hip and its thigh rises again. Repeat this asymmetric rhythm without a full cycle on the low-step leg. Use small flight, natural arms and nearby foot contacts; do not hop twice on one foot. Finish the third cycle under control. Lower knee height/speed for long backswing, drift, reaching or backward lean. |
| 2 | **Single-Leg Vertical Jump to Two-Foot Landing** | **1 × 2 per takeoff leg**, bodyweight, natural arms; forceful push at modest height. **20 s between same-leg reps; 60 s between legs.** | Express each leg's upward push while the free thigh rises, then share reception across both feet. Use a small countermovement on the takeoff leg; jump upward and bring both feet beneath the body for a **2 s held landing**. This changes Class 4's same-leg receiver rather than demanding greater height. Reduce height for pelvic rotation, wide/asymmetric reception or an extra hop. |
| 3 | **Single-Leg Knee-Drive Pogo — stationary, same support leg** | **1 × 2 hops per support leg**, bodyweight; very low flight. **60 s between legs.** | Couple a quick ankle push on the same leg with a pulse of the opposite thigh. Pop the free thigh forward as the support ankle pushes; let the free leg lower toward a low hover during recoil without touching the floor, then repeat. Keep the support knee soft and the torso tall; the free foot does not become the next support as it does in E1. Hold the final same-leg landing **2 s**, then set the free foot down. Reduce thigh range/amplitude if the two actions cannot stay coordinated. |
| 4 | **Stationary B-Skip — controlled lower-leg release** | **1 × 2 left–right pairs** = **4 step-hop actions**, two per raised-thigh side. Each action has one support-leg hop landing and one raised-foot transfer contact. | Add a controlled lower-leg release to the thigh recovery while preserving the skip rhythm. Lift a thigh during a small hop on the opposite foot; allow the raised knee to open modestly, then bring that foot down near its standing position and transfer support. Alternate sides without traveling. This is not a high straight-leg kick or a backward claw. Reduce knee opening/range for a reaching contact, trunk lean or disrupted rhythm. Finish after the fourth transfer; no extra skip. |
| 5 | **Reverse Lunge to Knee Drive — rapid ascent, no flight** | **1 × 3 per working/front leg**, bodyweight; **2 s lower, quick rise, 1 s tall finish**. **10 s reset between reps; 45 s between legs.** | Drive through a planted front foot while the stepping leg returns forward into thigh recovery. Step the free foot back a comfortable distance, lower into a controlled lunge, then push predominantly through the front leg and bring the rear knee forward/up. The front foot stays flat and planted throughout; no jump. Return the free foot beside it before the next rep. Shorten step/depth for rear-foot propulsion, knee collapse, pelvic hitching or a slow/unstable rise. |
| 6 | **Supine Alternating Hip Switch — both heels off the floor** | **1 × 4 opposing leg exchanges**, bodyweight; **quick switch, 1 s settled finish**, then **10 s reset between exchanges**. Each exchange moves both legs once; two returns to each starting configuration. | Practice rapid opposing thigh motion while the pelvis has floor support, removing the landing task. Lie with one hip/knee comfortably flexed and the other leg reaching diagonally away with a soft knee and heel clear of the floor. Exchange the leg positions through a short controlled range; do not fully straighten the reaching knee or force the thigh to the chest. Keep the pelvis quiet and breathe. Bring both feet down during resets, then gently re-establish the next starting configuration. Shorten the reach/bend the knees more for arching, breath-holding or slowing; stop if control cannot be restored. |

**Recovery:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Resets are recovery rather than extra holds. Setup/instruction can use rest time; count actual elapsed time once. Extend rest if force, focus or movement control has not returned.

**Room and equipment:** All defaults are stationary or use one backward lunge step within a clear floor station. Verify enough width and rear clearance for that step and any unplanned landing adjustment. Keep weights and waiting athletes outside the movement area. No runway, wall, low platform, band anchor, throwing clearance or device is required. The supplied three separate 10 m lanes do not establish group capacity or a continuous runway; the older 12 m facility note remains unresolved. DB ranges, fitted bench/box, surface and quantities still require on-site checks for the strength work.

**Replacements — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** Use **Stationary Single-Leg High-Knee March instead of the airborne run** if the rhythm cannot be controlled: same three cycles/target leg and rest, quick target-leg recovery with one foot always down. Twelve nonflight placements replace twelve running contacts; record the change.

- **E3:** Use **Single-Leg Pogo without the thigh pulse instead of Knee-Drive Pogo** if coordination is the limitation: same two hops/leg and rest. This explicitly repeats the Class 2 family at a lower dose. If unilateral reception itself is unsuitable, use **Bilateral Ankle Pogo instead**, **1 × 4**, very low flight and a 2 s final hold; not both replacements.
- **E4:** Use **Stationary A-Skip instead of B-Skip** if the release produces persistent reaching: same two left–right pairs, four hop landings and four transfer contacts. This repeats Class 1's family and removes the lower-leg release job; do not label it a successful B-skip.

**Quality rules:** Attempted work counts even when faulty. Adjust the next scheduled rep; recurring faults despite adjustment end that task. Pain, slipping, changed gait or loss of control ends the affected exercise immediately. Record omissions, actual replacements, extra settling/exit contacts and reasons. No make-up work or added exercise slots. If neither the default nor its regression is productive, actual delivery is incomplete rather than recorded as fourteen finished exercises.

# Sprinting — Class 4 of 12

**Primary effort:** Keep the pelvis and trunk organized over the supporting leg while the other leg returns quickly to a nearby foot placement. Train upright support and rapid limb action within a stationary gym footprint.

**Baseline and review:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting and landing technique, under qualified coaching. Classes 1–3, their workload and drill history, equipment assumptions and available feedback were reviewed. **Actual attendance, execution and recovery remain unknown.** Today's new drills are conditional entry prescriptions, not earned increases in intensity. The six defaults have distinct tasks; familiar strength lifts recur with one fewer split-squat working round.

**Framework:** This category-wide curriculum retains `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. Today's emphasis is gym support for the latter. There are **no starts or actual maximum-velocity runs in this class**. Stationary placement cues do not describe the exact touchdown geometry of full-speed running, and drill scores do not establish sprint speed.

**Quality marker within E1:** Record attempted and controlled contacts by foot, visible forward/backward drift, pelvic drop, backward trunk lean and conspicuous foot reaching. Observe only the prescribed contacts; no extra trials. A controlled contact preserves the upright position and compact exchange without an extra settling hop. Compare only repetitions of this same A-run protocol, not earlier skips or low dribbles.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload are unknown here. Use actual preparation/readiness to qualify the listed work; no replacement preparation sequence is created.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

E1 is the main coordination/rapid-force task. Work in order, with quick clean intent and small supporting doses. E4–E6 intentionally express speed without jump landings; they are not maximal-load efforts.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Stationary A-Run — alternating high-knee exchanges** | **2 × 6 alternating foot contacts**, 3/foot/set; **90 s between sets**. Bodyweight; quick rhythm without chasing cadence. Start the sets on opposite support legs. | **Main task:** alternate a bent-knee thigh recovery and rapid support exchange while staying tall. Begin on one foot with the other knee comfortably raised; make small airborne exchanges, landing the incoming foot close to its normal standing position as the opposite thigh lifts. No extra bounce between exchanges, forced hip-height target, backward lean or deliberate clawing. Finish on contact six, stabilize, then set the other foot down. Reduce knee height/cadence for drift, reaching or loss of posture. |
| 2 | **Single-Leg Vertical Jump to Same-Leg Stick** | **1 × 2 per leg**, bodyweight, natural arms; modest height with forceful takeoff. **20 s between same-leg reps; 45 s between legs.** | Produce an upward push and receive it over the same foot, separating vertical support from the earlier forward bounds. Use one small countermovement, jump upward and hold the same-leg landing **2 s** before the free foot touches down. Keep the pelvis facing forward and knee tracking with the foot. Lower height for reaching, rotation or a second hop; do not add a rebound. |
| 3 | **Straight-Leg Scissor Bounce in Place** | **1 × 6 alternating landing contacts**, 3/foot; bodyweight, very low flight. | Repeatedly exchange support through the ankles with the knees nearly straight, unlike E1's bent-knee recovery and E2's larger leg drive. Start on one foot; use a tiny forward/backward leg exchange in flight and receive the next foot near the standing position. Knees stay soft, not locked; no high kicks, long reach, double bounce or forward travel. Finish contact six under control, then set the other foot down. Reduce amplitude/speed for hard contacts or lost rhythm. |
| 4 | **Low Box Hip Switch — same free-foot tap and return** | **1 × 3 per moving leg**; bodyweight. Quick floor tap/return, **1 s balanced finish**; **10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs**. | Maintain a level pelvis as the free foot moves between a raised-knee position and a lower contact surface. Keep the entire support foot on a stable platform approximately **10 cm high**; begin with the other thigh comfortably raised. Quickly lower that free foot to a light floor touch beside the platform and return the knee, allowing a small support-knee bend as needed. Switch the arms with the free leg. The support foot stays on the platform: this is not a jumping box exchange or a step-up. Reduce knee range/speed for a hip hitch, forceful floor push or trunk tilt. |
| 5 | **Arm Action Drill — seated fast exchanges** | **2 × 4 continuous arm exchanges**, bodyweight; **75 s between sets**. One rep switches both arms from their opposing positions to the other positions; 8 total exchanges. | Practice quick opposing arm action while the torso stays organized, without adding another ankle-impact task. Sit tall on a fitted stable bench, feet on the floor, no backrest assistance. Move relaxed bent arms forward/backward from the shoulders within a comfortable sprint-like range. Hands do not cross the trunk or strike the seat; avoid shrugging or exaggerated rocking. Use the fastest relaxed exchanges that preserve posture; reduce speed/range if the trunk supplies the movement. This isolates arm action, not complete arm–leg timing. |
| 6 | **Single-Leg Glute Bridge — rapid hip drive** | **1 × 3 per working leg**, bodyweight; **quick rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower**. **10 s reset between reps; 45 s between legs**. | Express hip-extension force rapidly as the hip approaches neutral, supporting the upright position without another landing. Lie with the working foot flat, knee bent; hold the free thigh comfortably toward the torso. Drive the pelvis up quickly until the working thigh and trunk align, then lower under control. Keep the pelvis level, heel down and ribs settled; no lumbar arch, foot launch or maximal bridge height. Shorten the rise for twisting or cramp; if a single-leg drive cannot remain crisp, use the stated replacement. |

**Recovery:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Step out of held positions during resets. Instruction/setup can use rest time; count actual elapsed time once. Extend recovery for incomplete recovery of force, attention or control.

**Space and equipment:** All defaults are stationary, with a clear flat non-slip floor area and clearance for unplanned steps; no run-up or sprint finish. Keep boxes, weights and waiting athletes outside the landing area. A lane can contain the stations sequentially; its length does not establish usable width or simultaneous group capacity. Boxes/benches and DBs are listed equipment, but a suitable approximately 10 cm platform, fitted seat, surface and quantities are unconfirmed. No stacked plates, band anchor, throwing clearance, rack or device is assumed.

**Replacements — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** Use **Fast A-March instead of airborne A-Run** if the athlete cannot control the exchanges: same 2 × 6 alternating placements, 90 s rest, quick foot return without flight or extra bounce. This changes the loading and rhythm; log it as marching, not running.
- **E2:** Use **Bilateral Countermovement Jump to Stick instead of the single-leg jump** if single-leg reception is not qualified: **1 × 4**, modest height, 2 s hold and 20 s between reps. This deliberately reuses the Class 1 optional jump family for readiness.
- **E3:** Use **Alternating Straight-Leg Quick Steps instead of scissor bounces** if flight cannot remain small and controlled: **1 × 6 alternating placements**, knees softly extended and one foot always down. Keep quick placement intent; it is a nonflight replacement, not an equivalent elastic dose.
- **E4:** If no suitably low stable platform is available or its height cannot be managed, use **Standing Single-Leg Cycle and Strike instead of Low Box Hip Switch**, **1 × 3/moving leg**, 10 s resets and 45 s between legs. Keep the support foot planted, recover the free heel/thigh in a compact cycle, then quickly place that foot beside the support foot. This explicitly repeats Class 3 E5; no claim of unique novelty or equal pelvic demand.
- **E5:** A fitted stable box may replace the bench. If neither permits secure seating and arm clearance, use **Standing Arm Action Drill instead of the seated version**, same count/rest, parallel feet grounded and knees soft. Record the changed support condition.
- **E6:** Use **Bilateral Glute Bridge with rapid rise instead of the single-leg version** for persistent twisting or an unproductive unilateral rise: **1 × 6**, same tempo, 10 s between reps. Keep both feet planted; reduced per-leg demand is intentional.

**Quality rules:** Failed attempts count as exposure. Adjust the next scheduled rep; repeated loss of the same criterion despite adjustment ends that task. Pain, slipping, changed gait or loss of control ends the affected exercise immediately. Record omitted work, extra exit steps and actual replacements; no make-up attempts or extra exercises. # Sprinting — Class 10 of 12

**Primary effort:** Initiate forward force from a compact two-foot base, then support prompt free-leg recovery and nearby subsequent contacts. Practice the upright component separately in stationary space.

**Baseline and review:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting/landing technique and qualified coaching. Reviewed Classes 1–9, start/upright and strength anchors, workload, all drill contingencies, equipment and feedback. **Actual attendance, execution, loads and recovery remain unknown.** Five default variants have specific task differences; the paired wall switch deliberately recurs. Strength doses hold, with no inferred tolerance or automatic intensity increase.

**Framework:** `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. Today's starts are straight ahead; upright running drills and targeted strength are supplemental gym work. No actual maximum-velocity running or forced upright transition within the short start is prescribed.

**Quality marker within E1:** Record first stepping foot, setup, attempted/controlled starts, forward push without a backward step, body control and stopping. Observe only the four scheduled attempts. Keep this static bent-over record separate from falling or crouched-start scores.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload remain unknown here. Use actual preparation/readiness to qualify today's tasks; no replacement sequence is created.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

E1 receives the main performance practice. Other entries isolate forward projection, individual reception, upright recovery, inclined support exchange and light resisted thigh force. Use modest jump distances/heights and quick clean intent; do not turn the drills into conditioning.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Bent-Over Sprint Start — parallel feet, first two steps** | **2 × 2 starts**, one with each first stepping foot per pair. Toes at **1 m**; at most **2 driving strikes or 3 m of drive**, ending by **4 m**. Progressively slow and stop by **9 m**. **75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.** | **Main task:** create the first push from a still hand-free hip hinge, then step forward into individual support. Feet parallel near hip width, knees softly bent, hips slightly back, trunk inclined with a comfortable spine and arms free. Fit the whole starting body inside **0–2 m**. Settle **2 s**, push and bring the selected foot through; no backward step, preliminary hop or fall from tall standing. Let the posture rise naturally rather than forcing an early upright position. First pair is controlled-fast to establish stopping; second is faster only while control remains. |
| 2 | **Split-Stance Broad Jump to Split-Stance Stick — same lead** | **1 × 2 per lead leg**, natural dip/arms, modest forward distance; **2 s landing hold**. **20 s between same-lead reps; 60 s between leads.** | Preserve an offset base through forward projection and reception, complementing E1's parallel origin. Both feet contribute and leave the floor; receive with the same leg forward on separate hip-width tracks. Keep the split modest, front foot supported and rear forefoot stable; no scissor exchange or long lunge. Reduce distance/offset for twisting, uneven reception or rear-foot collapse. |
| 3 | **Two-Foot Vertical Jump to Single-Leg Stick** | **1 × 2 per receiving leg**, bodyweight, natural arms and modest height; hold each receiver **2 s**, then set the free foot down gently. **20 s between same-leg reps; 60 s between legs.** | Separate a shared two-foot push from one-leg support, without forward travel. Use a small countermovement with parallel feet; both feet leave before the free leg lifts clear. Bring the selected receiving foot beneath the pelvis, land softly and control the knee/hip without an extra hop. Do not chase height. Use the two-foot replacement if the single-leg receiver cannot be qualified. |
| 4 | **Stationary Alternating Step-Over Run — both legs cycle** | **1 × 8 alternating running contacts**, four/foot, low flight; finish with **one gentle free-foot set-down**. About 5 s including the finish; contacts govern. | Couple compact heel/thigh recovery to modest lower-leg release on both sides before the foot returns nearby. Begin on one foot with the other thigh comfortably raised; alternate supports with natural opposing arms. Let the knee open a little after recovery without a high kick, long backswing or deliberate backward claw. Unlike Class 6's asymmetric drill, both legs use the fuller pattern. Reduce range/speed for reaching, drift or a broken rhythm. |
| 5 | **Wall Drill Double Switch — paired exchanges** | **1 × 2 pairs per initially raised knee**. Each pair = **2 quick switches without an intermediate hold**, then **2 s hold** and a controlled free-foot set-down. **20 s between pairs; 45 s between starting sides.** | **Intentional Class 8 repeat:** retain two consecutive leg exchanges while the forward body line stays controlled, directly supporting the next-contact task after E1. Both hands press a verified immovable wall; switch supports twice and finish with the original knee raised. Keep hips level, elbows steady and feet near their starting positions. Eight fast contacts plus four controlled set-downs. Step out of the lean for recovery; shorten lean/range for sliding or sagging. |
| 6 | **Standing Banded Knee Drive — opposite foot planted** | **1 × 3 per moving leg**, very light suitable closed foot-loop band; quick lift / **1 s finish / 2 s controlled return**. **10 s between reps; 45 s between legs**. | Express rapid thigh recovery against light resistance while the other leg supports the upright body. Start with both feet flat near hip width and a secure loop around the shoe midfeet; the support foot stays flat and still as the moving knee lifts through a comfortable range. The band must oppose the lift. Return the moving foot gently and relax between reps. No added knee extension, hop, torso lean or heavy grinding lift. Reduce tension/range for a slowed drive, pelvic movement or slipping band. |

**Recovery:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Instruction/setup may occupy recovery, counted once. Relax out of held positions between efforts and extend rest when force, focus or control has not returned. No extra contacts fill waits.

**Room and equipment:** Use one protected **10 m lane**, with one athlete moving and the lane closed during return. E1 begins at 1 m and stops by 9 m: **8 m maximum outward travel per start**, including at most 3 m of driving. Verify the whole starting footprint, traction, stopping, lane width, waiting positions and return route. E2/E3 need clear receiving and overshoot space; E4–E6 stay in place. A movable rack/box is not a wall. The older 12 m facility note remains unresolved; no additional run-out is assumed.

**Band qualification:** Use only an intact closed loop intended and sized for the foot setup, securely seated across shoe midfeet, within its stated stretch limit. Check support-foot traction and verify that lifting stretches the band against the moving foot; do not improvise a knot, external anchor or extra loop. Actual loop type/length/tension, wall suitability, surface, equipment sizes, staff and quantities remain unconfirmed. If a fast controlled standing lift cannot be qualified, use the floor replacement before delivery; do not add tension to force a stronger stimulus.

**Replacements — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** If the parallel hinged launch is unproductive, use **Two-Point Standing Start instead**, four starts, front toe at 1 m, rear foot within the protected starting area, same drive/stop limits and rests. This repeats an earlier family. If stopping is insufficient, use one driving step at lower intent for remaining attempts; stop if still uncontrolled. No extra trials.
- **E2:** If split reception is unsuitable, use **Staggered-Stance Broad Jump to Parallel Two-Foot Stick instead**, same four jumps/rests/holds; Class 6 recurrence. If the offset takeoff itself is unproductive, use **Parallel Broad Jump to Stick instead**, same total/rests, natural dip/arms and modest distance; Class 3 recurrence. Choose one replacement, not both.
- **E3:** If single-leg reception is not controlled, use **Bilateral Countermovement Jump to Stick instead**, **2 × 2**, natural arms, modest height and 2 s holds; **20 s between reps, 60 s between sets**. This repeats an earlier fallback family. Four bilateral receivers replace four unilateral receivers; the four separate free-foot set-downs are removed.
- **E4:** If lower-leg release creates persistent reaching, use **Stationary A-Run instead**, eight contacts and one controlled finish set-down; earlier family. If flight is unsuitable, use **Fast A-March instead**, eight alternating controlled foot returns, one foot always down and no extra running finish set-down. No full step-over bout is added afterward.
- **E5:** For lost paired rhythm, use **Isolated Wall Single Switches instead**, eight total, four/foot: hold 2 s, set the free foot down and release the lean for **10 s** before resetting; alternate the initial raised knee. Eight fast contacts plus eight controlled set-downs. Without a qualified wall, use **High-Plank Isolated Single-Switch Knee Drives instead**, eight total: hands beneath shoulders, forward foot hovering, exchange once so only the extending foot lands, hold 2 s, lower knees and rest 10 s before resetting; alternate the initial forward knee. - **E6:** If the band, traction or standing support cannot be qualified, use **Supine Unresisted Knee Drive, opposite heel grounded, instead**, **1 × 3/leg**, quick knee lift / 1 s finish / 2 s controlled lower, 10 s between reps and 45 s between legs. Keep the nonmoving leg comfortably long, heel grounded and pelvis quiet; gently return the moving heel to the floor. This repeats Class 3's fallback with different resistance/support and avoids adding another standing march. Stop for persistent arching or discomfort after reducing range.

**Quality rules:** Failed attempts count as exposure. Adjust the next scheduled rep; persistent faults despite adjustment end that task. Pain, slipping, changed gait, insecure band, lost control or lane intrusion stops the affected work immediately. Log actual substitutions, set-downs, extra contacts, stopping, omissions and reasons. Incomplete delivery remains incomplete; no make-up attempts, added tests or extra slots.

## 3. Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) — Exactly 2 Exercises

# Sprinting — Class 9 of 12

**Primary effort:** Maintain upright support while recovering a compact free leg and returning the foot near the hip, with quick force expression and little unnecessary trunk movement.

**Baseline and review:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting/landing technique and qualified coaching. Reviewed Classes 1–8, upright/start and strength anchors, workload, all drill contingencies, equipment and feedback. **Actual attendance, execution, loads and recovery remain unknown.** This is a conditional upright-support exposure, not evidence that earlier work was tolerated. New variants receive modest entry demands; strength doses hold.

**Framework:** `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. Today emphasizes gym support for upright running. No starts or actual maximum-velocity runs are prescribed; the earlier start work remains part of the curriculum.

**Quality marker within E1:** Record controlled/attempted contacts, whether the knee folds as the thigh comes forward, foot placement, trunk position, drift and extra contacts. Use only the two scheduled bouts. Compare only matched drill conditions; a fuller leg fold is not proof of a faster sprint.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload remain unknown here. Use actual preparation/readiness to qualify the listed work; no replacement sequence is created.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

E1 is the main rapid coordination task. E2 uses knee/hip-driven vertical rebound; E3 uses low ankle-led recoil. E4–E6 supply distinct nonflight placement, limb-timing and hip-force jobs. Keep intent quick and clean, without chasing height, cadence or fatigue.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Stationary High-Knee/Butt-Kick Run — coupled recovery** | **2 × 6 alternating running contacts**, three/foot/bout; **90 s between bouts**. Low flight, bodyweight. Start on opposite support legs; finish each bout with **one gentle free-foot set-down**. | **Main task:** fold the recovering knee while the thigh rises, then return the foot near its standing position. Begin on one foot with the other knee comfortably raised and heel folded beneath the thigh. Exchange supports with natural opposing arms and no extra bounce; allow a compact recovery on each side. Keep the pelvis tall, without forcing a hip-height knee or heel-to-butt contact. This is one integrated running pattern, not separate high-knee and butt-kick sets. Reduce height/speed for reaching, trailing thigh, arching or drift. |
| 2 | **Repeated Vertical Jump — two consecutive jumps, final stick** | **2 × 2 consecutive jumps**, bodyweight, natural arms; **120 s between two-jump bouts**. Modest height, no approach or external drop. | Accept the first vertical receiver and reuse it for another upward leg push. Start with parallel feet and a comfortable knee/hip dip; jump twice without a deliberate pause between them, then hold the final bilateral landing **2 s**. Keep the knees tracking and the torso controlled. Do not take the second jump if the first receiver collapses, twists or needs a deep recovery squat. |
| 3 | **Split-Stance Pogo — same lead retained** | **1 × 2 low hops per lead leg**, four hops total; **60 s between leads**. Bodyweight; final landing held **2 s**. | Keep upright alignment through ankle-led recoil with front/rear support offset. Use a small comfortable split with hip-width spacing, both forefeet contributing, knees soft and nearly unchanged. Both feet leave and return to their own positions together; no scissor exchange, travel, deep split-squat dip or forced toe-only finish. Let the heels settle for the final hold. Reduce offset/amplitude for uneven contacts or trunk pitching. |
| 4 | **Standing Straight-Leg Downstroke — other foot planted** | **1 × 3 per moving leg**, bodyweight; controlled **1 s low forward lift**, quick return near the support foot, then settle. **10 s between reps; 45 s between legs**. | Place a longer recovering leg near the hip through a small hip-driven downstroke, without a full running cycle or support-leg hop. Keep the moving knee softly extended, lift the foot only a little forward/off the floor, then bring it down beside its starting position. The other foot stays planted. Make a precise light contact, not a stomp or backward scrape. Reduce lift/range for pelvic tipping, a reaching contact or hamstring discomfort. |
| 5 | **Seated Alternating Sprint Action — knee lift with opposing arms** | **1 × 6 alternating knee drives**, three/leg; quick lift / **1 s finish / 2 s foot return**. **10 s between reps**, feet down and arms relaxed during resets. Bodyweight. | Couple the rising thigh to opposing arm action while the seat supports body mass. Sit tall on a stable fitted seat, feet initially flat and knees comfortably bent. Lift one thigh a few centimetres while the opposite arm moves forward and the same-side arm moves back; lower the foot gently and reset before alternating. No rocking, hand push, shrug or independent extra arm swings. Reduce the range/speed for lost timing or torso movement. |
| 6 | **Single-Leg Bodyweight Hip Hinge — rapid return** | **1 × 2 per support leg**, bodyweight; **2 s shallow hinge, quick controlled rise, 1 s tall hold**, then gentle free-foot set-down. **10 s between reps; 45 s between legs**. | Express hip extension over one planted foot without another jump landing. With a soft support knee, move the hips back as the trunk inclines slightly and the free leg follows behind; keep the hip points level without opening sideways. Return briskly to tall alignment without throwing the back leg, snapping the spine or adding a knee drive. Use a shallow range and light contact on verified stable hand support if needed. If the return becomes slow balance work, use the floor replacement. |

**Recovery:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Instruction/setup may occupy recovery, counted once. Relax out of held positions between efforts. Extend rest if force, attention or control has not returned; no extra contacts fill the waiting time.

**Room and equipment:** All defaults stay in place within a clear floor/seat station. Verify width and clearance for the hinge's trailing leg, arm action, small landing adjustments and any unplanned step. Keep weights and waiting athletes outside the movement area. A fitted bench or stable box is needed for E5; any optional hand support must be immovable and suitable, not improvised from loose equipment. Seat height, surface, equipment sizes, quantities, staff and group layout are unconfirmed. The three separate 10 m lanes do not establish group capacity or a longer runway; the older 12 m facility note remains unresolved.

**Replacements — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** If the coupled fold cannot stay controlled, use **Stationary A-Run instead**, same two six-contact bouts, rest and finish set-downs; comfortably bent-knee exchanges, without forcing the tighter heel fold. This repeats Class 4. If flight itself is unsuitable, use **Fast A-March instead**, **2 × 6 alternating returning-foot placements**, one foot always down and 90 s rest; no extra running finish set-downs. Record the actual pattern rather than assuming the default occurred.

E1 is the main performance task. E2/E3 supply modest forward projections; E4/E5/E6 express rapid force without jump landings. The wall pulse is a force-onset task, not external movement power or an endurance hold.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Seated Sprint Start — first two steps** | **2 × 2 starts**, one with each first stepping foot per pair. Start with feet at the **1 m line**; at most **2 driving strikes or 3 m of drive**, ending by the **4 m line**. Progressively slow and stop by **9 m**. **75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.** | **Main task:** transfer support from the seat to the feet and initiate forward travel without backward rocking. Sit at the front of a stable fitted bench/box, both feet flat near hip width, knees comfortably bent and trunk slightly inclined forward. Settle for **2 s**, then push up/forward through the legs and take the selected first step; arms assist naturally but hands do not push the seat. Keep the pelvis facing forward during the pause, push forward and hold the bilateral landing **2 s**. The pause changes Class 1's dynamic takeoff task; it does not make the tissues purely concentric. Firm submaximal effort, about **RPE 6–7/10**; **20 s between pulses, 60 s between sides**. | Rehearse rapid force onset through the legs while the body line remains fixed. With both palms on a verified immovable wall near shoulder height, take a comfortable split stance and shallow forward lean. Front foot stays fully planted, rear forefoot supports; quickly push the floor back through the front leg while the hands transmit pressure to the wall. No arm pressing motion, heel pop, rocking, breath-holding or maximal strain. Step out of the lean during recovery. Reduce pressure/lean for lost position; no measured rate-of-force-development claim is made. |
| 5 | **Wall Knee Drive — repeated same moving leg** | **1 × 3 per moving leg**, bodyweight; **quick knee lift / 1 s finish / 2 s controlled foot return**. **10 s reset between reps; 45 s between legs.** | Keep the stance leg transmitting pressure while the other thigh recovers rapidly. Start with both feet on the floor in a comfortable two-hand wall lean. Keep the support foot planted as the target knee lifts forward, then return that foot gently beside its starting position. Repeat the same moving leg; do not swap supports explosively or hop. Reduce range/speed for sag, leaning from the waist or a lifted/sliding support heel. |
| 6 | **Dead-Stop Kettlebell Swing — two hands, one float per reset** | **2 × 3 singles**; **20 s after each parked rep within a set, 90 s between sets**. Light-to-moderate technically qualified bell; crisp drive and controlled park. | **Intentional retained drill:** independently initiate hip drive on each rep, directly matching today's settled-force theme. With the bell parked just ahead within comfortable reach, hinge with a stable spine, hike back once, drive to a tall finish and let the bell float **no higher than chest level**. Guide it back through the hinge and park under control. Feet stay planted; no arm lift, backward lean or release. Reduce load for a slow/unstable rep. Each single still contains a backswing; this is not a claim of zero eccentric loading. |

**Recovery:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Instruction/setup can occupy rest; count actual elapsed time once. Release held positions between efforts and extend recovery if force, attention or control has not returned.

**Room and setup:** Seat plus the athlete's starting feet must fit inside the first metre of one protected **10 m lane**, with feet at 1 m. The seated start therefore has **8 m outward travel** to the 9 m stopping line, including at most 3 m of drive; the final metre stays clear. Verify actual seat footprint, traction and stability before using this layout. It leaves less slowing room than earlier starts, so use the first pair's controlled intent and the stated regression. One athlete moves at a time; close the lane during return and verify coach/waiting positions. E2/E3 use modest distances with clear landing and overshoot space; the seat remains behind the takeoff feet. Wall tasks require a verified immovable non-slip wall; no movable box/rack is assumed suitable. Keep the full bell path separate. Seat/DB/KB sizes, wall suitability, floor, staff and quantities are unknown. The older 12 m facility note remains unresolved; use the tighter 10 m footprint.

**Replacements — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** If the seat cannot fit securely or the rise is unproductive, use **Two-Point Standing Start instead of seated start**, four starts, feet at **0 m**, drive at most two steps/3 m, stop by 9 m. This repeats an earlier family and changes the outward bound to 9 m/start. If stopping is insufficient in either layout, use one driving step at lower intent for remaining attempts; stop if still uncontrolled. No extra trials.
- **E2:** Without a suitable seat or controlled seated takeoff, use **Paused Broad Jump to Stick instead**, **2 × 2**, comfortable dip held 2 s, hands on hips, no re-dip, modest distance and 2 s landing hold; same rests. This repeats Class 1's task.
- **E3:** If the single-leg pause is unstable, use **Paused Staggered-Stance Broad Jump to Two-Foot Stick instead**, two attempts per front-leg configuration, small offset, both feet pushing, 2 s pause/landing hold and the same rests. Related broad-jump family; do not label it a completed unilateral takeoff.
- **E4:** If the wall or posture cannot be qualified, use **Paused Squat Jump to Stick instead of wall pulses**, **1 × 4**, hands on hips, comfortable dip held 2 s, no re-dip, modest upward jump, 2 s bilateral landing hold and 20 s between reps. This repeats an earlier fallback family and adds four landings instead of six force pulses.
- **E5:** If no suitable wall is available, use **Supine Unresisted Knee Drive, opposite heel grounded, instead**: **1 × 3/leg**, quick lift, 1 s finish, 2 s lower, 10 s resets and 45 s between legs. Keep the other leg comfortably long with heel grounded and pelvis quiet. This repeats Class 3's unresisted fallback family with different body support.
- **E6:** If swing competence, bell or clearance is unsuitable, use **Bilateral Glute Bridge with rapid rise instead of dead-stop swing**, **1 × 6**, feet planted, quick hip rise, 1 s top, 2 s lower, 10 s between reps. Stop at a level pelvis without lumbar arch. This repeats Class 4's rapid bilateral bridge fallback; no added jump landings and no claim of equivalent resistance.

**Quality rules:** Failed attempts count as exposure. Adjust the next scheduled rep; persistent faults despite adjustment end the affected task. Pain, slipping, changed gait or lost body/implement control ends it immediately. Record actual substitutions, extra contacts, slowing steps, omitted work and reasons. No make-up attempts or extra exercise slots; incomplete delivery remains incomplete.

## 3. Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) — Exactly 2 Exercises

Easy effort, approximately **RPE 3–4/10**. Retain these small strengthening doses without pre-fatiguing the loaded work.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Short-Foot Drill** | **1 × 3 holds × 5 s per foot**, both feet supported. **5 s release between holds; 20 s between feet.** | Maintain heel and both forefoot bases as the working arch gently rises, supporting the foot repeatedly used for E1/E3. Keep toes long; reduce effort or use **seated foot doming instead of standing** for clawing/rolling. |
| 2 | **Side-Lying Hip Abduction** | **1 × 6 per side**, bodyweight; **2 s up / 1 s hold / 2 s down**. **20 s between sides.** | Give the lateral hip a small strengthening dose for holding pelvic position over one support leg as the other moves. Bottom knee bent, top leg aligned with torso, toes forward; reduce range if the pelvis rolls or the thigh drifts forward. |

Rest **45 s between exercises and 60 s after S2** before P1 preparation. Stop for pain or persistent compensation; do not add resistance to create a burn.

## 4. Strength (Primary) — Exactly 6 Exercises

Use challenging loads/leverage leaving approximately **2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve (RIR)**. Keep Class 6's working doses and preparation rules. Actual prior loads are unknown: qualify today's load rather than assuming an increase or a previously completed set. No forced reps, maximal tests or automatic restoration of reduced volume.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides** | **1 × 5 per leg**, 2–3 RIR; **2 s down**, strong controlled ascent. **60 s between legs.** | Retain loaded lead-leg extension from a stable base for the seat-to-stance push and unilateral projection. Both feet stay on the floor; modest whole-trunk inclination without rounding. Reduce load/depth for knee collapse, pelvic rotation or rear-leg hopping. The reduced single round limits overlap with starts and horizontal jumps. |
| 2 | **Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells** | **1 × 6**, 2–3 RIR; **2 s down**, strong controlled ascent. | Retain hip-extension strength through a flexed-hip range, complementing E6’s brief rapid hinge with a controlled loaded range. Soft knees, bells close; stop depth before spine/pelvic compensation. Reduce range/load as needed. |
| 3 | **Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion** | **1 × 6 per leg**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s lift / 1 s hold / 2 s lower**. **45 s between legs.** | Strengthen the thigh lift used for free-leg recovery in E1/E5. Secure a DB on the distal thigh above the knee with both hands; lift the knee a few centimetres without hand assistance or backward lean. Start on a fitted stable seat with foot supported and knee near a right angle. Reduce load/range for pinching, tipping or a shifting implement. |
| 4 | **Glute Bridge Walkout** | **1 × 3 complete cycles**, approximately 2–3 clean cycles in reserve. One cycle = **4 small alternating heel steps out + 4 back**, about **8–10 s**. | Strengthen knee-flexor support as the knee opens/returns, supporting the takeoff/receiving legs alongside the hip hinge. Keep the pelvis raised, knees soft at the far endpoint and return to the original heel positions. Shorten steps for sag/cramp; stop if control cannot be restored. This is capacity work, not high-speed swing simulation. |
| 5 | **Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, floor range** | **1 × 10**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower**. | Retain near-straight-knee plantarflexion force as the driving leg lengthens during E1's push and forward takeoff. DBs at sides, both forefeet loaded, heels return to floor. Reduce load for lost heel height, outward roll or bounce; do not lock the knees forcibly. |
| 6 | **Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, bilateral DB loading** | **2 × 8**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower / 1 s bottom**. **90 s between sets.** | Maintain ankle-force capacity with the knee bent for the seated/paused push before leg extension, complementing P5. Secure weights on thighs above the knees; forefeet stay down and heel range stays repeatable. Reduce load for knee straightening, rolling or bounce. |

**Load-preparation sets, separate from working sets:** P1 **1 × 4/leg** bodyweight/light (30 s between sides, 60 s before work); P2 **1 × 5 easy then 1 × 3 moderate** (60 s between, 90 s before work); P3 **1 × 3/leg light** (30 s between, 45 s before work); P4 **1 short-lever cycle** (45 s before work); P5 **1 × 5 easy** (45 s before work); P6 **1 × 5 easy** (60 s before work). Additional small ramps, if needed, stay within the listed movement and are logged; no additional preparation sequence is invented.

**Between primary exercises:** **120 s after P1/P2; 90 s after P3/P4/P5**, before the next preparation set. Setup may occupy recovery; no extra required rest after final P6. If P5 balance limits productive loading, use **supported Single-Leg Calf Raise instead of bilateral P5**, **1 × 6/leg**, same tempo/RIR, 30 s between legs; preparation **1 × 3/leg easy**, 20 s between, 45 s before work. Verify stable hand support and log laterality. A fitted stable box may replace the bench for P3/P6.

**Timing and recovery:** Allow **76–86 minutes after Access & Prepare 1** with prompt individual equipment access: about 37 min explosive work, 5–6 min light strengthening and 33 min primary work, including teaching, rests, preparation and transitions. Extra setup, ramps, queues or recovery can extend this. Preparation duration, booking, group and staffing are unknown; full-session time is unresolved. A 60-minute complete booking cannot fit this version. Review actual sport, sprinting, other gym/classes and separate tumbling before scheduling. Nonconsecutive demanding lower-body exposures, often roughly 48–72 hours apart, are only a planning starting point; actual response and the wider schedule govern.

**Progression note:** Seated support and a paused unilateral takeoff change how forward force is initiated. Brief wall pulses add a rapid-force-onset task without a landing; the same-leg wall drive adds free-thigh recovery. Dead-stop swings recur deliberately because their existing initiation job is useful and another loaded hinge would add complexity without a clearer benefit. All strength doses hold. No heavier load, greater distance or earned tolerance is inferred. Class 8 should consider another useful start facing/stance only after reviewing actual needs and response; no later workout is written now.

**Audit summary:** Exact 6/2/6 and original framework retained. Defaults: **4 seated starts; 4 seated broad jumps; 4 paused unilateral-takeoff/bilateral-landing jumps; 6 one-second wall-force pulses; 6 wall knee drives/controlled foot returns; 6 parked-single swings**. Jump subtotal **8 bilateral landing events / 16 landing foot impacts**; start/slowing contacts are separate. Primary work remains **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 54 dynamic reps plus 3 walkout cycles**. The seat consumes lane space, and explicit fallback geometry is documented. # Sprinting — Class 3 of 12

**Primary effort:** Direct each leg's push into forward projection and transfer to the next support without pelvic rotation or reaching. Pair that work with rapid free-leg recovery and targeted strength.

**Baseline and review:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting and landing technique, under qualified coaching. The saved Classes 1–2, map, ledger, drill history, audits, equipment assumptions and available feedback were reviewed. **No actual completion or recovery observations are reported.** This is a conditional prescription, not evidence that the athletes earned greater intensity. The six default explosive tasks differ from earlier defaults; familiar strength lifts continue with less overlapping hinge/walkout work.

**Framework:** `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. This class uses straight-line starts and supplemental gym work. It does **not** contain actual maximum-velocity running or establish a top-speed result.

**Quality marker within E1:** For each scheduled start, record front leg/grounded hand, whether hand release and leg drive produce a direct forward launch, any backward rock or rotation, whether the opening steps reach conspicuously ahead, and stopping control. Log attempted/valid starts and specific faults; no extra trials. A three-point start has its own record and is not numerically comparable to standing or half-kneeling starts.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload remain unknown here. Use actual preparation and readiness to decide whether the athlete is ready for the listed tasks; no replacement preparation is created.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

E1 is the primary performance task. Complete the exercises in order, with quick, clean intent and modest supporting doses. Rapid force expression does not require every exercise to include flight.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Three-Point Start Acceleration — first two steps** | **2 × 2 starts**, one with each front leg per pair. Two driving foot strikes or **3 m**, whichever comes first, then progressively slow and stop by **9 m**. **75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.** | **Main launch task:** coordinate release of hand support with the legs' forward push. Use staggered feet and the hand opposite the front leg on the floor; choose comfortable spacing that allows both feet to push without a cramped crouch. Hold still briefly, then release and drive without twisting. First pair uses controlled fast intent to establish stopping; second pair uses the fastest clean intent that preserves it. No blocks or maximal-load test. |
| 2 | **Rapid Step-Up to Knee Drive — no flight** | **1 × 3 per working leg**, bodyweight; rapid rise, **1 s tall finish, 2 s controlled lower**. **10 s reset between reps; 45 s between legs.** | Make the elevated leg supply most of the upward push while the other thigh recovers. Whole working foot on a stable low box; front knee below hip level at the start. Rise quickly without bouncing off the floor leg, hopping off the box or lifting the working heel. The free knee rises naturally as the body comes up; return that foot gently to the floor, keeping the working foot on the box. Lower the box height for pelvic hitching or loss of forceful ascent. |
| 3 | **Forward Bound to Opposite-Leg Stick** | **1 × 2 per takeoff leg**; modest distance, natural arms. **20 s between same-takeoff reps; 45 s between legs.** | Transfer a forward push from one leg into controlled support on the other, rather than receiving every projection on two feet. From one-leg support, use a small dip, bound forward and hold the opposite-leg landing **2 s** before setting the free foot down. Keep the pelvis facing forward; shorten distance for reaching, trunk rotation or an unstable receiver. No linked bounds. |
| 4 | **Broad Jump to Stick — countermovement and arm swing** | **2 × 2**; natural arms, one smooth dip and immediate forward jump. **20 s between reps; 90 s between sets.** | Integrate arm action and a dynamic leg drive into horizontal projection. This differs from Class 1's paused, hands-on-hips jump: there is no held squat or deliberate interruption of the dip. Land on both feet and hold **2 s**; select a distance that permits control rather than chasing a record. |
| 5 | **Standing Single-Leg Cycle and Strike** | **1 × 3 cycles per moving leg**. One compact recovery cycle followed by a quick target-foot strike; **10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs**. | Rehearse returning the free foot beneath the pelvis while the other leg provides stable support. Keep the support foot planted. Recover the moving heel beneath the hip, bring the thigh forward through a comfortable range, let the lower leg unfold without kicking, then place the foot quickly beside the support foot. No running travel or hopping on the support leg. Reduce cycle height/range for leaning, a long backswing or an ahead-of-body strike. A rep is one complete recovery-and-strike cycle. |
| 6 | **Supine Banded Knee Drive — opposite heel grounded** | **1 × 3 per moving leg**, very light band. **Quick knee drive, 1 s finish, 2 s controlled lower**; **10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs**. | Express rapid thigh recovery against light elastic resistance while the pelvis is supported, complementing E5's placement task. Lie with both legs comfortably long and heels on the floor, a suitable closed band around both shoe midfeet. Keep the nonmoving leg long, heel grounded and foot secure; quickly bend/lift the moving knee toward the torso as the band stretches, then lower under control. Stop the lift before pelvic movement or the band's stretch limit. The grounded heel must not slide or lift. The band must oppose the knee drive, not assist it; do not start with the opposite thigh raised. Use lighter resistance/shorter range for a slowed drive, rolling band or loss of pelvic control. |

**Recovery between exercises:** **90 s after E1–E4; 60 s after E5–E6**, including the transition to S1. Resets are recovery, not extra isometric holds. Instruction/setup may occupy these intervals; count actual elapsed time once. Extend recovery if force, focus or movement quality has not returned.

**Space and equipment:** Use one protected **10 m lane** for starts: start at 0 m, driving ends by 3 m, progressively stop by 9 m, leave the final metre clear. One athlete moves at a time; close the lane during the walking return and verify separate coach/waiting positions. The footprint does not prove an individual can stop within it. E3/E4 use a modest selected landing distance within a clear 3 m area with further empty space beyond; no approaching run. E2/E5/E6 are stationary. Boxes, benches and bands are listed equipment, but low-box height, closed-loop band type/length, surface, quantities and clearances are not confirmed. No wall, band anchor, sled, rack, throw or long running lane is required by the defaults.

**Replacements and regressions — use instead of, never in addition:**

- **E1:** If hand support is uncomfortable or the stance cannot be controlled, use **Two-Point Standing Start instead of Three-Point Start**, same four starts and boundaries. This deliberately reuses an earlier family for readiness. If stopping space is insufficient, use one driving step at lower intent for remaining attempts; stop if that still fails. Do not add attempts.
- **E2:** If no suitably low stable box is available, use **Split Squat Jump to Stick, same lead, instead of Rapid Step-Up**, **1 × 2 per lead leg**, bodyweight, modest height, two-second finish, 20 s between same-lead reps and 45 s between leads. This repeats Class 2's task for equipment feasibility and adds four split-stance jump landings in place of six nonflight rises. No unstable stacked plates or improvised platform.
- **E3:** If opposite-leg reception is not qualified, use **Single-Leg Broad Jump to Two-foot Landing instead of the opposite-leg bound**, same 1 × 2/takeoff leg and rests, shorter controlled distance. This repeats Class 1's reception option; record the changed landing type. Do not demand a one-leg finish to preserve novelty.
- **E6:** Use only an intact closed band suitable for the foot-loop setup and within its stated stretch limit; do not tie an improvised loop or use an unverified external anchor. If no suitable band is available, use **Unresisted Supine Knee Drive instead of the banded version**, same count, controlled lowering, rapid drive and rests. Its resistance is different and must be logged; no claim of equal force demand.

**Quality rules:** Attempted work counts even when faulty. Cue or reduce demand before the next scheduled rep; repeated loss of the same criterion despite adjustment ends that exercise. Pain, a slip, changed gait, an insecure band or loss of control ends the affected task immediately. Log omitted work and actual substitutions; do not add make-up reps or other exercises. If an athlete cannot perform a default or its stated replacement productively, actual delivery is incomplete rather than falsely recorded as fourteen finished entries.

## 3. Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) — Exactly 2 Exercises

Easy effort, approximately **RPE 3–4/10**. These retained bodyweight strengthening doses support the foot base and lateral hip without tiring the athlete before the primary lifts.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Short-Foot Drill** | **1 × 3 holds × 5 s per foot**, both feet supported. **5 s release between holds; 20 s between feet.** | Maintain heel and both forefoot bases while gently raising the working arch, supporting the foot used to push and the opposite foot receiving the bound. Keep toes long; reduce effort or use **seated foot doming instead of standing** for clawing or rolling. |
| 2 | **Side-Lying Hip Abduction** | **1 × 6 per side**, bodyweight; **2 s up / 1 s hold / 2 s down**. **20 s between sides.** | Give the lateral hip a small strengthening dose for keeping the pelvis level/directed forward during step-up, bound reception and the planted-leg cycle. Bottom knee bent, top leg aligned with torso, toes forward; reduce range if the pelvis rolls or the thigh moves forward. |

Rest **45 s between exercises and 60 s after S2** before P1 preparation. Stop for pain or persistent compensation; do not increase resistance to create a burn.

## 4. Strength (Primary) — Exactly 6 Exercises

Select a challenging load or leverage leaving approximately **2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve (RIR)**. A prior prescribed weight is not known: qualify today's load rather than assuming any earlier set was performed. No forced repetitions, maximal tests or automatic load increase. P2 drops from two working sets to one and P4 from four cycles to three to limit overlap with new leg-specific work; the other prescriptions stay consistent.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides** | **2 × 5 per leg**, 2–3 RIR; **2 s down**, strong controlled ascent. **60 s between legs; 120 s between rounds.** | **Main strength anchor:** load lead-leg knee/hip extension in a split base while preserving pelvis direction. Both feet remain on the floor; modest whole-trunk inclination without rounding. Reduce depth/load for knee collapse, rotation or rear-leg hopping. |
| 2 | **Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells** | **1 × 6**, 2–3 RIR; **2 s down**, controlled strong ascent. | Retain challenging hip-extension strength from flexed hips, with one working set because forward bounds and rapid step-ups already add new posterior-chain work. Soft knees, bells close; stop depth before pelvis/spine compensation. Reduce range/load if needed. |
| 3 | **Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion** | **1 × 6 per leg**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s lift / 1 s hold / 2 s lower**. **45 s between legs.** | Build force for lifting the thigh through a stable seated range, complementary to E6's light rapid drive from a longer-leg starting position. Secure a DB across the distal thigh above the knee with both hands; lift the knee a few centimetres without hand assistance or leaning, then return the foot gently. Use a stable fitted seat with foot supported and knee initially near a right angle. Reduce load/range for pinching, tipping or shifting load. |
| 4 | **Glute Bridge Walkout** | **1 × 3 complete cycles**, approximately **2–3 clean cycles in reserve**. One cycle = **4 small alternating heel steps out + 4 back**, about **8–10 s**. | Retain knee-flexor support as the knee opens/returns while reducing the total lever-loading dose. Keep pelvis raised and knees soft at the far endpoint; return to original heel positions. Shorten steps for sag/cramp; do not lengthen them just to compensate for the lower rep count. Stop if control cannot be restored. |
| 5 | **Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, floor range** | **1 × 10**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower**. | Strengthen straight-knee plantarflexion for the pushing/receiving foot without adding rebound contacts. DBs at sides, both forefeet loaded, heels return to floor; reduce load for lost height, outward roll or bouncing. Knees stay nearly straight, not forcibly locked. |
| 6 | **Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, bilateral DB loading** | **2 × 8**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower / 1 s bottom**. **90 s between sets.** | Retain plantarflexion force with the knees bent for initial support and the low launch, complementing P5's knee position. # Sprinting — Class 2 of 12

**Primary effort:** Push out of a low start position while recovering the opposite thigh, keeping the pelvis directed into the lane. Support that push with rapid leg extension, then a small dose of upright ankle support and compact foot recovery.

**Baseline and review:** Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting and landing technique under qualified coaching. Class 1, its workload, drill history, assumptions and feedback record were reviewed. **Class 1 execution and response remain unknown.** Class 2 is a conditional new prescription, not an earned load increase. All six default explosive drills differ meaningfully from Class 1; the eight strengthening exercises retain useful roles and doses.

**Framework:** `Sprinting > Acceleration (straight-line and multidirectional)` and `Sprinting > Maximum velocity`. Today uses a straight-line start application. Upright work is supplemental gym practice; this session does **not** include actual maximum-velocity running.

**Quality marker within E1:** For each scheduled start, note whether the athlete leaves the low position without rocking backward, folding at the waist, twisting away from the lead leg or taking a separate upright step before driving forward. Record controlled stopping separately. Log lead leg, attempted/valid starts and specific faults. This task establishes its own observation record; do not compare its score or distance directly with Class 1's standing start. No extra trials.

## 1. Access & Prepare 1

Complete the **existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1**, unchanged and supplied separately. Its contents, duration and workload are not supplied here. The coach checks actual readiness for the listed efforts; this document creates no preparation sequence.

## 2. Explosiveness — Exactly 6 Exercises

Perform in order. E1 is the main performance task. All six drills use rapid intent, with amplitude and speed constrained by clean execution; no effort is a conditioning interval.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Half-Kneeling Sprint Start — first two steps** | **2 × 2 starts**, one with each leg forward per pair. Drive for two foot strikes or to **3 m**, whichever comes first; progressively slow and stop by **9 m**. **75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.** | **Main low-start task:** create forward motion from a flexed lead hip/knee while bringing the rear thigh through. Front foot flat, rear knee comfortably supported on the floor and rear toes tucked; establish a modest forward torso lean without rounding, pause briefly, then push into the lane. Both legs may contribute; this is not a test of isolated lead-leg force. First pair uses controlled fast intent to establish the route; second pair uses the fastest clean intent that preserves stopping control. |
| 2 | **Wall Drill Fast Switch — isolated single exchanges** | **2 × 4 total alternating switches** = 2/leg/set, **8 switches total**. After each rapid exchange, hold the new position **2 s**; reset **10 s between switches**, **60 s between sets**. | Rehearse rapid reciprocal thigh action while external support constrains the forward-leaning body line. Hands on a **verified solid wall**, feet far enough back for a comfortable whole-body lean; one thigh forward, stance leg long but not locked. Exchange legs quickly, placing the new stance foot beneath the hip line without stamping or folding. Reduce knee height/lean for pelvic rotation or heavy contact. |
| 3 | **Seated Vertical Jump to Floor Landing** | **2 × 2**, bodyweight, natural arms. Settle **2 s** on a stable, fitted bench/box with feet flat; jump without a backward rock. **20 s between reps; 90 s between sets.** | Express rapid knee/hip extension after supported sitting, reducing the contribution of a preceding dip. This supplies a bilateral force-production task from flexed legs, separate from the traveling start and split-stance jump. Sit near the edge, torso already inclined over the feet; jump mainly upward and only enough forward to clear the support. Land on both feet and hold **2 s**. Reduce height for a noisy/unstable finish. |
| 4 | **Split Squat Jump to Stick — keep the same lead leg** | **1 × 2 per lead leg**; bodyweight, shallow dip and modest height. **20 s between same-lead reps; 45 s before changing lead.** | Express rapid extension from an asymmetric base without asking the athlete to alternate legs in flight. Both feet leave the floor and return to their original split relationship; finish with controlled weight through both feet for **2 s**. Stay aligned into the lane; reduce depth/height for scissoring, twisting or rear-foot collapse. This is one jump at a time, not continuous jumping lunges. |
| 5 | **Single-Leg Pogo — low amplitude, final same-leg hold** | **1 × 3 hops per leg**, **45 s between legs**. Two quick rebounds, then hold the third same-leg landing **2 s** before gently setting the other foot down. | Introduce a very small repeated same-leg ankle-support demand, closer to unilateral support than Class 1's bilateral pogo. Stay tall, free foot clear, minimal knee dip; prioritize controlled recoil over height. Lower amplitude or use the replacement below if the athlete cannot keep the pelvis/foot organized. |
| 6 | **Stationary Low Dribble Run** | **2 × 6 alternating foot strikes** = 3/foot/set, **12 fast contacts total**; approximately 3–4 s per set. **60 s between sets.** | Coordinate compact ankle-to-low-shin foot recovery with brief alternating upright contacts. Make small circular foot paths and place each foot close beneath the pelvis; relaxed opposite-arm action, no high-knee lift or forward reaching. This uses running exchanges rather than A-skip step-hop pairs. Slow cadence/shorten the cycle if posture or placement degrades; end the bout rather than extending it. |

**Switch reset:** After E2's two-second position hold, step out of the wall lean for the ten-second reset; resume from that ending leg position for the next alternating exchange. The floor replacement rests the knees during resets. Do not turn the resets into prolonged isometric work.

**Between exercises:** Allow **90 s after E1, E2, E3 and E4**, then **60 s after E5 and E6** before the next task (including the transition to S1). Instruction and setup may occupy these intervals; count elapsed time once. Extend recovery when breathing, focus or movement quality has not recovered.

**Start and station layout:** Use one protected **10 m lane**: 0 m start, driving ends by 3 m, progressively slow to a stop by 9 m, last metre clear as reserve. These boundaries do not establish that every athlete can stop there. One athlete moves; keep the lane closed during the walking return and verify waiting/coach positions outside it. No joined lanes, hard stop at 3 m, long acceleration or flying sprint. E3/E4 use a cleared floor area with room around the landing, clear of bench edges and waiting athletes. E5/E6 are stationary. Do not place the wall station or equipment inside the active start/run-off path.

**One-for-one replacements and regressions:**

- **E1:** If the first prescribed attempts show insufficient stopping control, use **one driving step instead of two** for remaining attempts at lower intent; stop the task if control still fails. If kneeling is uncomfortable, **use a low two-point standing start instead of the half-kneeling start**, same 2 × 2 schedule and boundaries. This is an explicitly justified recurrence of the Class 1 start family, not a claim of a unique drill; record the substitution and do not add starts.
- **E2:** A suitable wall is **not confirmed by the inventory**. If unavailable, **use High-Plank Single-Switch Knee Drive instead of Wall Drill Fast Switch**, same 2 × 4 exchanges, two-second holds, ten-second resets and sixty-second set rest. Hands on the floor below shoulders, one knee drawn forward with foot hovering and the other leg extended on its toes; rapidly exchange legs and place only the new rear foot down. Keep the trunk still; briefly rest the knees during resets. This retains rapid hip exchange with trunk control but changes support and is not equivalent to inclined sprint stance. End for wrist/shoulder discomfort or loss of trunk control.
- **E3:** Choose a stable seat height permitting flat feet and knees near a right angle. If no suitable seat exists, **use Squat Jump to Stick instead of Seated Vertical Jump**, 2 × 2, two-second standing squat pause, natural arms, no re-dip, same rests and two-foot finish. This removes seat support; log the change. Do not improvise unstable stacked seats or add a hurdle.
- **E5:** If repeated same-leg contacts are not qualified, **use Ankle Pogo in Place instead of Single-Leg Pogo**, **1 × 6 low bilateral hops**, holding the last landing two seconds. This is an intentional recurrence of Class 1's drill family for readiness, not novelty. The nominal landing-event count remains six but laterality changes.

**Stop rules:** Every attempted jump/contact/start counts as actual exposure, including faulty attempts. Cue or reduce demand before the next scheduled rep; repeated loss of the same criterion despite adjustment ends that exercise. Stop the affected task immediately for pain, a slip, changed gait or lost control. Do not add make-up attempts or fill omitted work with unlisted exercises. If a default or its documented replacement cannot be performed productively, record incomplete actual work.

## 3. Strength (Stabilization/Resilience) — Exactly 2 Exercises

Keep effort easy, approximately **RPE 3–4/10**, well short of fatigue. These familiar strengthening tasks support the day's asymmetric push and unilateral ankle work without increasing pre-lift fatigue.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Short-Foot Drill** | **1 × 3 holds × 5 s per foot**. Both feet supported; **5 s release between holds, 20 s between feet**. | Control the working foot's arch while keeping heel and both forefoot bases supported, providing a stable base for start and pogo force. Keep toes long; reduce effort or **use seated foot doming instead of standing** for toe clawing or rolling. |
| 2 | **Side-Lying Hip Abduction** | **1 × 6 per side**, bodyweight; **2 s up / 1 s hold / 2 s down**. **20 s between sides.** | Give the lateral hip a small strengthening dose for keeping the pelvis directed forward over the support leg. Bottom knee bent, top leg in line with torso, toes forward; lift only while the pelvis stays stacked. Reduce range for rolling or thigh drift. |

Allow **45 s between exercises and 60 s after S2** before P1 preparation sets. No burn, grinding or testing to fatigue; stop for pain or persistent compensation.

## 4. Strength (Primary) — Exactly 6 Exercises

Keep Class 1's **working-set prescriptions**, not an assumed previously used weight. Qualify today's load or leverage to leave approximately **2–3 technically sound reps in reserve (RIR)**. Missing feedback authorizes no automatic increase in load, range or sets. No maximal tests or forced reps.

| # | Exercise | Sets × reps | Specific job in this workout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides** | **2 × 5 per leg**, 2–3 RIR; **2 s down**, strong ascent. **60 s between legs; 120 s between rounds.** | **Main strength anchor:** load lead-leg knee/hip extension from the split base used to leave the low start. Both feet stay on the floor; a modest whole-trunk forward inclination is allowed without rounding. Reduce load/depth for pelvic rotation, knee collapse or rear-leg hopping. |
| 2 | **Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells** | **2 × 6**, 2–3 RIR; **2 s down**, controlled strong ascent. **120 s between sets.** | Strengthen hip extension with flexed hips and lengthened hamstrings, complementing P1's knee-extension contribution to the start. Soft knees, bells close; stop depth before pelvic/spinal compensation. Reduce range/load when needed. |
| 3 | **Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion** | **1 × 6 per leg**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s lift / 1 s hold / 2 s lower**. **45 s between legs.** | Load the thigh-recovery action rehearsed rapidly in E1/E2 while removing the need to balance. Sit near a stable bench edge, foot supported and knee near a right angle; secure a DB across the distal thigh above the knee with both hands. Lift the knee a few centimetres without pulling with the hands or leaning back; return the foot gently. Reduce load/range for tipping, pinching or implement movement. |
| 4 | **Glute Bridge Walkout** | **1 × 4 complete cycles**, **2–3 clean cycles in reserve**. Each cycle = **4 alternating small heel steps out + 4 back**, about **8–10 s**. | Load knee-flexor support while the knee opens and returns, supplementing the hip hinge rather than adding a third hip-extension lift. Keep the pelvis raised; walk only to a controlled soft-knee position, then return to the original heel marks. Choose step length for the reserve target; shorten for sagging or cramp, stop if unresolved. |
| 5 | **Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, floor range** | **1 × 10**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower**, heels return to floor. | Develop straight-knee ankle force capacity supporting push-off and the new unilateral rebound task. Hold DBs at sides, rise through both forefeet without outward roll, bounce or forced knee lock. Reduce load for lost heel height. |
| 6 | **Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, bilateral DB loading** | **2 × 8**, 2–3 RIR; **1 s rise / 1 s top / 2 s lower / 1 s bottom**. **90 s between sets.** | Load plantarflexion with flexed knees for the low start/support demand, complementing P5's knee position. Keep knees near a right angle, weights secured on thighs above the knees, forefeet planted and heel travel repeatable. Reduce load for knee straightening, foot roll or bouncing. |

**Load-preparation sets, separate from work:** P1 **1 × 4/leg** bodyweight/light, 30 s between sides and 60 s before work; P2 **1 × 5 easy then 1 × 3 moderate**, 60 s between and 90 s before work; P3 **1 × 3/leg light**, 30 s between and 45 s before work; P4 **1 short-lever cycle**, 45 s before work; P5 **1 × 5 easy**, 45 s before work; P6 **1 × 5 easy**, 60 s before work. Additional small ramps may be used only in listed movements when necessary to select a qualified load; record their work/time. These sets do not replace Access & Prepare 1.

**Rest between primary exercises:** **120 s after P1 and P2; 90 s after P3, P4 and P5**, before the next preparation set. Count equipment changes and instruction inside recovery where possible; no mandatory extra interval after final P6. If P5 balance prevents a challenging set, **use supported Single-Leg Calf Raise instead of bilateral P5**, **1 × 6/leg**, same tempo/RIR, 30 s between legs; preparation **1 × 3/leg easy**, 20 s between sides and 45 s before work. A stable hand support must be verified. Log changed laterality. A fitted stable box may replace the bench for P3/P6; neither seat dimensions nor DB weight ranges are confirmed.

**Timing and scheduling:** Budget **75–85 minutes after the existing preparation** for an athlete with prompt equipment access, including coaching/setup, resets, rests, ramps and transitions. Model: approximately 30 min explosive, 6 min light strength and 39 min primary strength. Group queues, extra teaching/ramps or recovery add time. Preparation duration and actual booking remain unknown: full-class time is unresolved; a 60-minute whole-class window does not fit this version. Do not shorten required recovery to force a timetable. Treat as demanding lower-body work; review actual sport, sprint, gym, other classes and separate tumbling. A nonconsecutive demanding exposure, often around 48–72 hours later, is only a planning starting point; readiness and the wider schedule decide.

**Progression note:** Four low starts replace six standing starts; no sprint distance increases. The new tasks isolate different start/support demands, not a claim that the athlete earned harder training. Single-leg pogo has only three landings per side. Strength doses remain unchanged while loads are qualified anew. Class 3 should refine leg-specific push contribution with distinct drills after reviewing actual response; retain useful strength measures. Compare a drill only with its own matched protocol, never with a different start or jump as an improvement test.

**Audit summary:** Exact 6/2/6 and seven-category mapping preserved. Default explosive workload is **4 starts, 14 jump/hop landings, 8 supported switch strikes and 12 low-dribble contacts**; no throws, swings or top-speed runs. Compared with Class 1, fewer landings do not make a same-leg rebound equivalent to a bilateral pogo or skip. The limited new same-leg dose, unchanged strength sets and full recovery address that uncertainty. Solid-wall availability, seat fit, lane width/clearance, athlete response, outside workload, staffing and full-class time remain conditional. See the [Class 2 audit](../supporting/class_02_audit.md), [ledger](../progression_ledger.md) and [drill history](../supporting/drill_history.md).
