# Sprinting — drill history and uniqueness review

**User preference added during Class 1 development:** “Try to force unique drills; while strength lifts may recur as needed for progressions.” Apply this across the curriculum's explosive drills. Relevance, room, athlete competence and meaningful dosage still govern selection.

Track written drill identity separately from actual execution. A different label, cue, side, load, set count or arbitrary obstacle arrangement does not establish a new drill. A useful distinction changes the start/task constraint or force-expression demand and earns a specific job. Do not fill the later curriculum in advance just to reserve unique names.

| First prescribed | Explosive drill | Distinct demand to preserve in the history | Actual use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Class 1 E1 | Two-point start — two-step projection | Static staggered standing start, two driving strikes within 3 m, early progressive slowing. | Unknown |
| Class 1 E2 | Paused Broad Jump to Stick, hands on hips | Static bilateral horizontal impulse, no countermovement or arm aid, bilateral finish. | Unknown |
| Class 1 E3 | Single-leg Broad Jump to Two-foot Landing | Unilateral horizontal impulse, natural dip/arms, bilateral reception. | Unknown |
| Class 1 E4 | Ankle Pogo in Place | Repeated low bilateral ankle recoil without travel. | Unknown |

**Listed contingencies, not confirmed performed:** E1 one-step start; E6 hands-on-hips Countermovement Jump to Stick. Keep these visible when assessing later novelty. A scheduled alternative becomes actual history only when reported used. Avoid advertising it as a brand-new concept merely because its earlier use is unknown.

**Next-class rule:** Review all previous prescribed and actually used drills; prefer a distinct performance task and complementary drills directly relevant to the day’s start or upright-support emphasis. Reuse a drill only when the alternatives are less defensible for the primary effort, available room or athlete readiness, and state that reason. Strength and light resilience exercises may recur for a traceable reason. Keep any new explosive drill at an appropriate entry demand; uniqueness is not progression evidence.

**Measurement rule:** Different start types/jump variants are separate tests. Preserve their own conditions for any future repeat and compare strength anchors only under matched conditions. Coach observations of a shared quality can guide decisions across drills, but do not report a numerical performance improvement from changing the drill.

# Class 3 — design and audit

**2026-09-13.** The previous run made progress by saving Class 2. This run verified current state references and the unchanged supplied specification, then reviewed Classes 1–2, the map, ledger, drill history, audits, source notes and feedback. Neither class is reported performed. Adjacent feedback status records also report no supplied observations. Only Class 3 is finalized in this run.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Express a leg-specific push while keeping the pelvis directed forward and organizing the next support/free-leg recovery.
2. **Demand:** Release a supported start into forward motion; separate the working leg's extension from trailing-leg assistance; accept a modest transfer on the opposite leg without reaching.
3. **Main task:** Four three-point starts under the existing 3 m driving/9 m stopping limits. Record hand/foot setup, forward launch and stopping during prescribed attempts.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Nonflight rapid step-up extension; opposite-leg bound reception; dynamic bilateral horizontal push; planted-leg foot recovery/strike; externally resisted rapid knee drive. Light foot/lateral-hip control precedes split-stance, hinge, hip-flexor, knee-flexor and two knee-angle ankle strengthening.
5. **Constraints:** Ages 12–14 baseline competence, no execution/recovery evidence, exact 6/2/6, distinct-drill preference, gym supplementation beyond starts, unconfirmed equipment dimensions and group clock. New tasks require qualified entry demands; no numerical comparison across different drills.

## Choice and revision findings

| Concern | Decision and reason |
|---|---|
| Three-point versus another start | One grounded hand adds a release/leg-drive coordination demand that neither standing two-point nor half-kneeling starts shares. Prone get-ups would add more upper-body movement; a falling start would shift the task toward catching forward momentum. Three-point best fits coordinated launch from support today. It does not isolate either leg or simulate blocks exactly. |
| Step-up flight | A launch from the box would add landing height and expose unknown platform dimensions. The chosen rapid nonflight step-up still requires high acceleration of body mass through the working leg, with a controlled return and six purposeful reps. It is not slow stabilization work mislabeled as power. |
| Opposite-leg bound | Changes the receiving task from Class 1's two-foot landing to controlled support on the opposite leg. It remains one short bound at a time, two per takeoff leg, with no rebound progression. Fewer landings do not prove lower joint/tendon stress; the two-foot fallback remains available. |
| Dynamic broad jump | The prior broad jump removed countermovement and arm contribution. Today's continuous dip/arm action has an integration job and is a substantive variant, consistent with the spec's paused-versus-dynamic distinction. It is not a renamed load/repetition change, and its distance cannot be treated as improvement over the paused variant. |
| Upright drill choice | A longer-lever traveling straight-leg bound/run was considered but adds travel/landing demands unnecessary to this day. A planted-leg cycle-and-strike isolates return/placement without a new runway or hopping sequence. It differs from low-dribble alternating running exchanges and wall-supported reciprocal switches. It is a constrained drill, not a complete stride at top speed. |
| Banded knee drive | The setup was revised so the nonmoving leg stays long with its heel on the floor: stretching the loop must oppose the target knee drive. Starting with the opposite thigh raised could instead assist the returning leg and would not serve the intended job. The final task combines a rapid drive and controlled lowering as one cycle, distinct from heavy seated hip flexion. If traction, loop fit or resistance direction cannot be secured, use the unresisted version and label it. |
| Posterior-chain overlap | Step-ups, forward bounds and broad jumps introduce leg-specific extension/receiving demands while actual readiness is unknown. Reduce RDL from **2 × 6 to 1 × 6** and walkout from **4 to 3 cycles**. Keep both sets challenging through qualified technique/reserve, not heavy fatigue. This is a programming allocation, not an assertion that athletes were fatigued. |
| Retained strength | P1 remains the main comparable strength prescription. P3 still addresses loaded thigh lift, P5/P6 ankle force with different knee positions. Light short-foot and abduction still address the foot base and pelvic direction. No unrelated pushing/pulling lifts are inserted. |
| Exact counts and uniqueness | Six default explosive tasks have real jobs; two have rapid force intent without flight. Eight strengthening exercises remain. Default drill distinctions are documented in history; equipment/readiness fallbacks explicitly reuse prior tasks when appropriate rather than manufacturing novelty. |
| Space and equipment | Default class needs a protected start/jump floor, suitable low box, DBs, fitted seated support and a suitable light closed band. No throwing area, rack, sled or wall is presumed. The current supplied 10 m footprint governs despite the separate 12 m note. Bound distance is modest and individualized, not a measured performance target. |

## Workload and recovery review

Class 2 prescribed four starts, fourteen jump/hop events, eight supported switch strikes and twelve low-dribble contacts. Class 3 prescribes four starts, **eight jump/bound events** (four bilateral, four unilateral), **six nonflight rapid rises**, **six target-foot cycle strikes**, and **six banded knee-drive cycles**. E2 adds six controlled trailing-foot floor returns. Initial/exit foot placements and start slowing steps are not inferred from these numbers. There is no equivalence score for different contacts.

Primary strengthening falls from **9 rounds/12 bouts/70 reps + 4 cycles** to **8 rounds/11 bouts/64 reps + 3 cycles**. Light work and load-preparation doses remain unchanged. No automatic load, lever or range increase accompanies the lower rep/set count. The reduction addresses overlapping tasks while preserving meaningful work in all six primary slots.

The main start remains first. Supporting drills have low rep counts and full resets; calf working volume remains three bouts with no added pogo block. Light resilience work stays easy. Conditioning, extra reaction work, extra testing and separate tumbling are absent. Any failed attempt still counts as actual exposure; stop conditions take precedence over completing the paper count.

## Timing model

Individual delivery with prompt equipment access is the planning assumption. Work/instruction durations are estimates, while rest intervals are prescribed. Instruction below is conservatively budgeted outside rest; when delivered within rest, count actual elapsed time once. Do not add both a queue interval and an identical recovery interval.

| Task | Work/instruction allowance | Recovery | Seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 4 × 10 s start/slowing + 120 s instruction | 2 × 75 s + 120 s | 430 |
| E2 | 6 × 4 s rise/hold/lower + 90 s setup/instruction | 4 × 10 s resets + 45 s side change | 199 |
| E3 | 4 × 5 s setup/bound/hold + 90 s instruction | 2 × 20 s + 45 s side change | 195 |
| E4 | 4 × 5 s dip/jump/hold + 60 s instruction | 2 × 20 s + 90 s set rest | 210 |
| E5 | 6 × 3 s cycles + 90 s instruction | 4 × 10 s resets + 45 s side change | 193 |
| E6 | 6 × 4 s knee-drive cycles + 90 s setup/instruction | 4 × 10 s resets + 45 s side change | 199 |
| E transitions | No extra work | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s, including to S1 | 480 |
| S1/S2 | Full prior light dose and teaching allowances retained | Releases, side changes, between-row and entry-to-P1 rest included | 330 |
| P1 | 24 s preparation + 60 s work + 90 s instruction | 30 + 60 s preparation; 2 × 60 + 120 s work rest | 504 |
| P2 | 24 s preparation + 18 s work + 90 s instruction | 60 + 90 s preparation; no second working set | 282 |
| P3 | 24 s preparation + 48 s work + 75 s instruction | 30 + 45 s preparation; 45 s work-side rest | 267 |
| P4 | 10 s preparation + 30 s work + 60 s instruction | 45 s | 145 |
| P5 | 20 s preparation + 40 s work + 60 s instruction | 45 s | 165 |
| P6 | 25 s preparation + 80 s work + 75 s instruction | 60 + 90 s | 330 |
| P transitions | No extra work | 2 × 120 s + 3 × 90 s | 510 |

**Totals:** E **1,906 s / 31.77 min**; S **330 s / 5.50 min**; P **2,203 s / 36.72 min**; total **4,439 s / 73.98 min**. Use **74–84 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1** as the nominal planning range. Extra teaching/ramps, equipment queues or longer recovery add time. The supported unilateral P5 replacement adds about one minute; other replacements change the actual flow and should be timed as used.

The actual class size, staff, preparation duration, booking and device capabilities remain unknown. A sixty-minute whole-session booking conflicts with this version; ninety minutes is not automatically enough. If a real window is supplied, revise the dose/flow together with meaningful slots and proper recovery intact.

**Group delivery:** One active start, no cross-traffic, and the lane closed during each walking return. A hypothetical three-athlete rotation at thirty-second dispatches gives roughly eighty seconds after a ten-second start/slowing task before that athlete's next turn; hold its next pair until at least 120 seconds after the prior finish. This requires all setup, return and feedback to fit; extend dispatch spacing if they do not. A single coach must not be assumed able to supervise a start and a new bound/step-up simultaneously. Box/DB/seat sharing and load adjustment determine the actual strength queue; three lanes are not three confirmed staffed stations.

## Acceptance and handoff

- Correct next class and reviewed prior files verified; observed work remains unknown.
- Original seven-category framework preserved in curriculum; exact Sprinting subcategory mapping used.
- Existing Access & Prepare 1 referenced without authored contents/time.
- Four ordered sections and fourteen meaningful entries: six explosive, two light, six primary. Alternatives are replacements, not extras.
- Per-side doses, preparation/work separation, load/intent, rest, quality and stop/regress criteria supplied.
- New task demands, contact types, hip/hamstring overlap, equipment replacements and realistic time audited; RDL/walkout dosage revised before finalizing.
- No athlete outcomes, earned progressions, numerical cross-drill comparisons or top-speed running claims.
- Save Class 3 and update map, ledger, history, feedback/state, source notes and verification. Only the next class's intended job is recorded.

**Next job:** Class 4 shifts emphasis toward upright posture and foot placement beneath the body, while keeping useful leg-force strength anchors. Select distinct drills only after reviewing all three classes and any actual response, including bound reception and step-up/hip-cycle control. Do not infer any class was performed.

# Sprinting Class 2 — design, progression and delivery audit

**Checkpoint:** 2026-09-13. Class 1 is a saved prescription, not confirmed completed work. Its files and state references exist; the specification snapshot matches the supplied original. The preceding goal turn made concrete progress by saving Class 1 and its records. This run advances one class only.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Performance result:** Initiate a forward start from a low position without an unnecessary upright detour or pelvic rotation, recovering the opposite thigh into the opening steps.
2. **Movement demand:** Coordinate force from a flexed lead leg with the free thigh and trunk; retain ankle support as the action becomes upright in supplemental drills.
3. **Primary task:** Four half-kneeling starts, paired by lead leg, within the existing 3 m driving/9 m stopping footprint. Observe launch alignment and stopping during the prescribed attempts.
4. **Required supporting jobs:** Inclined reciprocal thigh exchange; supported-sitting leg extension; split-base rapid extension; a small unilateral ankle recoil dose; compact upright running exchanges. Then light foot/hip control and familiar split-stance, hinge, hip-flexor, knee-flexor and two knee-angle ankle strengthening.
5. **Constraints:** 12–14 baseline competence, no actual performance/recovery feedback, unique-drill preference, exact 6/2/6, 10 m lane interpretation, no maximum-speed runway, unconfirmed wall/seat/group/booking. Every new task gets a conditional entry dose; novelty supplies no readiness evidence.

## Review, comparisons and revisions

| Decision | Alternatives considered and audit result |
|---|---|
| Half-kneeling main start | The preceding standing start addressed a higher static stagger. A low kneeling origin changes starting support and hip/knee position and makes standing-up-before-driving observable. A falling start would prioritize accepting a moving body; a prone start would add a substantial hand-release/get-up task. Half-kneeling better matches today's flexed-leg push/recovery job. This is not a block-start or isolated-leg force test. |
| Four starts, not six | Novel origin plus unknown feedback justifies reducing attempts from six to four, retaining paired lead-leg opportunities and full rest. Distance is unchanged; first pair establishes stopping feasibility. Quality feedback comes within these attempts, not extra testing. |
| Wall switch | Its external support constrains whole-body travel and helps isolate reciprocal thigh action in an inclined position. This is materially different from Class 1's upright skipping, whose step-hop rhythm remains absent here. A solid wall is unconfirmed, so the class supplies a floor-supported rapid-exchange replacement with its different support limitation stated. |
| Seated vertical jump | Supported sitting to leg extension differs from Class 1's standing static horizontal jump. An external seat reduces the role of an immediate dip, but does not justify claiming all elastic contributions disappear. No target box or hurdle is added; floor landing avoids a height contest and extra descent impacts. It is a small bilateral support task for force from flexed legs, not the main sprint drill. |
| Split-base jump | Both feet take off and return to the same split relationship. Its asymmetric extension/receiving base differs from Class 1's single-leg horizontal takeoff to bilateral parallel landing. Alternating scissor jumps would introduce a midair leg-switch task that is unnecessary for today's push; the default does not use them. |
| Unilateral pogo | A same-leg repeat is a real support-demand change, not renamed bilateral pogo. Initial consideration of four hops/leg was reduced to **three/leg** because response is unknown and direct calf lifts remain. No numerical contact-equivalence argument is used. Bilateral recurrence is explicitly available if readiness requires it. |
| Low dribble | Alternating running contacts with a low circular recovery are distinct from A-skip step-hop pairs. Stationary execution fits the gym and is logged as an authored adaptation, not bound to the traveling library card. The six-contact bouts prevent drift into endurance work. |
| All eight strengthening tasks retained | Their jobs still directly match the low start, thigh recovery and ankle support, and the explosive tasks already change. Prescribed dose/tempo/implements remain stable so actual load/RIR can become comparable when reported. Retention is not evidence that earlier loads were used, nor an instruction to increase them. |
| Hip/hamstring overlap | P1 and P2 already supply two challenging compound patterns. P3 addresses the opposite action (thigh lift), P4 adds knee-flexor support through changing knee angle. One walkout set prevents turning the posterior-chain support slot into another full hinge workout. |
| Calf overlap | Starts, wall switches, pogo and dribble all load foot/ankle tissues differently. Keep only three calf working bouts, preserve low rebound amplitude and do not add contacts to fill recovered time. Lower event counts alone do not prove lower tissue stress. |
| Recovery and chronology | Main task first; isolated/static leg-force tasks precede the upright contact doses; light strengthening remains easy before loaded work. Rest is kept despite a reduced main-start count. Every row has a stop/regress condition. |
| User preference | Six default drills differ from Class 1 by origin, support, direction or cyclic pattern, not just load/name. Explicit readiness/equipment fallbacks may recur. Record that truth instead of presenting a fallback as unique. Strength recurrence follows the user's stated exception. |

## Prescription comparison

| Exposure | Class 1 written | Class 2 written | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starts | 6 standing starts; up to 12 driving strikes / 18 m drive / 54 m outward path | 4 half-kneeling starts; up to 8 driving strikes / 12 m drive / 36 m outward path | New origin, lower opportunity count, same distance boundary. No direct score comparison. |
| Jump/hop landings | 24: 18 bilateral, 6 unilateral | 14: 8 bilateral, 6 unilateral | Same unilateral event count does not equate skip landings and repeated same-leg ankle rebounds. |
| Other drill contacts | 6 skip transfers | 8 supported switch strikes + 12 low-dribble contacts | Types remain separate; no combined stress index. Start slowing steps still unknown. |
| Other ballistics | 10 KB swings | None | Supported/stance-specific jump tasks replace this hip-hinge ballistic exposure. |
| Light strengthening | 2 rounds / 4 bouts; 12 reps + 30 foot-seconds | Same | Easy control work retained. |
| Primary strengthening | 9 rounds / 12 bouts; 70 reps + 4 walkout cycles | Same | Hold prescription; qualify actual load each session. |
| Preparation sets | 7 rounds / 9 bouts; 32 reps + 1 walkout cycle | Same | Distinct from working sets and unknown Access & Prepare 1. |

Actual cumulative exposure is unknown. These columns compare documents, not completed sessions. No athlete-level adaptation is inferred.

## Time and delivery

The model assumes one athlete with prompt access to fitted equipment. Work and instruction times are estimates; recovery minima come directly from the class. Walking returns may occupy rest only if the lane clears. Table instruction allowances are conservatively reserved outside the listed rests; if instruction fits within rest at delivery, use actual elapsed time rather than double counting.

| Task | Work and instruction model | Recovery | Seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 4 × 10 s start/slowing + 120 s demonstration | 2 × 75 s within pairs + 120 s between | 430 |
| E2 | 8 × 2.5 s exchange/hold + 90 s instruction | 6 × 10 s resets + 60 s set rest | 230 |
| E3 | 4 × 5 s settle/jump/finish + 90 s seat/setup instruction | 2 × 20 s + 90 s | 240 |
| E4 | 4 × 5 s setup/jump/finish + 60 s instruction | 2 × 20 s + 45 s side change | 165 |
| E5 | 12 s total hops/settling + 60 s instruction | 45 s side change | 117 |
| E6 | 2 × 4 s contacts + 90 s instruction | 60 s set rest | 158 |
| E transitions | No extra work | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s, including entry to S1 | 480 |
| S1/S2 | Same complete light prescriptions and teaching allowances as Class 1 | All releases, side changes, 45 s between rows and 60 s before P1 included | 330 |
| P1 | 24 s preparation + 60 s work + 90 s setup/instruction | Preparation 30 + 60 s; work 2 × 60 + 120 s | 504 |
| P2 | 24 s preparation + 36 s work + 90 s setup/instruction | Preparation 60 + 90 s; work 120 s | 420 |
| P3 | 24 s preparation + 48 s work + 75 s setup/instruction | Preparation 30 + 45 s; work 45 s | 267 |
| P4 | 10 s preparation + 40 s work + 60 s instruction | 45 s | 155 |
| P5 | 20 s preparation + 40 s work + 60 s setup/instruction | 45 s | 165 |
| P6 | 25 s preparation + 80 s work + 75 s setup/instruction | Preparation 60 s; work 90 s | 330 |
| P transitions | No extra work | 2 × 120 s + 3 × 90 s; no extra final rest | 510 |

**Totals:** E = **1,820 s / 30.33 min**; S = **330 s / 5.50 min**; P = **2,351 s / 39.18 min**; total **4,501 s / 75.02 min**. Plan **75–85 min after Access & Prepare 1**, not a promised whole-class duration. Longer teaching, wall/floor replacement setup, extra ramps, longer rest and queues can exceed the range. The supported unilateral P5 replacement adds approximately a minute; bilateral pogo fallback reduces side-change time but is not a reason to shorten other recovery.

No actual booking/group/staff is supplied. A 60-minute full-session window conflicts with this version; a 90-minute full-session window remains unconfirmed until preparation and group delays are known. Re-audit if a real booking arrives; do not quietly remove meaningful slots or rush rest.

**Group feasibility:** Keep one active start lane and close it during each walking return. A hypothetical three-athlete rotation on 30 s dispatches gives an athlete 80 s recovery after a 10 s start/slowing bout before the next 90 s-cycle turn. Between that athlete's two pairs, delay its next dispatch until at least 120 s after its prior finish. This only works when kneeling setup, stopping, return and coach feedback all fit; otherwise extend dispatch spacing. Wall/floor, jumps and lifts must not occupy the run-off. Do not infer three staffed stations from three lanes or let children perform extra work while waiting. Equipment counts and coach sightlines determine actual strength throughput.

## Requirements and unresolved conditions

- Correct next exposure, prior class/ledger/map/history/feedback reviewed; no observations added or inferred.
- Seven-category framework remains unchanged in curriculum; Sprinting subcategory names preserved.
- Existing Access & Prepare 1 referenced only; exact six/two/six nonzero rows in the required order and four-column format.
- Every exercise earns a specific job; no finishers, circuits, extra tests, throw retrieval or hidden jumps. Replacement doses and laterality are explicitly logged.
- Novel-drill count and same-leg demand reviewed; strength dosages retained for a reason; no automatic increase or cross-drill test comparison.
- Actual surface, 10 m/12 m discrepancy, knee comfort, suitable wall or floor alternative, seat fit, loads, waiting space, staffing, outside training, preparation and booking remain conditional.
- Class 2 and all updated records must be saved and reference/count/arithmetic checks must pass before this run ends. The verification report is document evidence, not a substitute for coaching or evidence of execution.

**Next intended job:** Class 3 should refine leg-specific push contribution using distinct explosive drills selected against the complete history and actual response. Retain or reduce familiar strength work as evidence warrants; do not prewrite the next class or assume Class 2 was performed.

# Class 4 — design and audit

**2026-09-13.** Previous run: progress, Class 3 saved. Reviewed Classes 1–3, map, prescription/workload ledger, drill history including contingencies, audits/source notes, equipment conflicts and athlete-feedback file. The specification snapshot is unchanged. No actual attendance, training response or recovery is supplied. Only Class 4 is finalized.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Maintain an upright trunk/pelvis while rapidly organizing the next nearby foot placement and supporting the body over one leg.
2. **Demand:** Separate support-leg force from free-leg recovery; avoid drift, reaching and excessive pelvic movement during brief rapid exchanges.
3. **Anchor:** Two six-contact stationary A-runs. Record attempted/controlled contacts, drift, lean and pelvic control within those contacts; this is a new protocol, not a speed test.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Single-leg vertical push/reception; alternating long-leg ankle rebound; foot return across unequal surface heights with a stable support foot; rapid arm action with limited torso compensation; rapid hip extension toward neutral. Strength retains split-leg extension, a flexed-hip hinge, thigh lift, changing knee-lever work and two knee-position ankle-force tasks. Light foot/lateral-hip strengthening supports the same upright demand.
5. **Constraints:** Exact 6/2/6, ages 12–14 baseline competence and supervision, no reported prior execution, unique-drill preference, gym footprint and unconfirmed platform/seat dimensions. No actual maximum-velocity practice can be supplied by this room.

## Consequential choices and revisions

| Question | Final decision and reason |
|---|---|
| Another start or upright anchor? | Select upright A-run as the day's anchor. A fourth start variation would divert practice from the planned upright task. The category-wide curriculum still covers starts elsewhere; no start is added as a hidden fifteenth exercise. |
| A-run versus previous low dribble or A-skip? | A-run uses alternating airborne bent-knee thigh exchanges with one landing per exchange, rather than a compact ankle-level cycle or a step-hop skip rhythm. This is a substantive rhythm/recovery task, not a renamed higher rep count. Keep just 12 contacts and no forced knee height. |
| Vertical single-leg jump versus prior bound/pogo? | A countermovement supplies upward force, then the same leg accepts a held landing. Earlier forward transfer and repetitive low ankle rebound have different direction/receiving jobs. Use modest height and four total landings; bilateral reception remains the fallback if needed. |
| External drop/rebound or floor-origin contact? | A low-box drop jump was considered and rejected: a suitable drop height and individual drop/rebound competence are unconfirmed, and added externally imposed landing energy is unnecessary. The final alternating floor-origin scissor bounce uses very low flight, softly extended knees and only six contacts. No drop jump was prescribed or performed. |
| Traveling straight-leg bounds? | Revised to an explicitly stationary low-amplitude scissor bounce. This removes a travel target and a temptation to reach forward. It still differs from prior bilateral/same-leg pogos through alternating long-leg support, and from E1 through knee/recovery strategy. No knee locking or aggressive backward clawing. |
| Low box hip switch versus rapid step-up? | Keep the support foot elevated throughout and move only the free foot down/up. The body does not rapidly rise from a floor-supported trailing leg as in Class 3's step-up. The job is pelvic control across a lower free-foot contact surface. Label the otherwise misleading word “switch”: feet do not swap onto the box. No arbitrary box height is treated as confirmed equipment. |
| Arm task relevance | Seated fast exchanges target rapid upper-limb action without excessive torso rocking, directly serving today's posture theme while limiting impact overlap. This is not generic upper-body strength or conditioning. It isolates one component and cannot train whole-stride arm–leg coordination; keep only eight exchanges. |
| Rapid bridge versus another jump | Select six bodyweight hip drives near neutral to add rapid hip-extension intent without more landings. This differs from Class 3's supine hip-flexion task, the slower loaded flexed-hip RDL and walkout's changing knee lever. The bridge is a constrained force exercise, not a simulation of running stance or a proven speed intervention. |
| Overlap and primary volume | Upright contacts now concentrate one-leg ankle/hip support. Reduce split squat **2 × 5/leg → 1 × 5/leg**. Do not restore RDL's second working set or the fourth walkout cycle. Retain calf doses rather than adding sets to match the upright theme. No increased weight/lever is used to compensate for lower volume. |
| Strength recurrence | All six lifts retain specific jobs. P1 still provides a challenging force anchor despite one round; P2 addresses a different hip range than the rapid bridge; P3 loads the thigh lift; P4 loads the opening knee lever; P5/P6 differ by knee position. S1/S2 remain easy foot/pelvic strengthening. No unrelated push/pull lift is inserted. |
| Exact novelty claim | All six defaults differ meaningfully from previous written defaults, with distinctions above. E4 is a related free-leg-placement variant, not a claim that changing a platform alone guarantees transfer. Previous contingency identities were also checked: the bilateral jump and standing cycle fallback are disclosed recurrences. Relevance/readiness takes priority over an absolute uniqueness promise. |

## Workload and recovery

E1 has **12 unilateral running contacts** (6/foot). E2/E3 have **10 unilateral jump/hop landing events** (5/foot: two held vertical jump receptions and three low scissor-bounce contacts). E4 has **6 nonflight free-foot floor touches** (3/foot). E5 has **8 simultaneous opposing arm exchanges**, not sixteen exercise repetitions. E6 has **6 nonflight rapid hip drives** (3/leg). Starts, sprint distance, throws, swings, approach jumps, drop landings and actual maximum-velocity running are zero. Incidental start/finish foot placements are additional actual contacts, not invented jump reps.

Do not combine running, jump/hop, light taps and bridges into equal-stress units. Compared with Class 3's eight jump/bound events, the new ten-event subtotal alone says little about tissue demand because the type and running component differ. Neither a small count nor the lower strength total proves readiness.

S work: **2 rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps plus 30 foot-seconds**. P work: **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 54 dynamic reps plus 3 walkout cycles** (24 heel steps). Preparation: **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps plus 1 short-lever cycle** (8 heel steps), separate from Access & Prepare 1 and working work. P1 reduction removes one round, two side bouts and ten reps from Class 3; other work holds.

Replacements are one-for-one slots with changed exposure. Nonflight E1 removes 12 airborne running contacts and substitutes 12 quick placements. Bilateral E2 keeps four events but changes four unilateral foot impacts to eight bilateral foot impacts. Nonflight E3 removes six hop events and substitutes six quick placements. E4 cycle fallback keeps six target foot placements with a different task; E5 standing keeps eight arm exchanges; E6 bilateral keeps six hip-drive reps with different laterality. P5 supported unilateral changes work to **10 bouts / 56 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, preparation to **10 bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**. Combinations must be recorded from actual choices, not inferred.

No athlete response supports a load increase. Advance only a relevant variable after actual controlled execution, technical reserve and subsequent recovery are documented; hold when observations are absent. Reduce or replace for task-specific faults, and stop for pain/loss of control. The wider sport, gym and tumbling schedule remains unknown; no performed cumulative total or guaranteed recovery interval is claimed.

## Timing and delivery model

Individual prompt equipment access is the assumption. Work/teaching allowances are estimates; rests are prescribed. Teaching is conservatively budgeted outside rests below: if it occurs within recovery, count that elapsed time once. Extend actual time for additional preparation sets, coaching, queues or recovery.

| Task | Work/teaching allowance | Recovery | Seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 2 × 8 s including start/finish; 90 s instruction | 90 s between sets | 196 |
| E2 | 4 × 4 s jump/hold; 90 s instruction | 2 × 20 s + 45 s side change | 191 |
| E3 | 6 s contacts/finish; 90 s instruction | Inter-exercise recovery below | 96 |
| E4 | 6 × 3 s tap/return/finish; 120 s setup/instruction | 4 × 10 s + 45 s side change | 223 |
| E5 | 2 × 3 s exchanges; 60 s setup/instruction | 75 s between sets | 141 |
| E6 | 6 × 4 s rise/hold/lower; 60 s instruction | 4 × 10 s + 45 s side change | 169 |
| E transitions through S1 | Setup can occupy rest | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s | 480 |
| **Explosiveness** | | | **1,496** |
| S1/S2 + transitions | 70 s holds/releases/side change + 30 s teaching; 60 s abductions + 20 s side change + 45 s teaching | 45 s between, 60 s after | **330** |
| P1 | Prep 24 s; work 30 s; teaching 90 s | Prep-side 30 s, prework 60 s, work-side 60 s | 294 |
| P2 | Prep 24 s; work 18 s; teaching 90 s | 60 s between ramps, 90 s before work | 282 |
| P3 | Prep 24 s; work 48 s; teaching 75 s | 30 s prep sides, 45 s prework, 45 s work sides | 267 |

# Class 5 — design and audit

**2026-09-13. Previous run: progress**, evidenced by saved Class 4 and updated state. Before selection, checked current state paths, the specification snapshot and hashes of Classes 1–4; reviewed the map, preceding class, earlier strength prescriptions, workload ledger, all default/contingency drill history, audit/source records and feedback. No actual athlete work or recovery is supplied. Only Class 5 is finalized.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Recover one thigh quickly while keeping the supporting leg and pelvis organized for the next contact.
2. **Demand:** Distinguish the supporting leg's push from free-leg motion; keep a compact recovery without reaching, pelvic hitching or excess trunk movement.
3. **Primary task:** Stationary single-leg high-knee run, three cycles per target leg. Observe controlled cycles and extra contacts within the scheduled work, with a new drill-specific record.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Unilateral upward push with shared reception; same-leg ankle recoil coupled to the opposite thigh; modest lower-leg release in a skip rhythm; rapid front-leg extension as a trailing leg recovers; opposing thigh exchanges without landings. Light foot/lateral-hip work and six retained strength roles support those demands.
5. **Constraints:** Exact 6/2/6, baseline ages 12–14 with established technique and supervision, no reported response, unique-drill preference, no maximum-velocity runway, unconfirmed group/booking and equipment dimensions. The session is gym supplementation, not a complete top-speed exposure.

## Selection, overlap and actual revisions

| Choice | Finding and final decision |
|---|---|
| Main unilateral recovery task | Choose asymmetric high-knee running in place over repeating Class 4's alternating high-knee pattern. One leg repeatedly performs the fuller recovery while the other takes a low running step; both legs still contact the floor. Do not mislabel this as three same-leg hops or a permanently planted support. |
| Main-task dose | Reduce the considered two rounds of two cycles per target leg to **one round of three cycles per target leg**. That gives three continuous observations per target with **12 running contacts**, rather than 16; it holds Class 4's running-contact count while changing the task. No repetitions are added to fill a quality score. |
| Vertical takeoff and reception | Use single-leg takeoff to a two-foot landing. The receiver changes materially from Class 4's same-leg finish, sharing reception while preserving unilateral upward force. This is a task redistribution, not a claim that a more advanced athlete earned a harder landing or greater height. It also differs from Class 1's horizontal version by force direction. |
| Same-leg recoil with thigh motion | Add an active opposite-thigh pulse to the same-leg pogo, not merely a new free-leg pose/name. The timing of ankle push and free-thigh movement is the job. Reduce the considered three hops/leg to **two/leg**, because the coupling is new and E1/E4 already add rhythmic contacts. The plain-pogo fallback openly repeats Class 2. |
| B-skip versus another A-skip | A modest knee opening and foot return in the skip supplies a release task absent from Class 1's A-skip. The support hop and transfer are phases of one named drill, not separate exercises hidden in a row. Do not force a straight knee, kick forward or claw backward; use the prior A-skip family if control is worse. |
| Rapid lunge versus another platform exercise | A controlled backward entry followed by rapid ascent into thigh recovery uses the floor and removes Class 4's unconfirmed low-platform requirement. It differs from Class 3's elevated-foot step-up through a moving rear-foot entry and stable floor-based front-foot push. No barbell/band accommodating resistance or flight is added. |
| Supine opposing exchanges | Select short unresisted opposing switches, both heels off the floor, rather than another banded knee drive or upright jump. Class 3 moved one resisted leg while the other heel stayed grounded; here both thighs exchange while the pelvis is floor-supported. Bring feet down during resets to avoid turning four quick efforts into a prolonged abdominal endurance hold. |
| Alternatives not selected | A staggered ballistic swing adds loaded hinge/setup demands without a better recovery-coordination job; lateral hops would shift force direction away from today's target; airborne full single-leg cycling adds greater coordination/landing demand. These are not used simply to collect new names. |
| Strength overlap | Keep Class 4's **one split-squat round, one RDL working set and three walkout cycles**. Do not restore removed volume. E5's six quick bodyweight rises have a movement/recovery job; P1 supplies controlled external loading in a stable base. E6 is four light opposing exchanges, whereas P3 provides challenging seated hip-flexion force. All eight strengthening identities remain relevant. |
| Distinctness claim | Six default prescriptions differ in task or force/reception demand from previous defaults; several are related variants, not unrelated new movements. E2 deliberately changes the receiver, E3 adds dynamic coupling, E4 adds controlled release. Cosmetic dose/label changes alone receive no novelty credit. Contingency recurrence is explicit, and actual usage is still unknown. |

## Exposure and recovery accounting

Default running: **12 contacts**, six/foot. E2: **4 single-leg takeoffs and bilateral landings**, two takeoffs/leg. E3: **4 same-leg pogo landings**, two/leg. E4: **4 support-hop landings** plus **4 raised-foot transfer contacts**, two/foot in each role. Jump/hop total: **12 events, four bilateral and eight unilateral landings; 16 jump/hop foot impacts**. Running contacts and skip transfers are additional, different contact types.

E5: **6 nonflight lunge rises**, three/front leg; each includes one rear-foot floor placement and one returning free-foot set-down, **12 controlled foot placements** in total. E6: **4 simultaneous opposing exchanges**, both legs move on each exchange; eight limb excursions are not eight exercise reps. Gentle setup/reset/exit foot contacts are additional incidental contacts. Starts, sprint distance, throws, swings, external drops and actual maximum-velocity running are zero.

Class 4 had 12 running contacts, 10 unilateral jump/hop events and six low-box taps. Class 5 retains 12 running contacts but prescribes 12 jump/hop events with shared reception in four of them. The extra two events and changed types are disclosed, not presented as a neutral load swap or earned impact progression. Pogo dose is reduced and no height/distance target is increased. On-site competence and actual recovery govern use of the defaults or regressions; small counts do not establish readiness.

Light work remains **2 rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps + 30 foot-seconds**. Primary remains **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 54 dynamic reps + 3 walkout cycles** (24 heel steps). Preparation remains **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps + 1 short-lever cycle** (8 heel steps). A round includes both sides; a bout is one separately performed side. Unknown Access & Prepare 1 and outside sport/gym/tumbling are excluded, not assumed zero. No performed cumulative total can be calculated.

Rest separates brief fast tasks from light strengthening and loaded work. Keep the light work at RPE 3–4 and primary work at 2–3 technical RIR. Extend recovery or stop affected tasks when quality does not return; do not shorten rests to fit a clock or add make-up attempts. Future changes need actual execution, technical reserve and subsequent recovery. Retaining a written dose does not establish that it was previously performed or tolerated.

## Replacement effects

- E1 march substitutes 12 nonflight placements for 12 airborne running contacts.
- E2 bilateral takeoff keeps four bilateral landings/eight landing foot impacts but removes four unilateral takeoffs. It repeats the earlier optional jump family.
- E3 plain same-leg pogo keeps four unilateral landings with no thigh pulse; the family recurs at a lower dose. Bilateral pogo instead keeps four events but changes them to bilateral: with other defaults, jump/hop total becomes **8 bilateral + 4 unilateral events = 20 foot impacts**. Choose one replacement, not both.
- E4 A-skip preserves four hop landings/four transfer contacts but removes the release task and repeats the Class 1 family. No B-skip performance is recorded when A-skip was used.
- E5 shorter step/depth and E6 shorter reach/more knee bend scale the existing exercise; they do not add entries. Log actual execution range, failed/partial work and extra foot placements.
- Supported unilateral P5 changes working totals to **10 bouts / 56 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, preparation to **10 bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**. A fitted box can replace a bench without creating another exercise; actual support/seat conditions affect comparisons.

## Timing and delivery

Individual prompt equipment access is assumed. Work/teaching durations are estimates; rests are prescriptions. Teaching is conservatively budgeted separately below; if it occurs during rest, count actual elapsed time once. Queues supply recovery only when the actual interval meets the athlete's requirement.

| Task | Work and teaching allowance | Recovery | Seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 2 × 8 s including entry/finish; 120 s teaching | 90 s between target legs | 226 |
| E2 | 4 × 5 s jump/hold; 90 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 60 s side change | 210 |
| E3 | 2 × 5 s contacts/final hold; 90 s teaching | 60 s between legs | 160 |
| E4 | 4 × 4 s step-hop actions; 120 s teaching | Inter-exercise rest below | 136 |
| E5 | 6 × 5 s complete reps; 90 s teaching | 4 × 10 s + 45 s side change | 205 |
| E6 | 4 × 2 s exchanges/finish; 90 s teaching | 3 × 10 s, including feet-down reset/setup | 128 |
| E transitions through S1 | Setup may occupy rest | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s | 480 |
| **Explosiveness** | | | **1,545** |
| S1/S2 and transitions | Same as Class 4: 225 s work/teaching/side changes | 45 s between + 60 s after | **330** |
| P1 | Prep 24 s + work 30 s + teaching 90 s | 30 s prep sides + 60 s prework + 60 s work sides | 294 |
| P2 | Prep 24 s + work 18 s + teaching 90 s | 60 s between ramps + 90 s prework | 282 |
| P3 | Prep 24 s + work 48 s + teaching 75 s | 30 s prep sides + 45 s prework + 45 s work sides | 267 |
| P4 | Prep 10 s + work 30 s + teaching 60 s | 45 s prework | 145 |
| P5 | Prep 20 s + work 40 s + teaching 60 s | 45 s prework | 165 |

| **Primary** | | | **1,993** |
| **Total excluding Access & Prepare 1** | | | **3,868 s = 64.47 min** |

Allow **65–75 min outside Access & Prepare 1**, with extra time as needed. Supported unilateral P5 adds about one minute. Full-session time is unknown; a 60-minute complete booking cannot fit this version. Group size, staffing, equipment quantities and actual queues are not supplied. Do not assume children can lift unsupervised while another station is coached, or repeat an explosive bout to fill queue time.

Verify non-slip floor, landing width, rear lunge clearance, waiting positions, fitted seated supports and suitable DB loads. Defaults remove dependence on a low platform, band anchor and throwing zone. The 10 m/12 m facility discrepancy remains recorded; neither is used to claim a maximum-velocity runway. Actual other sport/gym/tumbling and preparation exposure must inform scheduling; approximate 48–72-hour spacing is only a starting consideration, not a universal rule.

## Handoff

Save Class 5 and supporting notes; update map, workload/novelty history, feedback/state and verification. Preserve Classes 1–4. Archive the Class 4 verification as a historical checkpoint whose shared-file hashes are not current-state expectations.

Next run: review all saved work and actual feedback, then finalize **Class 6 only**, consolidating start and upright-support demands. Examine asymmetric rhythm, takeoff/receiver control, pogo/thigh timing, skip release, actual strength reserve and full-session workload. Do not automatically restore strength sets, add contacts or increase load/complexity. No later exercise tables are created now.

# Sprinting — source, assumption and exercise register

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-13. These are sources for constrained programming decisions and local identity evidence, not a claim that the exact class is experimentally validated, OTA-authored or published in the live library. No exercise database records were changed.

## External evidence and style sources

| Source | What it contributes | Limit on interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| [Overtime Athletes — Soccer Speed Drills for Acceleration and Max Velocity](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/soccer-speed-drills/) | Style inspiration from start practice, horizontal/unilateral plyometrics and upright skipping mechanics; the article distinguishes acceleration and maximum velocity. | Marketing and coaching guidance, not research validating a session. Its longer routes, repeated jumps and advice to vary stimuli are not imported. Stationary A-skip and local doses are our adaptations. |
| [Overtime Athletes — Strength Training for Basketball](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/strength-training-for-basketball/) | Public two-point-start example and organization of speed work with gym training. | Not a prescription for this cohort or 10 m lane. Its 10-yard run prescription is not used. |
| [Weyand et al. (2000), Faster top running speeds are achieved with greater ground forces not more rapid leg movements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11053354/) | Primary research supporting the relevance of force during ground contact to maximum running speed. | Does not show that pogos, calves or this class cause faster sprints, and is not a Class 1 youth intervention. No numerical speed prediction is made. |
| [Dorn, Schache and Pandy (2012), Muscular strategy shift in human running: dependence of running speed on hip and ankle muscle performance](https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/article/215/11/1944/10883/Muscular-strategy-shift-in-human-running) | Primary study combining measured running data with musculoskeletal modeling; gives a rationale for considering hip muscles as well as ankle plantarflexors as running speed changes. | Model-based muscle roles, not evidence for one exact hip-flexion exercise or a universal speed threshold in 12–14-year-olds. No study threshold is used as an athlete target. |
| [NSCA (Faigenbaum et al., 2009), Youth resistance training position statement](https://dxpprod.nsca.com/globalassets/about/position-statements/position_stand_youth_resistance_training---2009.pdf) | Official specialist guidance on qualified supervision, individual competence and appropriately prescribed resistance, technique and recovery for youth. | General guidance; does not establish readiness, confirm a safe total dose or validate the fixed fourteen-entry template. The 2–3 technical RIR target is supplied by the user's specification. |

The design inference is deliberately limited: strengthen and rehearse relevant capacities in the space available, then judge actual response. A drill's intended mechanical role is not a demonstrated sprint-performance outcome. No source justifies pretending upright gym drills are maximum-velocity running. No quoted marketing outcome, injury-prevention guarantee or precise cross-drill transfer percentage is used.

## Local identity evidence

The repository's [`docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv`](../../../docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv) was searched by name/slug. These are local identities, not verified current live IDs, approval status or athlete eligibility. Later canonical contracts were checked where consequential: the traveling A-skip explicitly excludes stationary skipping, and the standing-calf baseline does not automatically authorize an unsupported loaded bilateral variant.

| Slot | Class name / local identity evidence | Mapping boundary |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Two-point start — two-step projection; related local `2-point-acceleration-start`, `two-point-start-to-5-10-yard-sprint` | **Proposed short-step prescription; no exact canonical ID asserted.** The related library distances are longer; do not bind the two-step task to an incompatible sprint-distance card. |
| E2 | Paused Broad Jump to Stick, hands on hips | **Proposed addition/variant.** Related `broad-jump-to-stick` exists; the exact paused, no-arm task is explicitly authored here. |
| E3 | Single-leg Broad Jump to Two-foot Landing | **Proposed addition.** Do not map to a same-leg hop-and-stick or repeated single-leg broad jump. |
| E4 | Ankle Pogo in Place — `ankle-pogo-in-place` | Name/slug verified locally; low bilateral in-place execution is explicit. Canonical contract is available, but no live binding is claimed. |
| E5 | Stationary A-Skip | **Proposed distinct drill.** The inspected `a-skip` contract defines traveling step-hop cycles and expressly excludes stationary skipping. This plan declares its own stationary cycle count and does not pretend to use that exact canonical card. |
| E6 | Kettlebell Swing — `kettlebell-swing` | Migration 472 confirms canonical name and two-/one-hand family boundaries. Declare two hands, one bell, chest-height ceiling, hip-driven float and controlled park; current live variant publication unverified. |
| S1 | Short-Foot Drill — `short-foot-drill` | Name/slug verified. Both feet supported, one target foot's arch hold, long toes. Class hold time and light intent are authored dosage. |
| S2 | Side-Lying Hip Abduction | **Proposed addition; no exact local binding verified.** Plain bodyweight lateral-hip strengthening, not a clamshell or balance test. |
| P1 | Split Squat — `split-squat`; local `dumbbell-split-squat` also exists | Use canonical common name with explicit two-DB-at-sides, floor split stance. No elevated rear foot or lunge travel. Exact live variant binding unverified. |
| P2 | Romanian Deadlift — `romanian-deadlift`; local `dumbbell-romanian-deadlift` also exists | Common name plus explicit two-DB implement and class tempo/range. No single-leg or floor-deadlift substitution is silently inferred. |
| P3 | Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion | **Proposed addition; no invented slug or ID.** Related `banded-hip-flexor-march` exists, but seated distal-thigh DB loading is different and uses no band anchor. Hands secure the implement rather than lift it. |
| P4 | Glute Bridge Walkout — `glute-bridge-walkout` | Name/slug verified locally. Four steps out/four back and the leverage/RIR criterion are session details; not a plain bridge or a Nordic curl. |
| P5 | Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — local `standing-dumbbell-calf-raise` | **Explicit loaded bilateral floor variant; exact current binding unverified.** The inspected standing-calf research identifies a supported unloaded baseline and treats unsupported/loaded execution as separate variants. Do not claim that baseline validates this variant. |
| P6 | Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — `bent-knee-soleus-raise` | Migration 544 identifies seated DB calf work as part of the canonical knee-flexed plantarflexion identity rather than a separate surviving Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise record. Use explicit seated bilateral execution; no live UUID asserted. |

**Replacement identities:** One-step start is a proposed change to E1's short-step task. Hands-on-hips Countermovement Jump to Stick is an explicitly named unloaded dynamic vertical replacement; no exact live variant binding is claimed. P5's supported single-leg calf has local name `Single-Leg Calf Raise`, slug `single-leg-calf-raise`, but its support/load are declared session conditions. A fitted box instead of a bench changes equipment support, not the exercise slot. Seated short-foot is a stated support regression, not extra work.

## Files and records actually consulted

- Supplied Downloads specification, retained verbatim as [local snapshot](VORTEX_12_CLASS_CURRICULUM_SPEC.md).
- Root workout-plan inventory and existing per-focus class/state layout; no Sprinting progress found at initial review.
- Relevant adjacent athlete-feedback files: Vertical Jumps, Horizontal Jumps, directional Agility, reactive/anticipation Agility, force-absorption/elastic-rebound Jumps. They record no supplied actual observations.
- Selected neighboring progression/workload excerpts and Horizontal Jumps exercise register, used for overlap and local provenance, not as performed-work evidence.
- [`docs/programming/FACILITY_AND_EQUIPMENT.md`](../../../docs/programming/FACILITY_AND_EQUIPMENT.md), including the conflicting 12 m/eight-tenet/booking language; current user/spec architecture and 10 m footprint take priority here.
- Athleticism week-two attendance/workload JSON status and structure: `PASS_BOUNDED_WRITTEN_WEEK2_AUDIT`; these are modeled paths. Its presence is not evidence of real attendance or completion.
- Local exercise CSV and [`a-skip` identity contract](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/contracts/a-skip.v1.json).
- Relevant identity excerpts from [`standing-calf-raise.v1.json`](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/batches/standing-calf-raise.v1.json), [`acceleration-starts.v1.json`](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/batches/acceleration-starts.v1.json), [KB swing migration 472](../../../backend/migrations/472_coaching_kettlebell_swing_family_audit_hardening.sql) and [seated calf identity migration 544](../../../backend/migrations/544_coaching_seated_dumbbell_calf_raise_direct_identity_collision_closure.sql).

## Unresolved facts

No actual athlete attendance, loads, readiness, recovery or test results. No verified preparation contents/duration. No confirmed booking, group size, coach count, lane width, waiting route or equipment quantities/load ranges/bench dimensions. No timing-gate or force-plate feature assumptions. The newer user instruction changes future drill selection, not these unknowns. All results remain prescription-only until feedback is supplied.

# Class 9 — source and exercise identity notes

**Reviewed 2026-09-13.** The user requests Sprinting support, exact 6/2/6 and meaningful drill novelty. These local prescriptions are OTA-inspired, not an OTA-authored or experimentally validated session. Doses, stationary adaptations, replacements and timing are authored for the available space and unknown response.

## Sources and limits

| Source | Useful evidence | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| [OTA — Best Linear Speed Drills for Superior Speed, Part 2](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/best-linear-speed-drills-for-superior-speed-pt-2/) | Explicitly distinguishes high-knee, butt-kick and combined high-knee/butt-kick running; supplies the coupled hip/knee-recovery idea. | Twelve stationary contacts are our dose. No forced knee height, heel collision, guaranteed speed gain or appended sprint is imported. Prior A-run execution could overlap; actual technique determines whether the athlete experiences a new pattern. |
| [OTA — Full Top Speed Training Session](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/full-top-speed-training-session/) | Places recovery drills, ankle/leg support and subsequent running integration in the same coaching approach. | No replacement warm-up or traveling sprint is copied. This gym session does not provide the later top-speed integration. |
| [OTA — Three Speed Training Drills You Need](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/3-speed-training-drills-you-need/) | Emphasizes nearby foot placement in a straight-leg/bounding family and avoiding an artificially long reach. | E4 is our nonflight stationary downstroke, not its traveling bound. No locked knee, forceful backward scrape or claimed stride-length gain. |
| [OTA — How to Jump Higher Off One Foot, Part 2](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/one-foot-part-2/) | Identifies the single-leg RDL as a hip-dominant task and cues a hip hinge with a relaxed knee. | Does not validate our four shallow bodyweight rapid returns or demonstrate sprint transfer. The day remains Sprinting, not a jumping curriculum. |
| [NSCA — Romanian Deadlift](https://www.nsca.com/education/articles/kinetic-select/romanian-deadlift-rdl/) | Official technique guidance for hip-driven motion with slight knee flexion and controlled spinal position. | Its barbell technique is not the exact unilateral rapid-return prescription. Load, depth, speed and support here are separately qualified; no rehabilitation or injury-prevention claim. |

The foundational youth-supervision and hip/ankle research rationale remains in the [initial source register](sources_and_exercises.md). Those sources do not establish this athlete's readiness or validate the complete fourteen-entry session. The seated coordinated drill is an authored proposal; searches did not verify an exact OTA demonstration, and cycling pages or unrelated circuits were not used as evidence.

## Local identity checks

Searched `docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv` and the relevant generated-record paths. Found names/slugs for `repeated-vertical-jump`, `split-stance-pogo`, `single-leg-romanian-deadlift` and bodyweight single-leg RDL/reach variants. CSV presence verifies a local name/family only; no live publication, media approval or athlete availability was inspected.

Read the generated records for `straight-leg-bound-march` and `distance-jump-straight-leg-bound-march`. The former explicitly flags a conflation of marching and bounding; the latter describes a traveling alternating no-flight march. Neither exactly defines E4's stationary same-moving-leg downstroke. Do not bind E4 to an ambiguous march/bound card or claim its contact sequence was obtained from that name.

| Slot | Binding and novelty decision |
|---|---|
| E1 coupled stationary run | **Proposed stationary variant** of the OTA-named combined pattern; no exact local binding verified. Closely related to Classes 4/8. If prior actual A-run technique already included the same fold, record recurrence rather than a new athlete exposure. |
| E2 repeated vertical jump | Use local name/slug **Repeated Vertical Jump / repeated-vertical-jump** with an explicitly authored two-jump/final-hold prescription. No detailed generated variant was verified. Vertical immediate reuse differs from Class 8's horizontal reuse and earlier isolated vertical receivers. |
| E3 split pogo | Use local name/slug **Split-Stance Pogo / split-stance-pogo** with exact low-flight, both-feet, same-offset execution specified in the class. Not a scissor switch or deeper split jump. No unverified dominance percentage or published variant ID. |
| E4 straight-leg downstroke | **Proposed explicit addition:** one support foot fixed, low forward lift of the same moving leg, quick nearby floor return, no hop or traveling march. Distinct from Class 3's full cycle and Class 4's airborne scissor exchange. |
| E5 seated alternating sprint action | **Proposed coordinated variant:** one quick knee lift synchronized with opposing arms, then controlled foot return/reset. Unlike Class 4's arms-only seat task, Class 7's fixed-arm wall knee drive and P3's hand-secured loaded hip flexion. |
| E6 rapid unilateral hinge | **Proposed bodyweight rapid-return variant** within the verified single-leg RDL family. The local reach/control or loaded variants do not establish its tempo. No catch, deep reach or added knee drive; shallow unilateral force expression differs from P2's controlled bilateral loaded capacity work. |
| S1/S2 and P1–P6 | Previous identities, working/preparation doses and rests held; jobs revised for upright support/recovery. Load qualification remains individual and unobserved. |

The six defaults have task-specific distinctions, not six unrelated new base movements. All prior defaults and contingencies were reviewed. Earlier A-run, isolated CMJ, parallel pogo, full-cycle strike, standing arm and bridge tasks remain explicit replacements; no replacement is added to its default. Changing actual support, range, contact type or coordination condition changes the record and invalidates a casual cross-drill numerical comparison.

Fitted seating, optional stable hand support, floor, clearance, equipment size, staffing and full-session duration remain unconfirmed. No local library or application records were edited. Prescribed work remains separate from unknown actual attendance, execution and recovery.

# Class 5 — sources and exercise identities

Reviewed 2026-09-13. Sources inform component choices; the exact 6/2/6 session, small doses and replacements are authored for this request. No whole-session validation or guaranteed sprint improvement is claimed.

## Coaching and research basis

- [Overtime Athletes: Top Speed Training Progression](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/use-this-top-speed-training-progression/) describes a single-leg high-knee task before more complete cycling work. Class 5 adapts the asymmetric recovery idea to a stationary footprint with explicit contact counts. Traveling distances, forced right-angle positions, aggressive clawing and claims about preventing hamstring tears are not imported.
- [Overtime Athletes: Seven Plyometrics for Speed](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/the-7-best-plyometrics-for-speed/) describes coupling ankle push and opposite-thigh drive in a same-leg or alternating high-knee pogo. Class 5 uses only two stationary same-leg hops per side, natural arms and no dowel or traveling pass. The full airborne single-leg cycle described there is not selected. This is coaching inspiration, not proof of exact transfer or dose suitability.
- [Overtime Athletes: Sprint Mechanics for Maximum Speed](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/sprint-mechanics-for-maximum-speed/) and [Soccer Speed Drills](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/soccer-speed-drills/) discuss B-skip lower-leg release and compact recovery. Class 5 defines a modest release without a high kick/reaching contact. The original traveling/program context does not establish a stationary drill's effectiveness.
- [Overtime Athletes: Five Explosive Exercises](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/5-explosive-exercises/) includes forceful reverse-lunge ascent within an acceleration program. The selected bodyweight floor lunge-to-knee-drive is a local adaptation for unilateral force/recovery, without bands, rack, loaded ballistic ascent or a claim that its slow phase reproduces sprint stance.
- Previously reviewed [Dorn, Schache and Pandy, 2012](https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/article/215/11/1944/10883/Muscular-strategy-shift-in-human-running) informs hip/ankle-function reasoning. The unresisted supine switch is an authored constraint on opposing thigh motion and pelvic control, not an exercise validated by that running model. Retained strength rationales and supervised technical loading remain as documented in the [initial source register](sources_and_exercises.md) and [Class 4 notes](class_04_sources_and_exercises.md).

## Local library checks

Inspected `docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv` and the generated records named below. These establish local identity evidence only; no live exercise account/database was queried and no library record was changed. No identifiers are invented.

| Slot | Verified local evidence | Binding decision |
|---|---|---|
| E1 stationary single-leg high-knee run | No exact high-knee identity found in the inspected CSV | **Proposed addition:** asymmetric running rhythm, one target contact plus one low opposite contact per cycle. Do not bind it to a same-leg pogo, planted-support cycle or alternating A-run. |
| E2 single-leg vertical to bilateral landing | Related `single-leg-hop-to-stick` / `single-leg-hop-to-stick-low-amplitude` found | **Proposed explicit variant.** The inspected `single-leg-hop-to-stick-low-amplitude.v1.json` specifies forward same-leg reception, so it is not an exact match for upward push/two-foot reception. |
| E3 knee-drive pogo | `single-leg-pogo` family and `single-leg-hop-pogo-identity/single-leg-pogo.v1.json` | Family verified; terminal-stick variant requires at least two same-leg contacts. **Proposed dynamic thigh-coupling variant**, with stationary motion, no intermediate stick and a final hold. The thigh pulse is an additional task, not a claim that a new cue alone creates an identity. Plain-pogo fallback openly reuses the prior family. |
| E4 stationary B-skip | `a-skip` and related skip names found; no exact B-skip identity in inspected CSV | **Proposed addition.** Generated `a-skip.v1.json` is a traveling step-hop definition, not B-skip. The four-column class explicitly distinguishes hop landings and transfer contacts; A-skip fallback repeats the earlier stationary adaptation. |
| E5 rapid reverse lunge/knee drive | `reverse-lunge`, `bodyweight-reverse-lunge` and loaded reverse-lunge families found | **Proposed rapid-ascent/knee-drive variant** of the bodyweight family. Do not treat a CSV family name as proof of the exact moving-foot/finish prescription or bind to banded/barbell work. |
| E6 supine opposing hip switch | Nearby dead-bug heel-tap/leg-lower records exist; no exact rapid opposing-switch identity found | **Proposed addition:** both heels remain off the floor during an exchange, both legs move, feet down during rest. It is not a heel-tap dead bug, one-leg banded knee drive or bridge. |
| S1/S2 and P1–P6 | Prior [source register](sources_and_exercises.md) | Retain existing family/variant qualifications and doses. No new IDs or assumed published-card matches. |

Generated records inspected are under `scripts/data/canonical-research/generated/`. Their media candidates or taxonomy recommendations do not certify this class. No exercise-video viewing, numerical force measurement or athlete performance is claimed.

## Practical limits

The gym supplies only a short footprint; all Class 5 work remains stationary or within one rear lunge step. Seat fit, loads, floor, staffing and group timing still require actual verification. Readiness, attendance and recovery are unknown; do not infer completed work from the state file. The 65–75 minute allowance excludes existing Access & Prepare 1 and unmodeled delays. The current seven-category/spec architecture governs over the separate older facility template. Full-speed running integration remains a direct-practice gap.
