# Sprinting Class 1 — design and audit

**Status:** Finalized conditional prescription, 2026-09-13. Audit addresses programming and document consistency, not athlete clearance, actual completion or guaranteed performance transfer. The latest user steering prioritizes unique drills across classes while permitting recurring strength lifts.

## Daily stimulus brief, before exercise selection

1. **Result:** Better-organized projection into the first two start steps, supported by relevant hip, knee and ankle force capacity.
2. **Demand:** Generate forward impulse from stillness while coordinating the free thigh, arms and a connected trunk/pelvis. Introduce upright support mechanics in a small supplemental dose; the start and upright tasks have different body orientations.
3. **Anchor:** E1's six short starts, observed for the push, first contacts and controlled stopping. No top-speed measurement or extra testing block.
4. **Other jobs:** Bilateral static horizontal impulse; unilateral horizontal impulse with simpler landing; isolated ankle recoil; upright step-hop/thigh coordination; externally loaded rapid hip extension. Then easy foot-base and lateral-hip control; finally split-stance extension, flexed-hip hinge strength, hip flexion, knee-flexor support, straight-knee and bent-knee ankle force.
5. **Marker and constraints:** Record E1 quality within scheduled attempts. Use a protected 10 m lane with early termination of driving, ages 12–14 baseline competence, unknown individual readiness and unknown preparation/booking/group size. Exact 6/2/6; gym supplementation beyond starts.

## Consequential choices and audit revisions

| Question | Finding and final decision |
|---|---|
| Which main task most directly answers the request? | Two-point starts give direct opening-step practice. A 10 m sprint would consume the entire known lane and leave unverified run-off; flying sprints and a full acceleration-to-upright transition do not fit. Limit driving to two strikes/by 3 m, then progressively stop by 9 m; first prescribed attempts establish feasibility at controlled intent. |
| Six explosive rows without six full workouts? | Put six attempts into the main start. Limit paused bilateral and single-leg horizontal jumps to four each; pogo to ten and skip to six hop landings. Keep the swing at ten repetitions. This preserves useful work while avoiding a repeated-bound circuit. |
| Are the horizontal jumps redundant? | E2 removes the countermovement/arms to isolate a still-start bilateral push. E3 requires one leg to supply takeoff impulse with bilateral reception. Different takeoff demands justify separate small doses; neither distance is used as a sprint-time surrogate. |
| Are pogo and skip the same? | E4 isolates bilateral ankle recoil at small amplitude. E5 integrates unilateral step-hop support with opposite thigh and arm recovery in an upright stance. Their contact types are separately counted. Neither approximates an actual maximum-speed stride's full forces or velocity. |
| Why swing instead of a throw or repeated maximal jump? | The externally loaded rapid hinge uses available KBs and adds no planned impacts. A throw would need unconfirmed containment; more repeated jumps would add calf/landing demand. A qualified swing is required; the stated CMJ replacement is one-for-one and changes the exposure record. |
| Why these two light exercises? | Short-foot addresses the foot base with no added loaded calf set. Side-lying abduction addresses lateral hip control without a tiring single-leg stance test before split squats. Doses stay easy and short. |
| Why six strength slots rather than six compound lifts? | A split squat gives the primary split-stance knee/hip extension task; the RDL adds a hip-dominant pattern. A third squat/lunge or hip-thrust slot would overlap heavily. Direct seated hip flexion, a small long-lever knee-flexor task, and two knee-angle ankle tasks fill distinct gaps instead. No upper-body fillers. |
| Posterior-chain overlap? | Starts, both horizontal jumps, swings, RDLs and walkouts all involve the posterior chain. The walkout is one challenging set, and only two hinge working sets are prescribed. Its job is knee-flexor support as the knee opens/returns, not another hip-extension lift or maximal eccentric Nordic dose. |
| Calf overlap? | Starts, pogos and skipping overlap with P5/P6. Three primary calf bouts are enough for this initial prescription; no extra ankle-hop drill or calf endurance finisher. Straight versus bent knees is a purposeful joint-position distinction, not a claim of exclusive muscle isolation. |
| Equipment requirements? | Default class uses confirmed equipment categories and no wall anchor/rack/sled. Bench height, DB/KB loads, grip, landing surface and sweep clearance still need checking. Stable box substitution preserves the seated movement. Unsupported bilateral P5 avoids assuming a hand-support structure; its supported unilateral replacement requires an actually verified support. |
| Missing feedback? | Other local plans and modeled workload scenarios do not demonstrate athlete attendance or tolerance. Start at Class 1; keep loads conditional and observation fields unknown. Later novel drills must not smuggle in an automatic impact/intensity increase. |
| User's drill-uniqueness update? | Updated map, ledger and handoff to prioritize distinct explosive drills across classes. Repeated strength lifts carry matched progression. Track actual exercise identity and job in drill history; a renamed or differently loaded drill is not unique. Any necessary recurrence needs a documented feasibility/relevance reason. |

## Workload check

The [ledger](../progression_ledger.md) records all 14 rows, both sides, preparation sets and replacements. Default totals are **6 starts, 24 jump/hop landing events plus 6 skip transfer contacts, 10 swings, 2 light rounds/4 bouts and 9 primary rounds/12 bouts**. Primary work is **70 dynamic reps plus 4 complete walkout cycles**; load-preparation adds **32 dynamic reps plus 1 cycle**, in **9 bouts**. There are no throws or maximum-velocity runs. Unknown preparation means these are not complete-session totals.

Quality-limited starts may have fewer than two driving contacts before the distance boundary. Failed attempts and stopped work stay in actuals. A final document can prescribe 14 meaningful entries while allowing an athlete to stop when conditions require; omitted actual work is not retroactively treated as a full-dose class.

## Timing calculation

This is an **individual, prompt-equipment-access planning model**, not confirmed group throughput. Work seconds are reasonable execution estimates; required rests come from the class. Demonstration/setup allowances are assumptions. Rest is measured after the previous effort, with walking return, setup and instruction allowed inside it. No queue time is counted twice. Additional coaching beyond these allowances adds time.

| Task | Active/setup assumptions | Recovery counted | Model minutes |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 6 × about 10 s for start/ease down; 120 s demonstration/layout instruction. Walking back is inside the rests. | 3 × 75 s within pairs + 2 × 120 s between pairs. | 10.75 |
| E2 | 4 × about 5 s for pause/flight/finish; 60 s instruction. | 2 × 20 s within sets + 90 s between sets. | 3.50 |
| E3 | 4 × about 5 s; 60 s instruction. | 2 × 20 s same-leg resets + 45 s side change. | 2.75 |
| E4 | About 10 s work + 45 s instruction. | No within-exercise set rest needed. | 0.92 |
| E5 | About 12 s work + 75 s teaching/count clarification. | No within-exercise set rest needed. | 1.45 |
| E6 | 2 × about 15 s including setup/parking + 90 s instruction. | 90 s between sets. | 3.50 |
| Explosive transitions | No extra work. | 3 × 90 s + 3 × 60 s, including final transition to S1. | 7.50 |
| S1 | 30 s holds + 20 s releases + 30 s instruction. | 20 s side change. | 1.67 |
| S2 | 60 s work + 45 s instruction. | 20 s side change. | 2.08 |
| Stabilization transitions | No extra work. | 45 s between rows + 60 s before P1 preparation. | 1.75 |
| P1 | 24 s preparation + 60 s working + 90 s setup/instruction. | 30 + 60 s preparation; 2 × 60 s side changes + 120 s round rest. | 8.40 |
| P2 | 24 s preparation + 36 s working + 90 s setup/instruction. | 60 + 90 s preparation; 120 s working-set rest. | 7.00 |
| P3 | 24 s preparation + 48 s working + 75 s setup/instruction. | 30 + 45 s preparation; 45 s working side change. | 4.45 |
| P4 | 10 s preparation + 40 s working + 60 s instruction. | 45 s before work. | 2.58 |
| P5 | 20 s preparation + 40 s working + 60 s setup/instruction. | 45 s before work. | 2.75 |
| P6 | 25 s preparation + 80 s working + 75 s setup/instruction. | 60 s before work + 90 s between working sets. | 5.50 |
| Primary transitions | Instruction allowances above describe time beyond the baseline inter-exercise recovery if needed; do not add them a second time at delivery. | 2 × 120 s + 3 × 90 s before next preparation; none after final P6 set. | 8.50 |

**Modeled totals:** explosiveness **30.37 min**; stabilization **5.50 min**; primary **39.18 min**; combined **75.05 min**. Round to a **75–85-minute planning allowance outside Access & Prepare 1**, with the upper end for routine load adjustment/recording. The model deliberately reserves some instruction time beyond pure recovery; if instruction fits inside the rest, count only the actual elapsed time. Replacements add roughly one minute each where noted in the ledger. Extra preparation sets, extended recovery or material teaching needs are outside the nominal clock.

A **60-minute whole-session booking is incompatible with this version**. A 90-minute booking cannot be confirmed without the preparation duration and group model. No current booking was supplied, so there is no established window to falsely claim this meets. If a window is later supplied, revise dose and delivery together while preserving fourteen meaningful entries and necessary rest; do not delete rows or squeeze recovery.

## Group delivery feasibility

- **Start example only, not confirmed staffing/capacity:** a pod of three takes successive scheduled starts 30 s apart. If each start/ease-down takes about 10 s, that athlete receives about 80 s recovery before its next start, meeting the 75 s minimum. After each athlete's second start, delay that athlete's next start until at least 120 s after its finish. Every returning athlete must be clear before the next one moves. Longer clearances or stops lengthen the schedule.
- The first controlled pair still applies individually. Do not race side by side, launch through a returning athlete, or replace walking recovery with extra drills. Coach must be able to observe each start.
- For strength, the modeled time assumes prompt access to each individual's qualified loads and support. Shared dumbbells/bench, differing loads and side-specific sets can create queues; the fact that one pair rests does not establish another can lift safely in the same area. Use actual cohort/equipment counts before promising a group duration.
- Initial qualified coaching coverage is required for starts, unilateral jumps, swings and loaded lifting. If one coach cannot observe concurrent tasks, serialize them and extend time. Do not assume three lanes equal three staffed stations.

## Acceptance review

| Requirement | Result |
|---|---|
| Correct focus and framework | Sprinting category-wide request; all seven categories/subcategories reproduced unchanged in curriculum. |
| Correct next class | No previous Sprinting progress found; only Class 1 fully written. |
| Existing preparation | Exact Access & Prepare 1 reference; no authored content or invented duration. |
| Exact architecture | Four ordered sections, six explosive rows, two light rows, six primary rows. |
| Purposeful work | Fourteen nonzero entries; alternatives explicitly replace one slot; no hidden circuits. |
| Doses/recovery/loading | Counts, sides, rep/cycle definitions, RIR, ramps, resets and stop/regress criteria specified. |
| Relevance/overlap | Direct start practice protected; posterior-chain and ankle overlap acknowledged and limited; no unrelated lift filler. |
| Equipment/space | Defaults use listed categories in a 10 m footprint; fit, width, clearance and group quantities conditional. |
| Timing | Explicit model includes recovery, ramps and transitions; whole-session/group duration remains unresolved. |
| Progression and uniqueness | New-drill preference saved; recurring strength allowed; no prescribed-to-observed conversion or cross-drill performance comparison. |
| Evidence | Primary biomechanical research and official specialist guidance support limited rationale; OTA supplies style inspiration, not validation of the complete session. |
| Save/handoff | Class, map, ledger, history, feedback and state saved; file/count/reference check recorded separately in verification.json. |

**Unresolved operational assumptions:** athlete readiness and recent/next load; actual preparation time/content; 10 m versus 12 m facility record; lane width/return/waiting locations; equipment weights/quantities, bench/box fit and bell clearance; cohort size/staffing/booking; actual response. None is presented as confirmed. These are delivery conditions, not a request to assume a full twelve-class program is complete.

# Class 11 — sources and exercise identity

**Reviewed 2026-09-13.** The user's Sprinting scope, exact seven-category framework, existing Access & Prepare 1 and 6/2/6 govern. The latest request favors useful drill uniqueness while allowing strength recurrence. Sources inform selected mechanical jobs; none establishes readiness, actual completion or efficacy of this entire session.

## Evidence used and limits

| Source | Contribution | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [OTA — Best Single Leg Plyometrics for Football Athletes](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/best-single-leg-plyometrics-for-football-athletes/) | Describes forward same-leg takeoff/reception within its double-broad example. | Class 11 uses isolated modest jumps and held receivers, not the second linked jump or the source's broader performance/injury claims. Four local attempts are not an OTA validated youth dose. |
| [OTA — Ballistics Training for Athletes](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/ballistics-training-for-athletes-how-to-build-total-body-explosiveness-power/) | Includes forward scoop throws as a horizontal force-expression tool. | The retained split base, four throws, floor target and containment are authored local constraints. No claim of faster sprint splits follows from a throw or a new stance. |
| [OTA — Power and Mechanics Drills to Sprint Faster](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/power-and-mechanics-sprint/) | Provides a coordination rationale for opposing thigh/arm action and controlled lower-leg release. | E4's isolated unsupported exchange is a proposed variant; E5/E6 use earlier curriculum definitions. Do not import long traveling skips, exaggerated pulling/kicking, fixed adaptation timelines or claims that a drill reproduces top-speed running. |
| [Pain and Hibbs — Sprint starts and the minimum auditory reaction time](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17127583/) | Separates an external auditory signal from measured movement/force onset in instrumented sprint starts. | This class uses a coach's qualitative observation, not synchronized blocks/EMG or a millisecond threshold. The adult study does not validate the local youth dose or allow a reaction-time claim from ordinary timing gates. |

General supervised youth-strength and hip/ankle evidence remains in the [initial source register](sources_and_exercises.md). Today’s 2–3 technical RIR and light RPE 3–4 are prescription targets, not observed athlete results.

## Local library review

Read `docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv` and the local generated research record `scripts/data/canonical-research/generated/split-stance-auditory-sprint-start.v1.json`. The existing **Split-Stance Auditory Sprint Start / split-stance-auditory-sprint-start** name and slug are verified locally. The research record identifies a static staggered two-point stance with one sound-to-forward response and flags gaps in the underlying card's procedure/media. It is review evidence, not proof of live publication or an exact approved demonstration. Our four opportunities, 2–4 s waits, 1 m origin, short drive, stopping and no-make-up rules are explicit local programming; its longer route and accepted-reaction volume are not copied.

The local CSV also lists **Arm Action Drill — Seated or Standing / arm-action-drill** and **Sprint Arm Action Switches / sprint-arm-action-switches**. Use the former family for E6; no new identity is created by choosing its standing form. No exact generated matches were found for the other searched variant names. Earlier identity notes remain the source for their families. No invented database IDs, live publication claims or exercise-record edits.

| Slot | Identity and novelty decision |
|---|---|
| E1 Split-Stance Auditory Sprint Start | Verified local family name/slug. **New curriculum task constraint:** wait for one external cue instead of self-selecting onset. The two-point movement family recurs; this is not a newly invented start mechanic or a direction-choice drill. |
| E2 Single-Leg Broad to Same-Leg Stick | **Proposed isolated variant:** same-leg horizontal takeoff/receiver differs from earlier two-foot/opposite-leg receivers and same-leg vertical jumps. The linked version in OTA is not prescribed. |
| E3 Split-Stance Forward Scoop Toss | **Proposed related stance variant:** retain offset foot support through an external forward release, unlike Class 8's parallel origin. This earns a staggered force-transfer job; changed ball mass would not earn novelty. |
| E4 Standing A-Switch to Stick | **Proposed isolated unsupported variant:** initiate one low airborne support exchange, hold and reset. Unlike continuous A-run or externally supported wall switches, each attempt ends in upright individual support before another begins. |
| E5 Standing Single-Leg Cycle and Strike | **Intentional Class 3 default recurrence**, same six cycles and rests. Full free-leg recovery with no support-foot exchange remains useful; replacing it with a more complex airborne cycle would add demand without established need. |
| E6 Standing Arm Action Drill | **Intentional Class 4 contingency recurrence**, same eight exchanges and 75 s rest. Its direct arm-timing job avoids another impact task. Seated fallback also recurs. |
| S1/S2, P1–P6 | Same strengthening identities; all doses/preparation held from Class 10 except P6 2 × 8 → 1 × 8. A planned volume reduction, not evidence that a deload was needed or completed. |

Four proposed task variants and two declared recurring families are an honest inventory, not six unrelated new movements. All earlier defaults and contingencies were reviewed. Actual previous technique could establish additional overlap and must be recorded if reported.

## Substitution and practical boundaries

Self-starts, shared broad receivers, parallel tosses, parked swings/rapid bilateral bridges, simplified downstrokes and seated arms are declared earlier families. E4's nonflight exchange changes whole-body support; E5 retains a planted support foot and a full cycle, so they do not become duplicate slots. E2's horizontal receiver remains distinct from E4's low in-place exchange. Every alternative replaces its slot; none is an extra exercise.

Cue audibility, coach position, whole start footprint, same-leg receiver competence, ball grip/floor rating/bounce/roll behavior, lane width and all station/group arrangements remain unconfirmed. Use defined replacements when the default cannot be qualified. The user/spec’s ten-metre constraint governs over the separate twelve-metre/eight-tenet reference. Actual maximum-velocity running remains unavailable. No external athlete account or application data was edited.

# Class 7 — sources and exercise identities

Reviewed 2026-09-13. Exact doses, seated lane geometry, floor adaptations and replacements are authored here. Sources inform components, not validation of this complete youth session or guaranteed sprint transfer.

## Evidence and coaching inspiration

- [Overtime Athletes: Three Single-Leg Plyometric Exercises](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/3-single-leg-plyometric-exercises-for-more-bounce/) discusses forceful seated jump initiation without rocking and permits removing a receiving box. Class 7 uses the broader settled-support idea; its bilateral seated forward jump, seated start and short layout are local adaptations, not exercises or doses copied from that article.
- [Overtime Athletes: Isometric Training](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/isometrics-training-for-athletes-build-elite-strength-and-joint-resilience/) distinguishes force against an immovable object from sustained position holds. Class 7 chooses brief submaximal rapid-onset pulses; it does not import the article's long maximal efforts, therapeutic claims or claims that such work lacks joint stress.
- [Balshaw et al., 2016, Journal of Applied Physiology](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/japplphysiol.00091.2016) compared brief explosive and sustained isometric knee-extension training in healthy young men. This supports distinguishing force-onset intent from a prolonged hold. It did not test six submaximal wall pulses in ages 12–14 or sprint outcomes. The current entry dose/posture is a programming inference, not that study's protocol, and no force-onset measurement is available here.
- [Overtime Athletes: Five Explosive Exercises](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/5-explosive-exercises/) informs the single-leg forward-push/two-foot-reception family. The two-second unilateral pause is an authored constraint. A pause reduces preceding motion but does not prove all muscle/tendon action is purely concentric.
- The retained swing uses the previously reviewed [StrongFirst parked-swing guidance](https://www.strongfirst.com/the-kur-for-your-kettlebell-swing-and-clean/). Its recurrence is explicit; no new source is claimed to justify changing the name or load. Earlier hip/ankle/knee-flexor strength rationales and youth loading limits remain in the [initial source register](sources_and_exercises.md) and [Class 6 notes](class_06_sources_and_exercises.md).

The THIRST seated-broad-jump search result supplied name-level coaching evidence, but its full page timed out; no unseen execution instruction or outcome is attributed to it. Seated-start mechanics are locally authored. No inaccessible material is treated as reviewed evidence.

## Library identity checks

Inspected `docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv` for seated, wall, calf, paused and jump families, plus earlier identity records/history. No exact rapid-pulse or seated-start definition was verified. No identifiers are invented and no library/application records are edited.

| Slot | Local evidence | Binding decision |
|---|---|---|
| E1 seated start | No exact seated-start entry found in inspected CSV | **Proposed addition:** seat-to-foot support transfer into two-step running. Full class defines toe line, drive/stop bounds, seat fit and no rocking/hand push. |
| E2 seated broad | Related `seated-box-jump` found; prior seated vertical proposal documented | **Proposed explicit variant:** bilateral seated forward takeoff to floor, no receiving box. Do not bind to a box-jump record based on the word seated. |
| E3 paused unilateral broad | Prior single-leg broad/two-foot-reception family | **Proposed paused variant**, natural arm drive from a still start. Same landing family with a changed takeoff constraint; not a newly invented base exercise or direct distance comparison. |
| E4 wall force pulse | `wall-push-overcoming-iso`, `wall-drive-sprint-iso-hold`, `wall-drive-iso-hold` found by name | **Proposed rapid submaximal pulse prescription.** Exact one-second timing, split-foot pressure and effort are not inferred from these names. No external movement power or measured RFD is claimed. |
| E5 repeated same-leg wall knee drive | `wall-drill-march`, `wall-drill-iso-lean-march`, `wall-drill-fast-switch` found | **Proposed repeated-same-leg variant:** support foot fixed, rapid lift and controlled return. Not an alternating fast switch or wall pogo. |
| E6 dead-stop swing | Class 6's explicit parked-single variant | **Intentional recurrence**, same two sets of three; no uniqueness credit. Retain its prior family/implementation qualifications. |
| S1/S2 and P1–P6 | Prior source/variant register | All strengthening identities and doses held. Actual loads are unknown and selected for technical reserve. |

Generated exact records for the searched wall-pulse/march names were not located in the inspected generated directory, so CSV presence is only family/name evidence. No live database, athlete account, media approval or force-device capability was inspected.

## Limits and fallback record

Seat fit/stability, wall, DB/KB sizes, surface and staffing remain unconfirmed. Default seated starts use feet at 1 m and at most 8 m outward travel; standing fallback uses 0 m and at most 9 m. Each preserves a final clear metre. No full-speed runway is implied.

Earlier default/contingency families intentionally recur for equipment/readiness. E4 and E6 have different fallback exercises, preserving distinct jobs if both are replaced. All actual use, completion and recovery remain unknown. The 76–86 minute individual allowance excludes existing Access & Prepare 1 and extra delays; it does not establish full-session/group fit.

# Class 3 — source and exercise register

**Reviewed 2026-09-13.** The [original register](sources_and_exercises.md) retains primary hip/ankle biomechanics and official youth-resistance guidance. Its evidence supports intended mechanical jobs, not the exact session or a guaranteed sprint improvement. Class 3 makes no new quantitative transfer, injury-prevention or performance claim.

## Additional style and local evidence

[Overtime Athletes — Step-Up Variations for Explosive Athletes](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/the-best-step-ups-exercise-variations-for-explosive-athletes/) distinguishes controlled strengthening and rapid step-up tasks. It informs E2's leg-drive/free-thigh job. Our nonflight six-rep adaptation avoids the article's more demanding launches and their elevated landings; its outcome promises are not adopted.

[Overtime Athletes — Sprint Mechanics for Maximum Speed: Volume 2](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/sprint-mechanics-for-maximum-speed/) discusses foot recovery, placement and single-leg cycling, informing E5's isolated cycle/strike job. The stationary planted-support execution, three repetitions per leg and absence of a subsequent sprint are declared adaptations. The source favors repetition of useful drills; the user's later preference for distinct drills governs this curriculum's selection. Neither source validates this fourteen-entry class.

Local names/keys were checked in [`docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv`](../../../docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv). Selected generated records clarify identity boundaries. This is repository evidence, not confirmation of live approval, publishing or athlete eligibility. No IDs or library records are created by this plan.

| Slot | Local evidence | Exact class interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| E1 Three-Point Start Acceleration | `three-point-start-acceleration`; [generated record](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/generated/three-point-start-acceleration.v1.json) describes a static grounded-hand start over a longer route | **Proposed two-step prescription**, not an exact binding to a 5–10-yard or 10–20 m sprint. Grounded hand is explicitly opposite the front leg; preserve actual hand/foot choice and stopping geometry in feedback. |
| E2 Rapid Step-Up to Knee Drive, no flight | Related local `step-up`, `bodyweight-step-up`, `sprinter-step-up-jump` | **Proposed rapid nonflight execution.** The step-up jump identity is not an exact match. Working foot stays on a fitted low box, free thigh recovers and returns under control. |
| E3 Forward Bound to Opposite-Leg Stick | Related local `bound-to-stick`; `forward-hop-to-stick-low-amplitude` also exists | **Proposed explicit opposite-leg reception**, no exact current variant binding asserted. Do not substitute a same-leg hop or lateral bound merely because the library name is nearby. |
| E4 Broad Jump to Stick | Canonical common name/key `broad-jump-to-stick` | Natural countermovement/arms, parallel two-foot takeoff and held landing. Exact natural-arm execution is declared; no live variant assertion. It differs from the paused no-arm Class 1 prescription. |
| E5 Standing Single-Leg Cycle and Strike | Specialist cycling guidance above; no exact local stationary planted-support binding verified | **Proposed drill.** Other support foot stays planted, full compact recovery leads to one quick target-foot strike. No supporting-leg hop, travel or timed endurance bout. |
| E6 Supine Banded Knee Drive | Related local `banded-hip-flexor-march` | **Proposed supine rapid-drive variant**, not silently bound to a standing march. The nonmoving leg stays long with its heel grounded; the other knee drives toward the torso against increasing band tension, then lowers slowly. Check resistance direction, heel traction, closed-loop fit and light load. The unresisted fallback has different resistance. |
| S1/S2 and P1–P6 | Same identities/declared variants as the [Class 1 register](sources_and_exercises.md) | All recur for relevant jobs. RDL working sets fall from two to one; walkout cycles from four to three. Other prescriptions and all preparation doses remain unchanged. Actual historical load/lever is unknown. |

The inspected [straight-leg-bound/march research record](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/generated/straight-leg-bound-march.v1.json) flags a conflation between no-flight marching and flight-based bounding. That ambiguous card was not used as a convenient binding or exercise slot. E5 defines its own nontraveling, planted-support cycle and fast strike precisely.

**Replacements:** Standing two-point start, same-lead split jump and single-leg broad to two-foot landing deliberately recur from prior classes only under the stated comfort/equipment/receiving-control conditions. Unresisted supine knee drive removes external resistance while retaining the same rapid-drive task. Supported unilateral calf and fitted-seat/short-foot changes keep the earlier declared rules. Record actual identity and altered contact types; none is additional work.

**Unknowns after review:** Actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness/recovery, outside sport/gym/tumbling, preparation content/time, lane width and actual 10 m/12 m discrepancy, low-box/seat dimensions, closed-band suitability, group/staff/booking. No test equipment is assumed necessary, and no top-speed result is inferred from any gym drill.

# Class 2 — sources and exercise identity check

**Reviewed 2026-09-13.** The [original register](sources_and_exercises.md) continues to document the overall biomechanical rationale, youth guidance and retained strength identities. New sources below support limited drill-selection rationale. They do not validate this complete class or show that these athletes improved.

## Additional coaching sources

- [Overtime Athletes — Increase Your Quickness with 3 Acceleration Drills](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/increase-your-quickness-with-3-acceleration-drills/): wall-supported leg exchanges and start mechanics inspired E2's job. Class 2 uses isolated exchanges, a verified-support condition and a floor fallback; it does not import universal body angles, aggressive clawing cues or outcome promises.
- [Overtime Athletes — Pro Level Plyometrics Training Pt. 1](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/pro-level-plyometrics-training-pt-1/): supports the stylistic distinction between unilateral power and seated leg-extension tasks. The article's elite sequence, obstacles, repeated bounds, drop-rebound work and competition are not copied into this youth prescription.
- [Catalyst Athletics — Seated Vertical Jump](https://www.catalystathletics.com/exercise/624/Seated-Vertical-Jump/): official exercise guidance for using supported sitting before a jump. The intended reduction in countermovement contribution explains E3; it does not establish a measured sprint benefit or prove all elastic contribution is absent in an actual attempt.
- [OTA's previously reviewed speed-drill article](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/soccer-speed-drills/) includes a half-kneeling start. The shorter two-step/3 m driving boundary and four-attempt dose are authored for this facility. They are not the article's tested intervention or a full acceleration exposure.

Stationary low dribbling is a constrained coordination adaptation of the locally researched traveling drill. No new research result is claimed for that adaptation. Existing hip/ankle biomechanics sources inform intended capacity roles only; the class requires athlete response and coaching judgment, not an assumed transfer coefficient.

## Class 2 local identity review

Local evidence comes from [`docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv`](../../../docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv) and the inspected generated research records. A local name/slug does not establish current live publication, eligibility or an exact variant binding. Useful unverified variants are labeled proposed; no IDs were fabricated or library records edited.

| Slot | Local evidence | Binding/interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| E1 Half-Kneeling Sprint Start | CSV name `Half-Kneeling Sprint Start`, slug `half-kneeling-sprint-start` | Related identity exists. **Proposed short-step prescription**: rear knee down, comfortable floor support, two driving contacts/by 3 m then slowing; no exact current canonical variant asserted. Do not substitute an existing longer-distance card. |
| E2 Wall Drill Fast Switch | CSV name and slug `wall-drill-fast-switch` | Name verified; exact isolated-single-exchange/hold/reset dose is the class prescription. A suitable wall is unconfirmed and must be inspected. No current live binding claimed. |
| E3 Seated Vertical Jump to Floor Landing | Specialist exercise guidance above; no exact local name/variant verified in the scoped search | **Proposed addition**, no invented ID. Stable seat before takeoff, floor landing, no second box or hurdle; exact origin and finish matter. |
| E4 Split Squat Jump to Stick, same lead | Related CSV `Split Jump / Scissor Jump`, slug `split-jump-scissor-jump` | **Proposed non-scissoring variant**. Do not bind it to a card requiring lead-leg exchange or continuous alternating jumps. |
| E5 Single-Leg Pogo, final same-leg hold | Local `single-leg-pogo`; [generated family record](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/generated/single-leg-hop-pogo-identity/single-leg-pogo.v1.json) describes `stationary-low-amplitude-to-terminal-stick` | Same-leg repeated contacts with only the final contact held are explicitly represented. Class prescribes three contacts/leg, two-second final hold and a gentle opposite-foot set-down; no live publication assertion. |
| E6 Stationary Low Dribble Run | CSV `low-dribble-run`; [generated record](../../../scripts/data/canonical-research/generated/low-dribble-run.v1.json) describes traveling alternating compact foot cycles | **Proposed stationary adaptation**. Record contact-count dose and lack of travel; do not claim the traveling lane card is an exact match. Not an A-skip, high-dribble drill or maximum-speed run. |
| S1/S2 and P1–P6 | Same identities and declared variants as Class 1 | Refer to [original mapping](sources_and_exercises.md); all doses and primary loading targets retained. Actual previous loads remain unknown. |

**Replacement record:** High-Plank Single-Switch Knee Drive is a proposed floor-supported rapid-exchange replacement, not a wall drill under a different name. Squat Jump to Stick is a declared unsupported static-origin replacement; no current variant binding is claimed. Low two-point standing start and bilateral Ankle Pogo in Place recur from Class 1's families only when the documented comfort/readiness condition requires them. One-step start reduces drive opportunities within the same attempt; it does not create another slot. Supported single-leg P5, seated short-foot and fitted seat substitutions retain the earlier declared replacement rules.

**Uniqueness conclusion:** All six defaults differ from Class 1 by meaningful starting support, laterality, force direction or cyclic coordination. Their labels alone are not the evidence; the audit and history spell out the changed jobs. Necessary fallback recurrence is disclosed rather than relabeled. Nothing in this review establishes performance improvement across different drills.

# Class 10 — design and audit

**2026-09-13. Previous goal turn: progress.** Class 9 and updated state exist. All Class 9 checkpoint hashes match, referenced files exist and the saved specification matches the original. Reviewed Classes 1–9, start/upright and strength anchors, workload, default/contingency history, audits/source notes, equipment and feedback. No actual athlete results were supplied. Only Class 10 is finalized.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Initiate forward force from a compact hand-free base, then support prompt free-leg recovery and nearby subsequent contacts.
2. **Demand:** Transfer from a two-foot starting base to individual support while retaining body alignment; practice upright recovery separately within stationary space.
3. **Anchor:** Four static bent-over starts, observing first stepping foot, forward push without a backward step, body position and stopping. Use the scheduled attempts only.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Forward projection while retaining a split receiver; shared takeoff into one-leg reception; alternating upright step-over recovery; two linked inclined exchanges; brief resisted thigh recovery over a planted support foot. Retained strength supports these same demands.
5. **Constraints:** Exact 6/2/6, existing Access & Prepare 1, supervised ages 12–14 baseline competence, ten-metre footprint, unknown actual response and preference for meaningful uniqueness. Short starts cannot be stretched into maximum-velocity running.

## Selection and revision

| Issue | Final decision and reason |
|---|---|
| Start origin | Use a still parallel-foot hip hinge with both hands free. This differs from the staggered two-point start, Class 6's whole-body falling entry and Class 8's hand-supported crouch. OTA names bent-over starts, but the exact local stance, intent and boundaries are authored here. No backward loading step, kick-up or extra approach. |
| Space | Toes begin at 1 m; fit the body inside 0–2 m. Drive at most two strikes/3 m, ending by 4 m, then stop by 9 m. Standing fallback keeps the same front-toe line. The eight-metre outward bound is measured from that declared toe origin, not an exact centre-of-mass trajectory. |
| Horizontal projection | A split takeoff and same-lead split receiver retains the offset through forward force. Class 6 ended parallel; Class 8 began parallel and ended split; earlier same-lead split jumps were vertical. The receiver constraint earns this related variant, not its name alone. Four jumps, modest distance. |
| Individual support | A small two-foot vertical takeoff into a single-leg stick separates the shared push from individual reception. It is the inverse support transition of Class 5's unilateral takeoff/shared receiver. This is not a running stride simulation. Keep height modest and qualify the single-leg receiver; no external drop or high jump. |
| Upright allocation | Use eight alternating step-over contacts, reduced from the preceding upright day's twelve running contacts because starts and individual receivers return. Both legs use the recovery/release pattern, unlike Class 6's asymmetric step-over drill. Actual earlier technique may overlap; different titles do not prove a new athlete experience. |
| Intentional recurrence | Retain **Class 8's Wall Drill Double Switch**, same four pairs/eight fast contacts and recovery. It directly links two support exchanges under a controlled forward body line. A longer wall run or additional airborne switch was not better justified; no new identity or uniqueness credit is claimed for this slot. |
| Resisted recovery | Use a very light closed foot-loop band for a standing repeated knee drive. Compared with Class 3's supine band drive, body mass is now supported over one foot; compared with Class 7's wall drive, the torso is upright without fixed-arm support and the moving leg meets light resistance. This is a proposed related variant, not novelty from a heavier band. Reject the extra knee-extension action and unverified external anchor in the source example. |
| Band replacement | If loop fit, traction, speed or stance control cannot be qualified, use the earlier supine unresisted knee drive. This preserves a rapid thigh job with a different support demand and avoids duplicating E4's possible standing march in E6. No improvised loop/anchor. |
| Strength overlap | Hold all eight strengthening identities, working/preparation doses and rests. The single split-squat and RDL working rounds and three walkout cycles stay reduced; starts/new receiver types do not earn restored volume. P1/P2 support leg/hip push, P3 free-thigh force, P4 knee-flexor capacity and P5/P6 ankle force at different knee positions. |

## Prescription accounting and progression

| Entry | Default exposure |
|---|---|
| E1 | Four starts, two/first stepping foot. At most eight driving strikes and 12 m drive, contained within **32 m maximum outward travel** from line 1 to line 9 across four attempts. Four stopping episodes; actual slowing/return contacts unknown. |
| E2 | Four bilateral horizontal takeoffs and four split bilateral landings, two/lead. Each is held, with no rebound. |
| E3 | Four bilateral vertical takeoffs into four unilateral landings, two/receiving leg, followed by four gentle free-foot set-downs. |
| E4 | Eight upright running contacts, four/foot, plus one controlled finish set-down. |
| E5 | Four double-switch pairs = eight fast supported contacts, four/foot, plus four controlled set-downs, two/foot. Same prescription as Class 8. |
| E6 | Six resisted standing knee drives, three/leg, plus six controlled foot returns. Support foot stays planted; no flight. |

**Jump subtotal: eight events — four bilateral and four unilateral receivers, giving 12 landing foot impacts.** The four additional E3 free-foot set-downs are separate. No repeated pogo/rebound block, throw, swing, wall-force pulse or actual maximum-velocity run. Start contacts, stationary running, wall contacts, band returns and gentle set-downs are not equal loading units.

Class 9 had eight bilateral jump/pogo receivers and twelve upright contacts, without starts. Class 10 has four unilateral receivers, eight upright contacts, returned starts and wall exchanges, and light resisted thigh work. A lower landing-foot count does not mean a lower tissue load. This is a redistribution to match the primary effort, conditional on current competence, not evidence of earned progression. No greater height, distance, speed, lean or band tension is prescribed from saved class count.

Light work: **2 rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps + 30 foot-seconds**. Primary: **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 54 dynamic reps + 3 walkout cycles** (24 heel steps). Preparation: **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps + 1 short-lever cycle** (eight heel steps). Actual loads, preparation exposure and outside sport/gym/tumbling remain unknown.

Continuity is **Class 9 strength prescription → identical Class 10 dose → retain direct capacity without increasing overlap → change only after actual clean work at target reserve and adequate subsequent recovery**. E5 continuity is **Class 8 paired wall prescription → same Class 10 prescription → useful two-contact support task → retain or simplify based on actual posture/rhythm; do not lengthen automatically**. Neither earlier prescription proves an exposure occurred. Primary remains 2–3 technical RIR; light work RPE 3–4. The band stays light enough for a fast controlled lift, not a challenging strength set.

Hold with missing feedback; use the first scheduled attempts to qualify the current entry demand. Persistent faults despite adjustment end the task; pain, slipping, changed gait or lost control stop it immediately. Failed/partial/omitted work is logged without make-up attempts. Future changes need actual evidence and matched comparison conditions.

## Replacement effects and duplication

- Standing E1 retains four starts, 1 m front-toe origin and the same drive/stop bounds. If all are one-step starts, driving strikes cap at four; actual distance remains observed.
- Parallel-receiver or parallel-origin broad E2 retains four bilateral receivers but loses a split constraint; these repeat Classes 6/3 respectively. They remain horizontal, distinct from E3's vertical replacement.
- Bilateral-receiver E3 replaces four unilateral landings with four bilateral landings, making **eight bilateral jump events / 16 landing foot impacts** if E2 stays default; four separate free-foot set-downs are removed. This is an earlier CMJ fallback family, not equal loading.
- A-run E4 keeps eight running contacts plus one finish set-down; A-march gives eight controlled returns without the extra running finish. These are earlier families.
- Isolated wall E5 keeps eight fast contacts but produces eight controlled set-downs, rather than four, because posture is released after each exchange. The high-plank alternative gives eight fast extending-foot contacts; the forward foot hovers and knees lower for rest. Record setup/knee contacts separately and allow extra setup time. Earlier Class 2 families; no pairs added afterward.
- Supine unresisted E6 gives six knee drives and six gentle heel placements instead of six resisted standing drives/returns. Body support and resistance change; the foot counts do not imply equivalent impact. Explicit Class 3 fallback recurrence.
- Supported unilateral P5 gives **10 primary bouts / 56 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, and **10 preparation bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**, about one extra minute. All alternatives replace their slots; none duplicates another default/replacement in the intended paths.

## Timing and delivery

Individual prompt equipment access. Work/teaching allowances are estimates; rests are prescribed. Teaching/setup can occupy recovery, counted once; additional setup, ramps or recovery extend the model.

| Task | Work/teaching allowance | Recovery | Seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 4 × 12 s start/slowing + 120 s stance/layout teaching | 2 × 75 s + 120 s | 438 |
| E2 | 4 × 6 s jump/hold + 90 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 60 s lead change | 214 |
| E3 | 4 × 6 s jump/hold/set-down + 120 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 60 s leg change | 244 |
| E4 | About 5 s eight contacts/finish + 120 s teaching | Next transition | 125 |
| E5 | 4 × 4 s pairs/holds/set-downs + 90 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 45 s side change | 191 |
| E6 | 6 × 4 s drive/hold/lower + 150 s band fitting/removal/teaching | 4 × 10 s + 45 s side change | 259 |
| E transitions through S1 | Setup may occupy rest | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s | 480 |
| **Explosiveness** | | | **1,951** |
| S1/S2 and transitions | 225 s work/teaching/side changes | 45 s between + 60 s after | **330** |
| P1 | Prep 24 s + work 30 s + teaching 90 s | 30 s prep sides + 60 s prework + 60 s work sides | 294 |
| P2 | Prep 24 s + work 18 s + teaching 90 s | 60 s between ramps + 90 s prework | 282 |
| P3 | Prep 24 s + work 48 s + teaching 75 s | 30 s prep sides + 45 s prework + 45 s work sides | 267 |
| P4 | Prep 10 s + work 30 s + teaching 60 s | 45 s prework | 145 |
| P5 | Prep 20 s + work 40 s + teaching 60 s | 45 s prework | 165 |
| P6 | Prep 25 s + work 80 s + teaching 75 s | 60 s prework + 90 s sets | 330 |
| P transitions | Setup may occupy rest | 2 × 120 s + 3 × 90 s | 510 |
| **Primary** | | | **1,993** |
| **Total outside Access & Prepare 1** | | | **4,274 s = 71.2 min** |

Allow **72–82 minutes after Access & Prepare 1**, plus extra delays. A 60-minute complete booking cannot fit. Preparation, booking, staff/group size and station flow remain unknown, so complete-session/group fit is unresolved. No assumed simultaneous stations or unsupervised youth lifting; group waiting supplies recovery only when actual intervals meet the prescribed rest.

Verify the whole start footprint, stopping control, lane width and closed return route. Protect jump receivers, upright drill space and wall/band stations from cross-traffic. The band must be an intact suitable closed loop around shoe midfeet with secure traction and stretch allowance; it must oppose the knee lift while the other foot stays flat. No unverified anchor, knot or added loop is assumed. Use the floor replacement if fitting or speed cannot be qualified. The separate 10 m/12 m facility discrepancy remains unresolved; use ten metres.

Review actual sport, gym, sprinting, other classes and separate tumbling when scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between demanding lower-body exposures is only a planning starting point; actual response and surrounding workload govern. The short-start and stationary tasks do not replace top-speed running.

## Handoff

Save Class 10 and map/ledger/history/feedback/state/source/verification updates; preserve Classes 1–9 and archive Class 9's verification. Next run: review all saved work and available actual feedback, then finalize **Class 11 only**. Consolidate repeatable start/support mechanics with fatigue controlled, using actual quality, reserve and the surrounding schedule to select the allocation. Do not write Classes 11–12 now. Class 12 must still receive the full-sequence audit.

# Class 11 — design and audit

**2026-09-13. Previous goal turn: progress.** Class 10 and shared state exist. All Class 10 checkpoint hashes and state paths verified; the snapshot matches the original supplied specification. Reviewed the map, Class 10, relevant earlier start/strength/placement/arm anchors, Classes 1–10 default/contingency history, workload, source/audit records, equipment and feedback. No new actual athlete response was supplied. No applicable AGENTS.md was found in checked ancestors or workout_plan. Finalize Class 11 only.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Initiate a clean forward push on one clear signal, then organize individual support and limb recovery without long drill bouts.
2. **Demand:** Keep a prepared staggered base until the cue, then express force without guessing, reaching or losing subsequent support.
3. **Anchor:** Four split-stance auditory start opportunities with one known forward response. Record cue-relative initiation, body control and stopping within those attempts.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Same-leg forward force acceptance; staggered external release; isolated upright support exchange; full free-leg recovery/placement with one foot planted; rapid arms while the trunk stays quiet. Strength supports leg/hip push, knee recovery and ankle force.
5. **Constraints:** Exact 6/2/6, existing preparation, supervised ages 12–14 with established basics, ten-metre footprint, useful uniqueness and unknown actual attendance/readiness. No reaction-time measurement or true maximum-velocity run is claimed.

## Selection, audit findings and revisions

| Question | Final decision and rationale |
|---|---|
| How to consolidate starts without another arbitrary stance? | Use the locally named split-stance auditory start. It retains a known two-point movement but adds a meaningful externally controlled onset. One non-startling verbal cue means straight forward; no feints, multiple choices or directional cuts. This is a task variant, not novel start kinematics. |
| Does the main task get enough quality practice? | Four opportunities, balanced front legs, full 75/120 s recovery and first-pair stopping qualification. Rejected a draft accepted-rep rule that could inflate attempts after guesses/misses. An early launch consumes an opportunity and uses controlled slowing; a missed cue is logged as no start. No forced abrupt stop or penalty repetition. |
| Is the new unilateral reception justified? | A modest isolated same-leg broad receiver links unilateral forward push/acceptance. Earlier unilateral forward jumps ended on both feet or the opposite foot; Class 10’s unilateral receivers were vertical. It is a new demand, not earned progression. Keep four isolated attempts with a shared-receiver replacement. Rejected a linked double broad because repeating the same-leg receiver would increase demand without response data. |
| Why the split scoop toss? | A forward external release loads coordinated leg/hip force while retaining the stagger; this differs from body projection and Class 8's parallel toss. Four throws avoid another jump block. No added catch, step, rotational target or heavier-ball progression. Actual containment determines feasibility. |
| Why isolated A-switches? | Four short flight exchanges allow a coach to observe the support position after each rapid exchange without adding another eight-to-twelve-contact running bout. This is a related resettable force/coordination task, not a new movement because of a lower rep count. Full holds/resets distinguish the task. |
| Why two recurring drill families? | Class 3’s full-cycle drill retains complete free-leg placement with no support exchange; Class 4’s standing-arm contingency retains quick opposing arms with no foot flight. A more complex airborne cycle or another jump/throw was less defensible for this consolidation. Declare both recurrences instead of renaming them. |
| Are E4/E5 redundant? | E4 transfers body support with one rapid thigh exchange; E5 holds the support foot down while the other leg completes recovery, release and placement. If E4 becomes a nonflight step/hold, it still transfers support. E5’s simplified downstroke removes the full cycle but still keeps the other foot planted. |
| Does six-strength architecture overload the finish? | Keep P1–P5 and preparation at Class 10 doses, retaining 2–3 technical RIR. Reduce P6 from two working sets to one: this removes eight dynamic reps and 130 modeled seconds while keeping a challenging flexed-knee ankle contribution. No claim of a completed deload or lower observed fatigue. |
| Are claims and comparisons matched? | Single-cue onset is observed qualitatively. No ordinary gate measurement is treated as reaction time. Same-leg broad distances are separate from bilateral/opposite-leg/vertical variants. Unknown loads, recovery and actual previous technique remain unknown. |

## Workload accounting

| Entry | Default prescribed exposure |
|---|---|
| E1 | Four cue opportunities / four planned starts, two/front leg; at most eight driving strikes and 12 m drive within 32 m maximum outward start/slowing travel. Front toes 1 m, setup inside 0–2 m, drive by 4 m, stop by 9 m. Four planned stopping episodes; actual return/slowing contacts unknown. |
| E2 | Four isolated forward same-leg takeoffs/landings, two/leg; four gentle free-foot set-downs after held receivers. |
| E3 | Four forward split-stance throws, two/lead; feet stay down. Ball retrieval is additional movement, not a throw or a sprint. |
| E4 | Four low in-place airborne support exchanges, two/receiving foot; four gentle free-foot set-downs. These are isolated flight events, not an additional continuous-running count. |
| E5 | Six nonflight complete recovery/strike cycles, three/moving foot. Support foot stays planted. |
| E6 | Eight arm exchanges; both arms reverse together on each rep. Zero added foot contacts. |

**Flight subtotal: eight unilateral events / eight landing foot impacts**, comprising four forward hops and four low upright exchanges. **Eight controlled free-foot set-downs** are separate. Zero continuous upright-running contacts, supported wall contacts/pulses, default swings and actual maximum-velocity runs. Starts, forward receivers, small upright exchanges, throws, cycle strikes and set-downs are not interchangeable load units.

Compared with Class 10, four starts remain, while mixed jump receivers/eight running contacts/eight wall contacts/band drives are replaced by this allocation. All eight current flight receivers are unilateral; changed event/foot counts do not establish lower tissue stress. Four throws replace part of the impact work but have their own demand. Qualify the new same-leg horizontal receiver rather than assuming Class 10 was performed.

### Strength continuity and next criteria

- S1 1 × 3 × 5 s/foot and S2 1 × 6/side: unchanged easy strengthening at RPE 3–4. **2 rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps + 30 foot-seconds.**
- P1 1 × 5/leg, P2 1 × 6, P3 1 × 6/leg, P4 1 × 3 cycles, P5 1 × 10: unchanged. P6 **Class 10 2 × 8 → Class 11 1 × 8** to limit planned ankle-strength overlap; preserve load qualification and 2–3 technical RIR.
- Primary: **6 rounds / 8 bouts / 46 dynamic reps + 3 walkout cycles** (24 heel steps). One written unilateral round includes two executed side bouts.
- Preparation unchanged: **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps + 1 short-lever walkout cycle** (eight heel steps). Actual additional ramps and existing preparation are not hidden in those totals.
- Future strength changes require actual clean reps at target reserve, matched load/range/tempo/leverage and adequate subsequent recovery. Without those observations, qualify/hold or reduce. Do not automatically restore P6’s second set for Class 12.
- E5 **Class 3 six cycles → same Class 11 dose/rest → full-cycle placement without extra flight → retain/simplify using actual control and recovery**. E6 **Class 4 standing contingency eight exchanges/75 s → same Class 11 prescription → direct low-impact arm role → retain/reduce using actual relaxed posture**. Earlier written prescriptions do not establish previous use.

## Replacement effects

- E1 self-start retains the layout and four-opportunity ceiling, removing the external-onset task. If all starts use one driving step, driving strikes cap at four. Missing/early opportunities are logged, not made up.
- E2 shared reception replaces four unilateral receivers with four bilateral receivers and removes four free-foot set-downs: with default E4, total **eight flight events / 12 landing foot impacts + four separate set-downs**. Bilateral-origin broad also changes takeoff support. Both repeat earlier families.
- E3 parallel toss keeps four releases but removes the split constraint. Parked swings give four floats instead of four throws; rapid bilateral bridges give four nonflight rises if bell setup also fails. No default throw, swing or bridge is added to another path.
- E4 nonflight step/hold removes four airborne receivers, replacing them with **four support-transfer placements + four finish set-downs**. E2 remains four forward flight events if unchanged. Do not label the replacements equal-impact units.
- E5 simplified downstroke retains six target-foot returns but changes the recovery path. E6 seated arms keeps eight exchanges/75 s rest with a different support position; both declared recurrences.
- Supported unilateral P5 gives **9 primary bouts / 48 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, and **10 preparation bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**, about one extra minute. Exact 1 × 6/leg work and 1 × 3/leg preparation are in the class.
- Replacing multiple slots does not duplicate another listed exercise in the stated paths. Record actual identities, side doses, contacts, extra setup, omissions and reasons.

## Timing model

Individual prompt equipment access; work and teaching allowances are estimates. Required rests are preserved and begin after retrieval where stated. Teaching/setup may occupy recovery, counted once; additional waits/ramps/clearance work extend the model.

A 60-minute complete booking cannot fit. Access & Prepare 1, booking, group/staff and station flow remain unknown; full-session/group feasibility remains unresolved.

# Class 6 — sources and exercise identities

Reviewed 2026-09-13. Sources inform particular mechanics and exercise choices; no source validates this exact session, youth dosage or guaranteed sprint-speed improvement.

## Coaching and evidence basis

- [Overtime Athletes: Falling Starts](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/falling-starts/) describes a whole-body lean leading into initial running steps. Class 6 uses an earlier controlled recovery step, four attempts and the established short driving/stopping limits. Near-fall cues, toe stabbing, aerodynamic explanations and guaranteed outcomes are not adopted.
- [Overtime Athletes: Five Explosive Exercises](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/5-explosive-exercises/) describes staggered broad takeoff and a two-foot finish. Class 6 uses modest distance/offset and both front-leg configurations. Source claims of immediate sprint improvements and maximal distances are not imported.
- [Overtime Athletes: Top Speed Training Progression](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/use-this-top-speed-training-progression/) describes a step-over recovery between high-knee work and fuller cycling. Class 6 adapts the release to stationary asymmetric running, two cycles per target. A literal obstacle, aggressive clawing and injury-prevention guarantees are excluded.
- [StrongFirst: The Kur for Your Kettlebell Swing and Clean](https://www.strongfirst.com/the-kur-for-your-kettlebell-swing-and-clean/) discusses dead-swing initiation, controlled hikes and a conservatively selected implement. Only that parked-single concept informs E6. The article's long practice sessions, random selection, weekly frequency and loading examples are not used. The six singles, chest ceiling and fallback are authored here; each single still contains a backswing.
- Prior [source register](sources_and_exercises.md) and [Class 5 notes](class_05_sources_and_exercises.md) retain the ground-force/hip/ankle-function and supervised technical-loading rationale. Wall recoil and scissor exchange have mechanical component jobs, not demonstrated exact sprint-transfer outcomes. No new measurement, injury diagnosis or actual performance is claimed.

Read `docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv`, the generated falling-start and wall-pogo records below, prior swing identity notes and the full drill history. Local names/records do not establish live publication or athlete readiness; no application/database record was edited.

Do not import a 10 m sprint from its name. |
| E2 staggered broad | No exact staggered-broad entry found in inspected CSV; broad-jump family previously verified | **Proposed explicit variant:** offset two-foot origin, parallel two-foot receiver, both front-leg configurations. Not a single-leg bound or same-lead split jump. |

Do not claim a published/approved card or approved media. Local review/publication instructions concern that record; this task only authors a curriculum prescription with equipment/readiness conditions. |
| E4 scissor split jump | `split-jump-scissor-jump` — Split Jump / Scissor Jump found | Verified family name; explicit single airborne exchange and terminal opposite-lead stick are authored delivery details. Earlier Class 2 used the same broad family without the exchange; do not conceal this relationship. |

# Class 7 — design and audit

**2026-09-13. Previous run: progress**, evidenced by saved Class 6 and updated records. Verified current state references, unchanged Classes 1–6 and the original specification snapshot. Reviewed the map, preceding class, earlier start/strength prescriptions, all drill/default/contingency history, workload ledger, audits/source notes and feedback. No actual athlete response is supplied. Only Class 7 is finalized.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Initiate a forward push from settled support with a stable body line and prompt free-leg recovery.
2. **Demand:** Generate force after a seated or paused starting condition, rather than relying on an approach or repeated rebound; retain posture as pressure and support change.
3. **Anchor:** Four seated starts with observation of seat-to-foot transfer, first step and controlled stopping. Use only scheduled attempts, with a new origin-specific record.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Bilateral seated forward projection; paused unilateral forward impulse; brief leg-driven isometric force onset; same-leg free-thigh recovery under support; independently initiated hip-drive singles. Retained foot/lateral-hip strengthening and six primary roles serve the same task.
5. **Constraints:** Exact 6/2/6, supervised ages 12–14 baseline competence, unknown response, preference for unique drills, ten-metre lanes, unconfirmed seat/wall fit and group clock. A class file is not an athlete exposure or a top-speed test.

## Selection, revisions and recurrence

| Issue | Final decision and reason |
|---|---|
| New start origin | Seated start changes the initial support and requires a direct transfer onto the feet; unlike kneeling or three-point starts, body mass begins partly supported by a seat. No hands push the seat and no backward rock supplies momentum. It is not a simulation of block clearance. |
| Seat geometry | A toe line at 0 m would put the seat outside the stated lane footprint. Revise the default to seat/starting body footprint within 0–1 m and feet at 1 m: drive at most 3 m to line 4, stop by line 9. Actual seat fit and stopping remain prerequisites. Standing fallback returns to feet at 0 m. Do not silently reuse the earlier nine-metre outward-distance calculation for seated starts. |
| Seated broad versus seated vertical | E2 uses the supported origin for bilateral forward impulse, whereas Class 2 used an upward seated takeoff. Its job also differs from E1's sequential running steps. Hold only four jumps and modest distance, with a floor receiver rather than another box. |
| Paused unilateral takeoff | E3 retains a two-foot receiver but changes Class 1's dynamic unilateral origin to a settled two-second position. The pause is a meaningful initiation constraint, not a promise of zero elastic contribution. Unstable holds receive a two-foot staggered fallback. |
| Force-onset slot | A rapid wall-supported calf raise was considered but overlapped more closely with existing calf work. Choose a brief split-stance leg-drive pulse against a verified immovable wall instead. Its job is quick pressure development with unchanged body position; not a jump, external movement power, prolonged brace or maximal test. |
| Wall thigh recovery | E5 keeps one support foot planted while the same other leg repeatedly lifts and returns slowly. This differs from Class 2's fast support exchanges and Class 6's wall pogo; there is no airborne contact or sudden support swap. The support/pressure condition differs from the earlier floor-supported knee drive. |
| Intentional default recurrence | Retain **Class 6's dead-stop swing**, same two sets of three singles. It directly rehearses hip-drive initiation and controlled re-parking. Staggered swings, loaded jumps and catches would introduce extra loading/coordination without a better job in this session. The user's request is to try to force unique drills; this recurrence is explicit rather than hidden behind a new label. Five other default tasks have meaningful distinctions. |
| Fallback duplication | E4's wall replacement uses a paused squat jump. Give E6 a rapid bilateral bridge fallback so the two unavailable-equipment paths do not prescribe the same squat jump in two slots. The bridge is a disclosed earlier contingency family and changes resistance, not an equivalent swing. |
| Strength allocation | Hold the single split-squat round, single RDL set and three walkout cycles, plus the existing hip-flexion/calf doses. No removed volume is restored with the new starts/jumps. P1 supplies loaded leg extension, P2 a controlled loaded hinge, P3 thigh force, P4 knee-lever support and P5/P6 two knee-position ankle tasks. S1/S2 remain easy foot/pelvic work. |

## Workload and progression

E1: **4 seated starts**, two per first stepping foot; at most **8 driving strikes and 12 m of driving**. The drive is contained within **32 m maximum outward travel** (four × eight metres from line 1 to line 9), not added to it. Four stopping episodes; actual slowing/return contacts are unknown.

E2: **4 bilateral takeoff/landing events**. E3: **4 unilateral takeoffs**, two/leg, followed by **4 bilateral landings**. Jump subtotal **8 bilateral landing events / 16 landing foot impacts**. No running-in-place contacts or repeated pogo block. E4: **6 one-second pulses = 6 seconds of prescribed active pressure**, three pulses/front-leg configuration. This is separate from 30 foot-seconds in S1. E5: **6 fast knee drives and 6 controlled returning-foot contacts**, three/foot. E6: **6 parked-single floats**, six complete hike/float/park repetitions with no foot flight. No throws, external drops or maximum-velocity runs.

Class 6 had four starts, twelve mixed jump/hop events, eight upright running contacts and six swings. Class 7 keeps four starts/six swings but changes the origin, reduces jumps to eight bilateral receivers and removes upright running contacts. Pulses and controlled returns replace some impact work; they are not equal-stress units. The shorter seated run-out is a real constraint, not automatically lower fatigue or evidence of recovery.

Light work remains **2 rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps + 30 foot-seconds**. Primary remains **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 54 dynamic reps + 3 walkout cycles** (24 heel steps). Preparation remains **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps + 1 short-lever cycle** (8 heel steps). A unilateral round includes both sides; a bout is each separately performed side. No actual load, Access & Prepare 1 workload or outside sport/gym/tumbling is supplied.

New support/force tasks are conditional on current competence. Keep primary work at 2–3 technical RIR, light work at RPE 3–4, wall pulses brief/firm/submaximal and swings crisp. No load, distance, lean or lever increase follows from the class number. A later change needs actual clean work, target reserve and subsequent recovery; hold or reduce if those observations are absent or unfavorable. Record failed/partial/omitted work without make-up attempts. No performed cumulative workload can be inferred.

## Replacement effects

- E1 standing at 0 m keeps four starts and the two-step/3 m drive cap; outward bound changes from **32 m to 36 m** across four attempts. Mixed setups need per-attempt distances. One-step versions cap driving contacts at four if used throughout; actual travel remains observed, not assumed.
- E2 paused standing broad keeps four bilateral landing events; supported origin is lost and the Class 1 task recurs. E3 paused staggered takeoff changes unilateral takeoffs to bilateral while preserving four bilateral receivers. Neither is a completed default task.
- E4 squat jump replaces six pressure pulses with **four bilateral landings**, making **12 bilateral jump events / 24 landing foot impacts** if other defaults remain. No equivalent-load claim.
- E5 supine knee drive keeps six drive cycles but removes six prescribed standing foot-return contacts and changes support. Gentle floor setup/return placements are not impact-equivalent wall-drill contacts. The Class 3 fallback family recurs.
- E6 rapid bilateral bridge substitutes **six nonflight hip-drive reps** for six floats; no added jump. The Class 4 fallback family recurs. Record actual resistance/identity rather than swing completion.
- Supported unilateral P5 changes work to **10 bouts / 56 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, preparation to **10 bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**; verify support and allow about one more minute. Other range/stance reductions preserve slots but change comparison conditions.

## Timing and delivery

Individual prompt equipment access is assumed. Work/teaching allowances are estimates; rests are prescribed. Teaching may use rest time, counted once. Actual queues, extra ramps or recovery extend the model.

| E2 | 4 × 6 s pause/jump/hold + 120 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 90 s | 274 |
| E3 | 4 × 7 s setup/pause/jump/hold + 90 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 60 s side change | 218 |
| E4 | 6 × 1 s pulses + 120 s setup/teaching | 4 × 20 s + 60 s side change | 266 |
| E5 | 6 × 4 s lift/hold/lower + 90 s teaching | 4 × 10 s + 45 s side change | 199 |
| E6 | 6 × 6 s hike/float/park + 120 s teaching | 4 × 20 s + 90 s | 326 |
| E transitions through S1 | Setup may occupy rest | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s | 480 |
| **Explosiveness** | | | **2,231** |
| S1/S2 and transitions | 225 s work/teaching/side changes | 45 s between + 60 s after | **330** |
| P1 | Prep 24 s + work 30 s + teaching 90 s | 30 s prep sides + 60 s prework + 60 s work sides | 294 |
| P2 | Prep 24 s + work 18 s + teaching 90 s | 60 s between ramps + 90 s prework | 282 |
| P3 | Prep 24 s + work 48 s + teaching 75 s | 30 s prep sides + 45 s prework + 45 s work sides | 267 |

Allow **76–86 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1**, not a hard cap. The entire booking remains unresolved because preparation, group, staff and actual equipment flow are unknown. A 60-minute complete booking cannot fit this version. Do not shorten required rest to claim otherwise.

Verify seat stability/traction and the actual combined seat/athlete footprint inside 0–1 m. The first pair establishes whether the athlete can slow within the remaining space; use the stated standing/one-step options if necessary. One athlete uses the lane; close it during return. Protect jump receivers, bell sweep, wall stations and waiting positions. No assumed simultaneous stations or unsupervised youth lifting. Peer waiting counts as recovery only when actual intervals meet requirements, and no extra explosive bouts fill queues.

Approximate 48–72-hour spacing between demanding lower-body exposures is only a starting consideration alongside actual sport, gym and tumbling. The separate 10 m/12 m facility conflict remains unresolved. Stationary or short-start tasks do not replace maximum-velocity running.

## Handoff

Save Class 7, source notes and updated map/ledger/history/feedback/state/verification. Preserve Classes 1–6 and archive Class 6's verification as a historical checkpoint.

Next run: review all saved work and actual feedback, then finalize **Class 8 only**. Consider another facing/stance only if it serves the athletes' acceleration needs; a multidirectional start must still exit into a verified short lane and must not become an agility class. With no evidence of that need, retain a straight-line application. Check seated layout/control, static push, wall/floor choices, swing execution and actual strength reserve/recovery before changing demands.
