# Class 6 — design and audit

**2026-09-13. Previous run: progress**, evidenced by Class 5 and updated records. Verified the current state paths, unchanged Classes 1–5 and specification snapshot. Reviewed the map, Class 5, earlier start and strength prescriptions, workload/drill history including contingencies, audits/source notes and feedback. No actual attendance, execution or recovery is supplied. Only Class 6 is finalized.

## Daily stimulus brief

1. **Result:** Turn a controlled forward initiation into a supporting push/next step while retaining organized limb exchange and upright foot return in gym tasks.
2. **Demand:** Maintain the body line as support changes; distinguish forward impulse, ankle recoil, reciprocal thigh movement and hip-drive initiation.
3. **Anchor:** Four falling starts under the established two-step/3 m driving and 9 m stopping caps. Observe lean, recovery foot, reaching/folding and stopping within scheduled attempts.
4. **Supporting jobs:** Staggered bilateral forward projection; same-leg ankle recoil under a supported lean; a single airborne split-stance exchange; upright release/return in a running rhythm; independently initiated hip-drive singles. Retained light foot/lateral-hip work and six loaded strength roles support those tasks.
5. **Constraints:** Exact 6/2/6; supervised ages 12–14 baseline competence; no athlete response; purposefully distinct drills; short lanes and unconfirmed wall/equipment/group setup. Separate gym tasks cannot reproduce a start-to-maximum-velocity run.

## Selection and revisions

| Consequential choice | Finding and final decision |
|---|---|
| Start origin | Falling start supplies a controlled forward-momentum initiation unlike earlier static standing, kneeling or hand-supported origins. Keep four attempts and the earlier boundaries. Revise the cue from waiting for a near-fall to taking the recovery step early enough to remain controlled; greater lean is not the objective. |
| Forward force task | Staggered broad jump requires contribution from two offset feet, then a parallel receiver. It differs from Class 3's parallel-origin broad and Class 2's same-lead vertical split jump. Use a small offset and modest distance rather than forcing a long split stance or a distance record. |
| Supported ankle task | Wall pressure/forward body line gives same-leg recoil a distinct support condition from upright free-standing pogos and pulsed knee-drive pogos. Keep the free thigh still and only two contacts/leg. Wall availability is unconfirmed, so provide a floor fallback; no movable object is used as a wall. |
| Leg exchange | Single scissor jump changes lead legs in flight, whereas Class 2 preserved its lead. It receives on two split feet, unlike single-leg A-run support. Keep isolated modest jumps and terminal control, not repeated scissor rebounds. |
| Upright consolidation | Single-leg step-over running combines a modest release with the asymmetric running rhythm; it is neither the prior B-skip rhythm nor a planted-support cycle. Reduce from the preceding high-knee task's three cycles/target to **two**, giving eight running contacts because starts return today. No taller knee target, literal obstacle or airborne full same-leg cycling is added. |
| Hip-force drill | Select parked-single two-hand swings over a staggered loaded swing. Re-establishing the hike/drive/park on each single supplies a repeatable initiation task without introducing an offset loaded hinge. Six floats replace the earlier continuous swing family's ten; the identity change is interrupted initiation, not merely fewer reps. Each single still has a backswing, so do not claim absent eccentric loading or direct equivalence to sprint takeoff. |
| Combined workload | Reintroduce four bounded starts after the upright-focused prescriptions. Keep wall recoil at two/leg, reduce upright contacts to eight and swings to six singles. All primary strength doses hold at Class 5 levels; no split-squat/RDL/walkout volume is restored and no load increase is inferred. |
| Strength relevance | P1 loads stable split-leg extension; P2 provides controlled loaded hip extension distinct from a ballistic single; P3 loads thigh lift; P4 controls a changing knee lever; P5/P6 develop ankle force with different knee positions. Their overlap is purposeful but doses remain small/challenging. S1/S2 stay easy foot/pelvic strengthening. |
| Novelty and recurrence | Six defaults have relevant differences in origin, support, receiver, exchange rhythm or initiation. No credit for cosmetic renaming. Standing starts, ordinary broad/pogo/split jumps, high-knee running and squat-jump fallbacks openly recur for readiness/equipment reasons. No lateral drills, throws or extra combined drill blocks are inserted to force uniqueness. |

## Prescribed workload and recovery

**E1:** Four starts, two with each first stepping foot; up to **8 driving foot strikes**, up to **12 m total driving distance**, already contained within **36 m maximum outward travel including slowing**. Four stopping episodes; actual slowing/return contacts are unknown. Do not add the drive distance to the outward distance or infer measured distances from these caps.

**E2/E3/E4:** Four staggered broad jumps with bilateral landings; four wall-supported same-leg pogo landings; four split scissor jumps with bilateral landings. Total **12 jump/hop events: eight bilateral and four unilateral = 20 landing foot impacts**. E2 has two takeoffs per front-leg configuration; E4 has two attempts per starting front leg and receives with the opposite lead. E3 has two contacts/leg. These are different tasks, not equal loads.

**E5:** Four asymmetric cycles = **8 upright running contacts**, four/foot, separate from start contacts and jump landings. **E6:** Six individual hikes/floats/parks, one rep per complete parked single; six ballistic floats, no intended foot flight. Setup/exit steps, incidental contacts and extra actual reps remain separate. No throws, external drop landings or maximum-velocity runs.

Class 5 had twelve running contacts and twelve jump/hop events with four bilateral/eight unilateral landings. Class 6 adds four start attempts, reduces upright running to eight contacts and changes receiving types to eight bilateral/four unilateral. This is a planned allocation to the start/upright connection, not equal stress, observed tolerance or a claim of reduced total fatigue. Prior completion and scheduling are unknown.

Strength stays **2 light rounds / 4 bouts / 12 dynamic reps + 30 foot-seconds**, and **7 primary rounds / 9 bouts / 54 dynamic reps + 3 walkout cycles**. Preparation remains **7 rounds / 9 bouts / 32 dynamic reps + 1 short-lever cycle**. A unilateral round includes both sides; each separately executed side is a bout. Walkout working cycles contain 24 heel steps; its preparation adds eight. Actual loads/extra ramps, Access & Prepare 1 and other sport/gym/tumbling are not known.

Light work remains RPE 3–4; primary work uses 2–3 technical RIR. E6 uses a technically qualified crisp load, not a heavy test. RDL/walkout reductions remain particularly relevant with swings and starts present. Full resets preserve output; stop or reduce when quality fails instead of shortening rest or adding make-up attempts. Review actual calf/hip/hamstring response and the full schedule before future increases.

## Replacement accounting

- E1 standing start keeps four attempts and the same caps, but changes origin; one-step versions reduce driving contacts to at most four if used for all starts. Actual mixed attempts need individual records.
- E2 parallel broad keeps four bilateral landings; configuration changes, so it is a disclosed earlier-family recurrence.
- E3 upright same-leg pogo keeps four unilateral contacts with a different body line. Bilateral pogo instead changes the default total to **12 bilateral events / 24 landing foot impacts**. Choose one replacement.
- E4 same-lead split jump keeps four bilateral events but removes the scissor exchange; E5 high-knee run keeps eight running contacts without the release. Both repeat prior families.
- E6 paused squat jump replaces six nonflight floats with **four bilateral jump landings**. With other defaults the total becomes **16 jump/hop events: 12 bilateral + 4 unilateral = 28 foot impacts**. If combined with bilateral E3, the total is **16 bilateral events / 32 foot impacts**. This is not an equal-loading replacement.
- Supported unilateral P5 changes primary to **10 bouts / 56 dynamic reps + 3 cycles**, preparation to **10 bouts / 33 reps + 1 cycle**. Verify support and log the actual version.
- Reduced lean, offset, height, release range or load changes execution conditions. Failed/partial/omitted work remains visible; written exercise count does not prove completed delivery.

## Timing and delivery

Individual prompt equipment access is assumed. Work/teaching allowances are estimates; rests are prescribed. Teaching may occur during rests, in which case count elapsed time once. Extra coaching, ramps, queues or recovery extend actual duration.

| Task | Work/teaching allowance | Recovery | Seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 4 × 10 s start/slowing + 120 s teaching | 2 × 75 s + 120 s | 430 |
| E2 | 4 × 5 s jump/hold + 90 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 45 s side change | 195 |
| E3 | 2 × 5 s contacts/reset + 120 s setup/teaching | 60 s between legs | 190 |
| E4 | 4 × 5 s jump/hold + 90 s teaching | 2 × 20 s + 45 s side change | 195 |
| E5 | 2 × 6 s cycles/finish + 90 s teaching | 75 s between target legs | 177 |
| E6 | 6 × 6 s hike/float/park + 120 s teaching | 4 × 20 s + 90 s set rest | 326 |
| E transitions through S1 | Setup can occupy rest | 4 × 90 s + 2 × 60 s | 480 |
| **Explosiveness** | | | **1,993** |
| S1/S2 and transitions | 225 s work/teaching/side changes | 45 s between + 60 s after | **330** |
| P1 | Prep 24 s + work 30 s + teaching 90 s | 30 s prep sides + 60 s prework + 60 s work sides | 294 |
| P2 | Prep 24 s + work 18 s + teaching 90 s | 60 s between ramps + 90 s prework | 282 |
| P3 | Prep 24 s + work 48 s + teaching 75 s | 30 s prep sides + 45 s prework + 45 s work sides | 267 |
| P4 | Prep 10 s + work 30 s + teaching 60 s | 45 s prework | 145 |
| P5 | Prep 20 s + work 40 s + teaching 60 s | 45 s prework | 165 |
| P6 | Prep 25 s + work 80 s + teaching 75 s | 60 s prework + 90 s sets | 330 |

Allow **72–82 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1**, not a hard cap. The unilateral calf fallback adds about one minute; other replacements can change teaching time. Existing preparation duration, full booking, staffing and group size are unknown. A 60-minute complete booking cannot fit this version.

Starts use one protected 10 m lane, with progressive slowing by 9 m and closure during walking return. Verify width, traction, waiting/coach positions and individual stopping. E2 landing space, the wall station and full bell path must remain clear of cross-traffic. A suitable wall is not confirmed; no rated rack is assumed instead. Use the floor fallback if needed. Three lanes do not establish simultaneous group capacity. For groups, actual peer/wait intervals can supply rest only when they meet the prescribed interval; do not fill queues with unsupervised lifting or repeated explosive bouts.

The 10 m versus older 12 m facility discrepancy remains unresolved. Approximate 48–72-hour spacing is only an initial scheduling consideration after reviewing actual lower-body/sport/tumbling work and recovery; no calendar or attendance record is invented.

## Midpoint reassessment and handoff

The six finalized prescriptions cover static and moving start origins, forward projection, unilateral/bilateral support, upright recovery and ankle/hip force. They do not establish six completed athlete exposures or actual maximum-velocity practice. Strength continuity is traceable through reduced/held doses; novelty is concentrated in purposeful task variants rather than presumed performance gains.

Next run: review Classes 1–6 and actual feedback, then finalize **Class 7 only**, revisiting rapid hip extension and horizontal projection from stillness. Review start stopping/lean, offset push, wall/floor choice, scissor reception, upright return, swing hike/park and actual strength reserve/recovery. Do not automatically increase resistance, distance, contacts or restore strength sets. Save the next class/state and stop. Preserve Classes 1–5 and archive the Class 5 verification as a historical checkpoint.

# Class 10 — source and exercise identity notes

**Reviewed 2026-09-13.** The user-selected Sprinting scope, seven-category framework, existing Access & Prepare 1 and exact 6/2/6 govern. OTA provides coaching inspiration; local stance, distance, doses, replacements and timing are authored for this curriculum. No source validates the whole session or establishes an athlete response.

## Coaching sources and limits

| Source | Contribution | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [OTA — Offseason Football Linear Speed Workout](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/offseason-football-linear-speed-workout/) | Names bent-over starts and includes a hip-hinge initiation emphasis. | The still parallel-foot, hand-free setup and four short starts are our explicit variant. Its warm-up, longer routes and six-reps-each-side dose are not copied. No dominant-leg assumption. |
| [OTA — Advanced Linear Speed Drills](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/advanced-speed/) | Distinguishes step-over running from a one-sided dead-leg pattern and treats these as mechanics rehearsal. | Our version alternates both legs in place for eight contacts. No traveling bound, fixed mastery timeline, deliberate claw or injury-prevention claim is imported. If actual previous technique already matched, record overlap. |
| [OTA — NFL Combine Prep Training](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/maximize-your-speed-nfl-combine-prep-training-for-the-40-yard-dash/) | Names single/double/triple wall switches with a focus on posture and quality. | Class 10 intentionally repeats Class 8's four double-switch pairs. No novelty credit or automatic extension to longer runs. |
| [OTA — Three Drills to Get Faster Instantly](https://blog.overtimeathletes.com/3-drills-to-get-faster-instantly/) | Provides a resisted hip-recovery concept in its banded hip-drive example. | Our foot-loop standing drive has no external anchor or extra knee-extension action. Its band setup, six reps and quick-lift/controlled-return dose are authored here; the source's warm-up, volume and immediate-speed claims are not imported. |

Horizontal projection and individual force-acceptance families are already documented in the earlier OTA source registers. E2's same-lead forward receiver and E3's two-foot takeoff/single-foot receiver are explicit locally authored variants, not claimed exact OTA demonstrations. Neither is a literal simulation of a running contact. General youth-supervision and hip/ankle rationale remains in the [initial source register](sources_and_exercises.md); it does not establish readiness or equal loading between variants.

## Local library review

Searched `docs/exercise-difficulty-review.csv` for bent-over/parallel starts, split broad jumps, two-to-one takeoff/landing, alternating step-over running and banded hip-flexor/knee-drive families. The local name/slug **Banded Hip Flexor March / banded-hip-flexor-march** exists. Its name alone does not establish a repeated-same-leg, closed-foot-loop, rapid-drive definition. No detailed matching generated file was found in the inspected paths; do not invent a published variant or live database ID.

| Slot | Identity decision |
|---|---|
| E1 Bent-Over Sprint Start | **Proposed explicit variant/addition:** still parallel feet, hip-hinged trunk, hands free, no preparatory fall/step, two driving strikes within the defined lane. Different initial constraint from Class 1's stagger, Class 6's falling entry and Class 8's two-hand support. |
| E2 Split-Stance Broad to Split Stick | **Proposed same-lead receiver variant:** offset two-foot takeoff and offset two-foot receiver in forward projection. Class 6 finished parallel; Class 8 began parallel. No exact local binding claimed. |
| E3 Two-Foot Vertical to Single-Leg Stick | **Proposed receiver variant:** both feet leave, one selected foot receives, then the free foot sets down after a hold. Distinct from Class 5's opposite support transition and Class 4's unilateral takeoff/same-leg receiver. |
| E4 Alternating Step-Over Run | **Proposed stationary alternating variant** of the OTA-named pattern. Class 6 prescribed a one-sided fuller cycle; Class 9 emphasized compact knee folding without this lower-leg release. Related running family, not a new base movement or proof of new actual technique. |
| E5 Wall Drill Double Switch | **Intentional Class 8 default recurrence**, same name, dose and rest. Its directly useful two-contact inclined-support job is retained. |
| E6 Standing Banded Knee Drive | **Proposed exact variant** in the local banded hip-flexor family: repeated same leg, very light closed band across shoe midfeet, opposite foot flat, band opposing lift. Upright planted support differs from Class 3's supine band drive; no verified canonical binding inferred from the march label. |
| S1/S2 and P1–P6 | Identities, doses, preparation and rests held from Class 9; jobs revised for initiation, individual support and subsequent recovery. Actual loads are unknown. |

The five other default tasks have meaningful proposed distinctions, while E5 is openly repeated. All prior defaults and contingencies were considered. Earlier standing starts, broad-jump receivers, bilateral CMJ, A-run/march, isolated wall/plank switches and supine unresisted knee drives remain named replacements; none is added to its default.

The E6 floor replacement avoids duplicating E4's possible marching path, and E2/E3 replacements retain horizontal versus vertical jobs. Changes in support, direction, reception, resistance or actual technique must be logged; counts alone do not establish equivalent demand or performance improvement.

Wall, closed-loop band fit/stretch allowance, traction, whole starting footprint, receiving competence, equipment sizes and group flow remain unconfirmed. Use the documented replacements when a default cannot be qualified. All actual attendance, execution and recovery remain unknown. No exercise-library or application records were edited.
